features.feature: Graph nodes can drive the normal map and UV coordinates
features.evidence:
SHIPPED 2026-09-07.  Three of the eleven graph nodes were built and unwireable, and all three failed the SAME way: the node existed, its GLSL was correct, and nothing could consume the result.  None of them failed loudly and none of them is visible on the canvas -- the node sits there, the link snaps into place, and the generated shader quietly says something else.

NORMAL MAP had no destination.  The PBR Output node had no Normal socket and codegen emitted `vec3 mat_normal_ts = vec3(0,0,1);` unconditionally, with no case that ever read a link.  The Output now has a Normal input, DT_VEC3 -- matching what a tangent-space normal IS, and matching the Normal Map node's output, which used to be a vec4-wrapped DT_COLOR that the type checker (which requires exact equality) could never have connected to it even after the socket appeared.  Unconnected still emits (0,0,1), the identity, so a graph that does not drive it shades as before.

AND THE TEMPLATE THREW IT AWAY.  fs_graph_template.sc spent mat_normal_ts on `normalize(v_normal + mat_normal_ts * 0.0001)` -- a reference that keeps the compiler from stripping the variable and moves the shading normal by about a thousandth of a degree.  A graph could have driven it perfectly and the picture would not have changed.  It now applies the normal through a real TBN basis; v_tangent / v_bitangent joined the $input, which costs nothing because every graph FS is already compiled against vs_pbr.sc and varying_pbr.def.sc, both of which declare and write them.

UV WAS ONE FLOAT.  The node was labelled 'UV (Tile/Offset)' and its only output was a DT_FLOAT called 'Tile', emitted as a bare constant; the Texture node took no input at all and mat_uv was never reassigned, so nothing in the graph could tile or offset anything.  The node is now a DT_VEC2 that emits `mat_uv * tile + offset` from a four-float payload the canvas edits as two DragFloat2s, and the Texture and Normal Map nodes both take a UV input.  An unconnected UV substitutes mat_uv, NOT vec2(0,0) -- every Texture node hard-coded mat_uv before there was a socket, and a zero default would turn an untouched graph into one that samples a single texel.

TEXTURE READ A PATH NOBODY READ.  Node::text was serialised and reloaded and codegen ignored it: every Texture node emitted the literal `texture2D(s_albedo, mat_uv)`, so two nodes pointing at different things sampled the same map.  It is now a SLOT and that is the honest limit: a graph program is bound by jce_pbr_material_bind, which binds the material's five maps and nothing else, so a per-node FILE would need a sampler no material fills -- which reads whatever the previous draw left on that stage.  The node is 'Texture (Material Map)' with a five-way picker, the template gained s_ao (stage 3) so all five are reachable, and an unrecognised value falls back to albedo, which is what every graph authored before the picker did.

MEASURED as TEXT, because the generated shader IS the artefact and every one of these defects is a defect in it.  tests/editor/test_jce_shadergraph_codegen.cpp (NOT IN THE TREE -- tests/ is gitignored on this branch) builds graphs and asserts on the generated GLSL: the Normal socket exists with a matching dtype, an unconnected Normal is the identity and a connected one is read, the UV node emits a vec2 the Texture node samples with, an unconnected UV is mat_uv, all five slots reach five distinct samplers, and the template applies the normal through a TBN with the varyings declared.  FOUR negative controls each turned it red on the assertion that names the defect: stopping the Normal read, hard-coding s_albedo again, defaulting UV to zero, and restoring the template's 0.0001 line.

One instrument defect worth recording: the first TBN assertion searched for 'mat_normal_ts * 0.0001' and FOUND it -- in the COMMENT that explains what that line used to be.  A substring search over source is satisfied by prose about the source, the same way a check for a symbol name has been satisfied by an include line in this tree before.  The test now strips comments and asserts on the code.

NOT MEASURED ON PIXELS, and the reason is worth stating rather than leaving: rendering a graph material needs the editor to drive shaderc through the material-graph panel, and no automated path does that today -- the same gap the shader-blob backend-suffix work recorded.  What is proved is that the generated source now says the right thing, which is exactly what was wrong.
features.compared: Unity Shader Graph, UE and Godot all make the normal a first-class master-node input, let UV nodes feed sampler UVs, and give a Sample Texture 2D node its own texture property.  JCE now matches the first two.  The third it matches only for the material's own five maps: an arbitrary per-node texture needs a sampler the material binding does not provide, and that limit is named at the node rather than implied by a free-text box that does nothing -- which is what was there before.

features.feature: Shader keywords that strip unused features per material
features.evidence:
There is no keyword or static-switch system: I searched engine/include, engine/src/renderer, engine/shaders, editor/src, tools and scripts for multi_compile, shader_feature, keyword and permutation and the only relevant hits are comments saying it does not exist. engine/include/jce/renderer/jce_render_pipeline.h:146 states the shadow filter tier is a "frame-constant branch in fs_pbr/fs_terrain — no shader permutations". Variants are instead a hand-written fixed set enumerated in the public JceShaderSet (engine/include/jce/renderer/jce_shaders.h:76-116): pbr, pbr_inst, pbr_inst_tint, pbr_inst_tex_array, pbr_inst_fade, pbr_skinned, three Forward+ twins, toon, outline, four shadow variants and terrain — each a separate .sc file, none generated. The consequence is visible in the uber-shader: fs_pbr_body.sh:31-393 declares CSM, 32 point lights, 16 spot lights, IBL, SH9 GI, SSAO, clustered Forward+, cookies, weather and LOD fade uniforms in one program, so a flat unlit material pays for every branch. No material-level API exists to disable any of it.  || ADVERSARIALLY VERIFIED: a second agent was told to REFUTE this claim by finding the implementation, because this repository has been wrong about 'behind'/'absent' twice (auto-LOD, read off a truncated grep; script hot-reload, where interpreted scripts DO reload every Play). Verdict: refuted -- The mechanism claim ("There is no keyword or static-switch system... the only relevant hits are comments saying it does not exist") is factually wrong. There ARE five live preprocessor feature macros that gate real code in the PBR uber-shader and produce separately compiled programs.

FOUND — compile-time static switches on one shared body:
`engine/shaders/pbr/fs_pbr_body.sh` is a single shared body; thin entry `.sc` files define a macro and include it, so each macro yields a distinct compiled program with the disabled feature's code AND uniforms absent:
- `JCE_FORWARDPLUS` — defined `engine/shaders/pbr/fs_pbr_fwdplus.sc:23`; gates `fs_pbr_body.sh:204, 606, 1208` (replaces the brute-force 16-light loop with the cluster loop and drops the IES sampler to free stage 14).
- `JCE_TOON` — `engine/shaders/pbr/fs_pbr_toon.sc:16`; gates the uniform block `fs_pbr_body.sh:45-48` plus `1178, 1198`. The body's own comment at `fs_pbr_body.sh:42-44` says the toon uniforms "are NOT compiled in and the default programs are byte-identical" — that is compile-time stripping, stated in the file the auditor cites.
- `JCE_TEX_ARRAY` — `fs_pbr_inst_tex_array.sc:18`; gates `fs_pbr_body.sh:84, 940`.
- `JCE_INST_TINT` — `fs_pbr_tint.sc:20`; gates `fs_pbr_body.sh:966`.
- `JCE_FADE_DITHER` — `fs_pbr_fade.sc:12`; gates `fs_pbr_body.sh:700`.
These are loaded as named programs at `engine/src/renderer/jce_shaders.c:307-333`.

FOUND — the stripped variant is reachable from authoring (per-object), not just internal: `JceMeshRenderer.toon` (`engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_scene.h:117`, edited in the Inspector) selects the `JCE_TOON` permutation at `engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_sr_draw.c:5094`.

FOUND — per-material feature disable does exist, contradicting "No material-level API exists to disable any of it": `JcePbrMaterial.receive_shadows_off` (`engine/include/jce/renderer/jce_pbr_material.h:71`) is packed into `u_normalScale.w` at `engine/src/renderer/jce_pbr_material.c:238` and skips ALL CSM + local-atlas shadow sampling at `fs_pbr_body.sh:747, 1339, 1440`. The normal-map path is likewise auto-disabled per material when no normal map is bound (`jce_pbr_material.c:232-236` → `fs_pbr_body.sh:1018-1024`), removing a fetch, a normalize and a mat3 build per fragment.

FOUND — a per-material escape from the uber-shader entirely: `JcePbrMaterial.custom_program` (`jce_pbr_material.h:78`) / `jce_pbr_material_effective_program` (`jce_pbr_material.c:130`), persisted as `customProgramVs`/`customProgramFs` in `.mat.json` (loaded `jce_pbr_material.c:578-588`), produced by the editor Material Graph "Compile & Bind" (`editor/src/panels/material_graph/jce_material_graph_eval.cpp:477` + `editor/src/shadergraph/jce_shadergraph_shaderc.cpp`), and actually consumed at draw time via `sr_resolve_custom_program` (`engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_scene_renderer.c:455`) → `engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_sr_draw.c:5372-5380`. Wired end-to-end, not dead.

WHY "behind", not "parity" (the ledger row `pipeline.shader-variants` in `contracts/engine-parity.json` currently says parity — that is also wrong, in the other direction):
- No author-facing keyword surface. There is no `multi_compile` / `shader_feature` / `#pragma` and no keyword set on a material or a shader. The five axes are hand-written, one entry `.sc` per axis, filename-encoded.
- No permutation generation. `tools/compile_shaders.cmake:315-316` passes exactly ONE `--define` for every shader in the tree (`BGFX_CONFIG_MAX_BONES=128`) and never a feature macro; nothing enumerates a define matrix.
- No cook-time variant stripping; the sibling row `build.always-included-shaders` in the same ledger is itself "absent".
- Proof the macro set is unmanaged rather than generated: `JCE_RENDER_COOKIE_2D_ARRAY` guards code at `fs_pbr_body.sh:190, 1164, 1408` and is defined NOWHERE in the tree (checked engine/, editor/, tools/, scripts/, CMakeLists) — a dead permutation axis a generator would never have allowed.
- The auditor's *consequence* paragraph survives: a flat unlit material still gets the default `fs_pbr` permutation with CSM, 32 point lights, IBL, SH9, SSAO, cookies and weather compiled in as dynamic branches. Shadow-filter tier is confirmed frame-constant (`engine/include/jce/renderer/jce_render_pipeline.h:146`), i.e. a genuinely missing axis. Only `receive_shadows_off`, the auto normal-map zeroing, and the all-or-nothing graph `custom_program` actually reduce per-material cost.
So: the capability exists and is live, but it is a fixed five-axis hand-enumerated static-switch set with no per-material keyword control and no stripping pipeline — weaker than Unity keywords/variant stripping and UE permutations. || 2026-09-18 -- MEASURED, then REVERTED, and the revert is the finding. The row said a flat material 'pays for every branch'; that was an inventory, not a measurement, so the sections of fs_pbr were wrapped one at a time and compiled (jce.py shader-inspect, d3d11, -O3). fs_pbr's fragment program is 8311 instructions: CSM 6766 (81.4%), point lights 276 (3.3%), area lights 252 (3.0%), clearcoat+sheen 177 (2.1%), IBL/SH9 134 (1.6%), debug views 70 (0.8%), contact shadows 5, cloud shadows 5. FOUR FIFTHS OF THE SHADER IS ONE BLOCK, so a Unity-style pile of material keywords would have been spent on the other 18%. THE INSTRUMENT LIED TWICE BEFORE IT SAID THAT. jce.py shader-inspect passed the SDK's share/jce/shader_include FIRST, so it compiled dist/'s copy of every include and reported the same 8311 for six different mutations of the body; an `#error` added to the tree's fs_pbr_main.sh did not reach the compiler (fixed in 1d4fabd8, with that #error as the control). Then the probe reported 515 instructions saved for the Forward+ block -- a block already inside `#ifdef JCE_FORWARDPLUS` and not in this program at all -- because the wrap had opened between that #ifdef and its #else; three of six numbers were artefacts until the probe was made to refuse preprocessor-unbalanced regions. THE AXIS WAS BUILT AND IT WORKS: `JCE_NO_CSM` around the cascade block (no #else needed -- `shadow` is 1.0 above it and the prologue the rest of the shader consumes stays outside the guard) plus fs_pbr_noshadow.sc compiles to 1549 instructions with 22 texture fetches against fs_pbr's 1061 -- the 1039 it drops are the PCF taps -- while fs_pbr itself stays byte-identical (8311 / 4635 / 1061 / 2615, 44 declarations). IT WAS REVERTED BECAUSE ONE AXIS CANNOT BE WIRED ONCE. Selecting it per material needs, for EVERY existing vertex variant, a new .sc, a new JceShaderSet member, a renderer field + getter + destroy, and a selection site: pbr, pbr_inst, pbr_inst_tint, pbr_inst_tex_array, pbr_inst_fade, pbr_skinned, and the three Forward+ twins. The queue path was wired and a two-block fixture with Receive Shadows off on one of them proved it: forcing the variant on EVERY draw moved ZERO pixels, while the engine's own enable_csm=false moved 7979 px (0.73%, peak 155) on the same frame -- so the shadows were real and the program was not reaching them. The entities were shape primitives, which take a SEVENTH path (sr_prim_inst_add's factor-only tint batch) that the wiring had not touched. Half-wired is the failure this ledger exists to catch, so it went back out; the same call the light-render-layers row records. NO FRAME-TIME CLAIM IS MADE, and the attempt is recorded so nobody repeats it: interleaved A/B on hidden_cove, one env var apart, 5 pairs, frame 6.060 ms vs 6.060 ms -- pinned at the 165 Hz cap. Quadrupling the pixels (JCE_RP_FORCE=render_scale=2.0, confirmed applied in the log) took the reported GPU time from 5.6 to 5.9 ms, and a GPU figure that barely notices 4x the fragments is not measuring fragments. This machine cannot see a fragment-shader saving at all; the number that would settle it is a GPU timer query around the colour pass, which this engine does not expose per view. WHAT WOULD CLOSE THE ROW is therefore not more hand-wiring but the thing Unity has: a declared keyword manifest and a GENERATOR that emits the entry .sc files and the key->program table, so one axis costs one line rather than nine files, plus the per-draw selector reading that table at the ONE place a draw's program is decided -- which today is seven places.

2026-09-20 -- PARITY. The generator exists, and the axis reaches every draw path, which is the pair this row has been waiting for.

THE MANIFEST. contracts/shader-keywords.json declares fragment families, vertex variants and keyword axes. tools/shadergen/gen_shader_variants.py emits every fs_pbr*.sc entry file, the public <jce/renderer/jce_shader_variants.h> (the vertex-variant enum and the key macros) and the private key->program table. An axis is ONE ENTRY there; it used to be a file per family plus a JceShaderSet member, a renderer field, a getter, a destroy and a selection site per draw path. No arguments is CHECK MODE, read-only, exit 1 on drift -- the same shape as tools/scriptgen/*, and for the same reason: a generator whose check mode needs a flag gets run without it.

THE BASE PROGRAMS DID NOT MOVE, which is what made generating them safe: fs_pbr's compiled .bin is byte-identical before and after on all three backends (dx11 e20dbbfbb090f51f, glsl 3d2b243f09b83ea6, spv 5d2008ca3546da86). The hand-written entry files had rationale in their comments; that rationale is now in the manifest, one copy, and the generator prints it into every variant it applies to.

THE AXIS, MEASURED with jce.py shader-inspect: fs_pbr is 8329 instructions and fs_pbr_noshadow is 1549. Texture fetches 1061 -> 22, the 1039 it drops being the PCF taps. CSM is 81.4% of that shader, which is also why it is the ONLY axis the manifest declares for it -- a Unity-style pile of material keywords would have been spent on the other 18.6%.

ONE DECISION POINT. jce_renderer_get_program_variant(r, vertex_variant, keys) is where a PBR draw's program is chosen. Every named getter is a one-line call into it; the frame's own keys (Forward+, and JCE_SHADER_FORCE_KEYS) are folded there rather than at each site; tools/lint/check_shader_variants_generated.py fails if any other translation unit reads the table, and fails if a generated file is hand-edited. Both negative controls verified red.

AND IT REACHES EVERY PATH, which is the thing the previous attempt could not say. Deterministic fixture, D3D11, noise floor 0 px:
  JCE_SHADER_FORCE_KEYS=NOSHADOW on every draw ... 92.24% of the viewport takes the variant (marked red to make it visible), and 13995 px (1.277%) change against the engine's own enable_csm=false changing 8197 (0.748%) -- the compiled-out program drops both the cascade path AND the legacy single-map branch, so it removes MORE than the runtime switch.
  The previous attempt's reading on the same kind of control was ZERO pixels.

THE MATERIAL ASKS, and only the material. Same fixture, floor with Receive Shadows on vs off, the NOSHADOW program marked so which draws got one is visible:
  receivesShadow true  ....  0.00% of the viewport marked
  receivesShadow FALSE .... 68.53% marked (the floor is most of the frame)
AND THE PIXELS ARE IDENTICAL: axis on vs a mutation where the material never asks for it, 0 px differ, bit for bit. That is the assertion that matters and the one that can fail silently -- the base shader already read receive_shadows_off at runtime and multiplied by one, so the correct result of routing the keyword is an unchanged picture, which is also what a completely unwired axis produces. Only the marked-variant control tells those two apart.

SEVEN PATHS, AND THE LAST TWO WERE THE POINT. The render queue's two sites and the two mesh-draw entry points were straightforward. The built-in PRIMITIVE batch was not: it flushes through jce_mesh_draw_instanced_tinted OR jce_mesh_draw_instanced_gathered depending on whether its instances were gathered into scratch arrays, and both chose a program with no material in hand. Both now take the batch's keys (sr_material_shader_keys reads them back from the material registry the batch is keyed by). Wiring one branch and not the other would have given a primitive the cheap program on some frames and not others, with no visible difference either way -- the half-wired failure in miniature, inside the very path that defeated the last attempt.

MEASUREMENT ERRORS MADE GETTING HERE, both recorded because both looked like results: the first positive control ran on hidden_cove, whose foliage and water put the NOISE FLOOR at 16.8% and peak 120, so a real effect was reported as inconclusive; and one comparison used JCE_ENVSHOT_NO_BUILD after a mutation run, so it measured the marked build against an unmarked one and reported 64.9% of the frame changing on a pair that should have been identical.

WHAT IS STILL DIFFERENT FROM UNITY, stated: there is no per-material keyword AUTHORING surface -- a designer cannot declare a keyword on a material and branch a shader graph on it. The axes are engine-declared, and the one that exists is driven by a component flag that already existed. That is a smaller authoring surface, not a missing mechanism: the manifest, the generator, the table and the single selection point are what a second axis needs, and it costs one entry.
features.compared: Unity strips per material with shader_feature/multi_compile and ships the variant set the project actually uses; UE has static switches with a permutation cooker; Godot 4 generates variants from its shader compiler. JCE has a hand-written fixed set (JceShaderSet, 20 named handles) and no generator, so one new axis multiplies across every existing variant by hand. The axis itself is proven cheap -- 8311 -> 1549 fragment instructions for the shadow-free case; what is missing is the machine that would let it be declared once.

features.feature: A layout container sizes itself to what its children need
features.compared: Unity ILayoutElement preferred/min size, Godot Control.get_minimum_size, Slate ComputeDesiredSize
features.evidence:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-08, one day after this row was split out of ui.layout.groups. A parent can now ask its children how big they need to be, which is the bottom-up pass Unity has as ILayoutElement, Godot as get_minimum_size and Slate as ComputeDesiredSize.
THE MEASURING ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS ASKED IN ONE PLACE ONLY. uc_preferred_size measured a UIText's shaped extent -- through the FONT AND LINE SPACING IT DRAWS WITH, so a fitter cannot size a panel to a different measurement than the draw uses -- and a LayoutGroup node's packed extent. But only the ContentSizeFitter asked it, and it measured that group's CHILDREN by their authored rect. Its own comment said why: 'without a per-child LayoutElement there is nothing else to consult'. There is now, and the deeper miss was that a child which is ITSELF a label or a group was never asked either.
So the same function is now RECURSIVE and asked at both moments: the fitter asks 'how big is this node's content' to size the node, and the arrange asks it of each child to divide the parent. One implementation, asked twice -- two implementations would be two answers to one question, which is the shape this tree keeps finding.
PRIORITY PER CHILD, and the order is the whole design: an explicit LayoutElement preferred size wins (that is the author speaking directly); otherwise the child's own CONTENT; otherwise its authored rect. A child that sets ignore_layout contributes nothing, for the same reason it takes no cell and no share.
THE CONTROL MATTERS MORE THAN THE FEATURE HERE: a measure pass that returned ZERO for anything it could not measure would collapse every plain image in every group -- a far worse failure than the one it fixes. So a child that cannot say keeps its authored size, and that is asserted: two images at 44px and 77px come out at 44 and 77.
MEASURED, and the case chosen because it is the one a headless test can actually prove: an outer column with two rows, both AUTHORED 30px tall, the second of which is itself a vertical group holding three 50px children. The plain row stays 30px; the nested row comes out over 100px because its own children need 150. Negative control: with the arrange no longer asking, that same assertion fails with 'laid out at its authored 30 px instead of the 150 px its own children need'.
TEXT IS THE OTHER HALF AND IS NOT ASSERTED IN THE UNIT TEST, stated rather than left to be discovered: a headless canvas has no pak and no asset root, so uc_get_font returns NULL, and jce_font_open_* refuses to return a font whose atlas TEXTURE is invalid -- a unit test has no bgfx device, so text measurement is unassertable in that process rather than merely inconvenient. A nested group needs no font, which is why it is the case that carries the claim. The text path is the same code with a different first branch, and it is the branch the ContentSizeFitter has been exercising since it shipped.
AND THE SAME SILENT TRUNCATION, FIXED HERE TOO: the measure gathered at most 128 children into a stack array, so a 200-row list measured to the size of its first 128 rows and the container came out short with nothing said -- the same defect, and the same fix, as the canvas walk's own child arrays.
COMPARED: Unity ILayoutElement preferred/min size propagation, Godot Control.get_minimum_size, Slate ComputeDesiredSize.

features.evidence:

WHAT THEY MISSED. Their audit covered exactly one of JCE's two UI systems. Everything they wrote about the scene-graph Canvas stack is accurate: the 12-entry registry at jce_scene_components_json.c:3270-3337 really is closed, uc_resolve_rect (jce_ui_canvas.c:482-543) really does solve every rect from authored anchors alone, and JceLayoutGroupComponent (jce_scene.h:1876-1887) only pushes size DOWN from parent to child (control_child_size_w/h, jce_ui_canvas.c:1502/1513) — it never sums content upward. But JCE ships a second, complete retained-mode UI system built on RmlUi 6.2, a full CSS layout engine, and content-driven sizing is its default behavior:
- conanfile.py:196 — self.requires("rmlui/6.2")
- CMakeLists.txt:366 — find_package(RmlUi REQUIRED)  (hard requirement, not an option)
- engine/CMakeLists.txt:515-525 — _jce_add_layer(jce_ui DIRS middleware/ui ... LINK_PRIVATE RmlUi::RmlUi ...); the layer helper GLOBs the whole directory (engine/CMakeLists.txt:43), so jce_ui_rmlui.cpp compiles unconditionally — no #if, no feature flag.
- engine/src/middleware/ui/jce_ui_rmlui.cpp:970 — b->context->Update() runs RmlUi's layout pass every frame.
- Public, SDK-exported surface: engine/include/jce/middleware/ui/jce_ui.h (all JCE_API), umbrella engine/include/jce/api_ui.h.

The mechanism itself: RmlUi Source/Core/Layout/LayoutDetails.cpp:215 LayoutDetails::GetShrinkToFitWidth — "format the element ... then ask the resulting box for its shrink-to-fit width. For block containers, this is essentially its largest line or child box." Per-box overrides at BlockContainer.cpp:329 (max of children), ContainerBox.cpp:249 (flex), InlineContainer.cpp:214 (line boxes), FloatedBoxSpace.cpp:210. Auto height for block boxes is the CSS default via BuildBoxHeight (LayoutDetails.cpp:210).

IT ACTUALLY RUNS, in both directions the claim names, in engine-shipped content:
- FIT CHILDREN: engine/ui/engine_debug_hud.rml #hud-panel declares width:360dp and NO height ⇒ height is auto and derives from its stacked children; jce_ui_debug_hud.c:300-311 flips #extra-status between display:block and display:none at runtime, which resizes the panel live.

- EXPLICIT: engine/ui/engine_settings.rml:181 and :201 — width:auto on `select selectvalue` and `select selectbox option`. #settings-box is a flex column with max-height:86% and no fixed height (content-driven, clamped).

NOT built-but-unwired — real readers on both ends:
- Producers: caged_kingdom/src/game/ck_app.c:163 jce_ui_create, :184 jce_debug_hud_create, :192 jce_settings_create.
- Read-back of the auto-computed size: jce_ui_debug_hud.c:331 calls jce_ui_elem_get_bounds → jce_ui.c:192 → jce_ui_rmlui.cpp:784, which returns GetOffsetWidth()/GetOffsetHeight() — the laid-out box, not the authored one.
- Shipped to users: dist/sdk/{win32-x86_64,win32-aarch64,wasm,...}/share/jce/engine_ui/engine_debug_hud.rml and engine_settings.rml.

WHY THEIR GREP COULD NOT HIT IT. Every term they searched (fitter, preferred_size, LayoutElement, aspect_ratio_fitter, fit_to_content, shrink_to_fit, auto_size_rect) is Unity uGUI vocabulary. In this stack the spelling is CSS: `width: auto`, `height` omitted, `flex-grow`, `min-width`/`max-height`. Note their own list contained shrink_to_fit — the underscore form misses RmlUi's ShrinkToFit/"shrink-to-fit", and they restricted the search to engine/include, engine/src, editor/src and scripting while the demonstrating evidence lives in engine/ui/*.rml, conanfile.py and CMakeLists.txt.

WHY "behind" AND NOT "parity". The capability works, but only in the RmlUi document stack, which has no visual authoring: the editor treats .rml/.rcss as plain text (editor/src/panels/jce_panel_file_viewer.cpp:209, editor/src/viewers/jce_fv_code.cpp:106) — no Inspector, no viewport picking, no live preview. The stack that IS editor-authored, scene-serialized and component-scriptable — Canvas/RectTransform — genuinely has no fitter, which is also why UIScrollView.content_size (jce_scene.h:2067-2068) must be typed in by hand and defaults to 0 (jce_editor_component_defaults.cpp:996-997). In Unity (ContentSizeFitter/LayoutElement in uGUI), Godot (Container controls, fit_content) and UE (UMG SizeBox/Slate desired size), content sizing is available in the scene-graph UI the editor authors. So a JCE user building UI the editor way still cannot get a self-sizing panel — but one writing .rml gets a strictly richer engine (real flexbox, floats, tables, min/max) than uGUI's fitter. Existing-but-reachable-only-from-the-unauthored-stack is "behind", not "absent".  || CLOSED 2026-09-06. JceContentSizeFitterComponent (horizontal_fit, vertical_fit; Unconstrained or Preferred, per axis), registered, round-tripped as `contentSizeFitter`, addable and editable in the Inspector. The walk fits a node's rect BEFORE anything reads it -- the node's own graphics, its hit test and every child rect are resolved from that rect, so fitting afterwards would size the panel and leave its contents laid out against the old box.
'Content' is decided by what the element IS: a UIText measures its own shaped text through THE FONT AND LINE SPACING IT DRAWS WITH, because a fitter that measures differently from the draw puts the overflow back a pixel at a time; a LayoutGroup node measures the packed extent of its children. Anything else keeps its authored size, and the Inspector says so beside the control rather than leaving an author to set Preferred on an image and conclude the component is broken.
FLAGLESS: the 64-bit JCE_COMP_FLAG space is FULL (all 64 bits allocated), so this is presence-gated like IkConstraints and FootIk -- a documented pattern here, and worth knowing before the next component.
MEASURED (d3d11, black_hole_lab HUD, editor Game view, floor exactly 0 px; the component added to all 3 UIText nodes):
  floor  no component, twice        0 px (0.000%)
  component, both axes Unconstrained 0 px (0.000%)  BYTE-IDENTICAL
  both axes Preferred           23978 px (2.238%)  mean 0.370
The middle row is the control that matters: adding the component in its default state changes literally nothing, so the 2.238% is the FIT and not the component's presence.
jce_ui_canvas.c crossed the 3000-line cap the moment this landed in it, so the fitter is its own file. Raising the cap would have been cheaper and wrong -- this was the newest code in the file. The seam is three values (scene, canvas, ui scale), not UCFrame, because jce_ui_canvas_widgets.h already records that a UCFrame boundary would be 'the file's interior rather than a seam'.

Godot Containers size themselves from get_combined_minimum_size(), so a Label in a VBoxContainer grows the box automatically. UE UMG SizeBox / Auto-sized slots do the same. features.feature: Layout groups auto-arrange children horizontally, vertically or in a grid
features.evidence:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-07. The row named three concrete gaps and all three are closed; the third turned out to be a live defect rather than a parity shortfall.
GAP 3 FIRST, BECAUSE IT WAS A BUG. The 128-child cap was described as a cap on arrangement and is worse than that: uc_layout_draw read the TRUE child count and then gathered at most 128 into stack arrays, and jce_scene_get_children truncates SILENTLY. Everything downstream reads the gathered array -- the draw, the packing, the scissor stack, the raycast hit list -- so a node's 129th UI child was never drawn and never clickable, with nothing said. 128 children is an inventory, a server browser, a chat log. The stack arrays are now a fast path: one heap block carved into the three arrays when a node genuinely has more, so the common case stays allocation-free in a function whose recursion is the stack. Tested by CLICKING the last row of a long list, not by counting -- a count test would stay green if the gather were fixed and the raycast list were not. Against the old code: 12 rows PASS, 129 FAIL, 168 FAIL, 200 FAIL.
AND IT UNCOVERED A SECOND, WORSE ONE. Writing that test crashed the runner at 0xC0000409 before a single assertion. flecs keeps its name index unique PER SCOPE and ABORTS THE PROCESS on a duplicate -- no return value, nothing logged. create_entity and set_entity_name both knew this and both asked ecs_lookup(world, name), which searches the ROOT; set_parent did not ask at all. Since create-then-parent is the ordinary order, the check ran against a scope the name never had to be unique in and the collision landed one call later, so 'N children with the same name under one parent' killed the process. One rule now lives in jce_scene_names.c and all three sites ask it; the rename is not observable because JceCompAuthoredName is the identity for the public API and for serialization. Fixed in the same commit as the cap, since the cap's own test could not run without it.
GAP 1: WEIGHTED PER-CHILD SIZING. New JceLayoutElementComponent -- min, preferred and flexible per axis, plus ignore_layout. This is Unity's LayoutElement, Godot's size_flags_stretch_ratio and Slate's FSlateChildSize::Fill, and the row was right that none of it was expressible: control_child_size gave strictly EQUAL shares, and with it off a child's own rect was its size, so neither 'twice the space' nor 'at least this big' could be said. The pass is preferred, then leftover by weight, then minimums. Measured through jce_ui_canvas_entity_rect -- where the child ACTUALLY DREW after a real headless render, not the arithmetic: weights 1 and 2 over a 300px leftover give 150 and 250; a zero weight beside a flexible one gives 80 and 320; min raises a child under it to 120 and leaves one already at 200 alone.
THE NEGATIVE CONTROL THAT MATTERED MOST: two children with NO LayoutElement keep their own widths and pack from the start, exactly as before -- and preferred = -1 behaves identically to having no component, so adding one and leaving it alone cannot change the picture. A component that is a trap the moment it is added is worse than no component.
GAP 2: GRID CONSTRAINT. grid_constraint (Flexible / Fixed Columns / Fixed Rows), grid_constraint_count, grid_start_corner, grid_start_axis -- all APPENDED, and every zero is what a grid already did, so no authored scene moves. A 3-column grid was previously not expressible at all: you resized the parent until three happened to fit and it silently became four on a wider screen. Tested: 60px cells in a 400px parent flexibly give six columns and fixed-3 gives three, with item 3 wrapping; vertical start axis puts item 1 BELOW item 0 rather than beside it; upper-right puts item 0 in the last column and walks left on the SAME lattice.
ignore_layout was declared, parsed, serialized and shown -- and would have shipped with no reader, which is the exact shape this audit exists to find. It is wired in the same change: an ignored child keeps its own rect and takes neither a cell nor a share NOR A SPACING GAP, which is the half a skip-the-placement-only fix misses, and the test asserts the gap.
THE WHOLE SURFACE, NOT HALF OF IT. Round-trips through the scene file, registered with the component registry (legacy_flag 0 -- the 64-bit JCE_COMP_FLAG space is full at bit 63, and the registry documents 0 for new components), an Inspector editor, an ADD-COMPONENT DESCRIPTOR, and 15 locales. The descriptor was caught by test_jce_editor_component_registry, which already asserts every engine component can be ADDED: binding only the draw function makes a component that can be edited once it exists and can never be created.
jce_ui_canvas.c crossed the 3000-line cap when this landed, so the arrangement moved to jce_ui_canvas_layout.c -- the same thing that happened when the ContentSizeFitter landed, and jce_ui_canvas_fitter.h records the reasoning. The seam is five values and no UCFrame, which is the test that file gives for whether a split is a seam or an interior.
STILL NOT CLAIMED, AND THE ROW SAYS SO RATHER THAN ROUNDING UP: there is no BOTTOM-UP MEASUREMENT. Nothing reports content height upward, so a vertical group cannot size its rows to their text -- UIText's best_fit shrinks glyphs inside a fixed rect instead. Unity's ILayoutElement, Godot's minimum_size and Slate's ComputeDesiredSize all do this. It is a separate feature (a measure pass before the arrange pass), not a missing field, and it is tracked as ui.layout.content-measure rather than hidden inside this row.
COMPARED: Unity HorizontalLayoutGroup / VerticalLayoutGroup / GridLayoutGroup + LayoutElement; Godot BoxContainer / GridContainer + size flags; Slate SBoxPanel + FSlateChildSize.
features.compared: Unity's HorizontalLayoutGroup/VerticalLayoutGroup/GridLayoutGroup run a two-pass ILayoutElement protocol (minWidth/preferredWidth/flexibleWidth per child) and GridLayoutGroup exposes startCorner, startAxis and a FixedColumnCount/FixedRowCount constraint. Godot's HBoxContainer/VBoxContainer/GridContainer propagate each child's combined minimum size up the tree. UE's Horizontal/VerticalBox slots carry Auto vs Fill sizing rules. JCE has the containers and their alignment but not the per-child sizing protocol.

features.feature: A UI element can be rotated or scaled for pop and spin effects
features.evidence:
JceRectTransform (engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_scene.h:1843-1848) carries exactly five fields -- anchor_min, anchor_max, pivot, anchored_position, size_delta -- and no rotation or scale. uc_resolve_rect (engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_ui_canvas.c:482-543) returns a UCRect of {x,y,w,h} only, and every draw goes through the axis-aligned macros at :106-107 (jce_draw_filled_rect_view / jce_draw_textured_rect_view). I also checked whether an entity's regular Transform could supply rotation: a grep for get_transform, TransformComponent and jce_scene_get_world across the whole of jce_ui_canvas.c returns nothing, so the canvas walk never reads a Transform at all. The pivot IS read (jce_ui_canvas_entity_pivot, jce_ui_canvas.h:254) but only as an anchoring reference point, never as a rotation centre.  || ADVERSARIALLY VERIFIED: a second agent was told to REFUTE this claim by finding the implementation, because this repository has been wrong about 'behind'/'absent' twice (auto-LOD, read off a truncated grep; script hot-reload, where interpreted scripts DO reload every Play). Verdict: claim stands -- Could not refute. I searched both UI stacks, all 48 local branch tips, the serializer, the inspector, the sequencer and the 2D draw API, and there is no per-element rotation and no per-element scale anywhere.

THE CLAIMANT'S EVIDENCE HOLDS, and I re-verified each leg independently: JceRectTransform is 5 float[2] fields (engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_scene.h:1843-1848); parse_rect_transform / ser_rect_transform move exactly 10 numbers, no rotation or scale key (engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_scene_components_ui.c:57-83); uc_draw_image is axis-aligned in every branch including 9-slice, TILED and FILLED (FILLED is a left-to-right UV crop, not radial) at engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_ui_canvas.c:649-720; the editor UI inspector exposes no rect rotation or scale control, only cv->scale_factor (editor/src/panels/jce_panel_inspector_ui.cpp:190). The UI view matrix is jce_m4_identity() with a plain ortho (jce_ui_canvas.c:2516-2518), so there is no whole-screen rotation either. Negative control across branches: `git show <branch>:engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_ui_canvas.c | grep -ci "rotation\|rotate"` returns 0 on all 48 local branch tips, main and track-space-project included.

WHAT THEY MISSED, and it does not save the claim -- there is a SECOND UI stack: RmlUi 6.2 (conanfile.py:196), public API engine/include/jce/middleware/ui/jce_ui.h, backend engine/src/middleware/ui/jce_ui_rmlui.cpp. RmlUi's RCSS natively supports `transform: rotate()/scale()` plus @keyframes/transition -- literally pop and spin. But JceRmlRenderInterface (jce_ui_rmlui.cpp:223-425) overrides CompileGeometry, RenderGeometry, ReleaseGeometry, EnableScissorRegion, SetScissorRegion, LoadTexture, GenerateTexture and ReleaseTexture, and NEVER overrides SetTransform. RmlUi declares it at RenderInterface.h:93 with a default no-op and its own doc note says the renderer must apply the matrix; grep for `SetTransform` or `Matrix4f` across all of engine/ and editor/ returns ZERO hits. So RmlUi computes the rotation and hands it to a function that throws it away: geometry is submitted in untransformed layout coordinates and the element draws square. This is exactly the "code exists, reader is missing" shape -- and it is a LIVE path, not a dead one: caged_kingdom/src/game/ck_app.c:163 calls jce_ui_create, so the main consumer project's document UI would silently ignore any rotate/scale it authored.

CARRIER WITHOUT READER, confirmed a second way: every UI entity has a JceTransform carrying rotation and scale, and the sequencer can key JCE_SEQ_PROP_ROT_EULER_X/Y/Z and SCALE_X/Y/Z/UNIFORM on it (engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_scene_sequencer.h:31-37). But grep for Transform across jce_ui_canvas.c + jce_ui_canvas_widgets.c yields only `bgfx_set_view_transform` (:2518) and the word RectTransform -- the canvas walk reads no Transform at all. So you can author a spin keyframe on a UI entity and nothing moves.

NEAREST WORKING THING, and why it is still "absent" not "behind": JceCanvasComponent.scale_factor IS read (jce_ui_canvas.c:2609-2610) and multiplies fr.ui_scale, which really does scale size_delta and anchored_position (uc_resolve_rect :492-494), font px (:941), 9-slice border widths (:713), the slider handle (:1180) and scrollbar thickness (:1338). Since jce_scene_get_canvas returns a mutable pointer, a game can animate it per frame -- a genuine uniform scale, but of an ENTIRE canvas subtree, not of one element, and it gives no rotation at all. Half the claim (spin) has no implementation on any path; the other half (scale) exists only at canvas granularity.

ASIDE FOR THE LEDGER, found while reading the same file: contracts/engine-parity.json row `ui.canvas.world-space` is marked "parity" citing jce_ui_canvas.c:2595 as "the mode branches the draw". That line is a CanvasScaler EXCLUSION, and the comment immediately above it (:2582-2594) states in-tree that Camera- and World-space canvases are NOT implemented, that the root rect is the framebuffer unconditionally, and that render_mode "is read nowhere else in this file". That row should not be "parity".  || CLOSED 2026-09-06. JceRectTransform gains rotation_deg and scale[2] (Unity's rotation and localScale), round-tripped as rotation/scaleX/scaleY, edited in the RectTransform inspector. The draw layer gains a JceRectXform and three entry points -- filled rect, textured rect and a whole glyph BATCH -- all writing their four corners through one routine, so a rotated panel and its rotated label cannot disagree about what the angle means.
THE PIVOT IS ABSOLUTE, in draw-space pixels, and that is the design decision the feature turns on: a button is an image quad plus a run of glyph quads, each glyph with its own little rect, so a fraction-of-rect pivot would spin every glyph about its own centre and scatter the word. The canvas resolves the element's pivot once and hands the same absolute point to the panel and to every glyph.
MEASURED (d3d11, black_hole_lab HUD, editor Game view where a screen-space canvas draws; that view's floor is exactly 0 px):
  floor  no transform, twice        0 px (0.000%)
  rotation 12 deg              50171 px (4.683%)  mean 5.954
  scale 1.4                   117545 px (10.97%)  mean 16.716
Scale moves more than a 12-degree rotation, which is the ordering a larger visual change should have. The capture shows the panel turned and the text turned WITH it.
NOT DONE, and named rather than left to be found: the transform applies to the element, NOT to its children -- the canvas walk passes an axis-aligned parent rect down, so propagation would need that walk to carry a 2D matrix. Unity does propagate. Math-typeset labels (jce_text_draw_math_view) keep their own batching and stay upright.
features.compared: Unity's RectTransform inherits Transform rotation and localScale, and the pivot is the rotation centre -- a scale-punch on a button press is the standard idiom. Godot's Control has rotation, scale and pivot_offset properties. UE UMG gives every widget a Render Transform (translation, scale, shear, angle). In JCE a UI icon cannot be spun or a button cannot pop on click without leaving the ECS UI system entirely. JCE now rotates and scales a UI element about its pivot, panel and label together; nested propagation is the remaining difference.

features.feature: A character the font lacks is drawn from a backup font, not a box
features.evidence: A SHIPPING BLOCKER FOR ANY NON-LATIN PROJECT, and it was total rather than partial: a font that lacks a codepoint rasterises .notdef -- a crossed box -- so a Latin UI face in front of a Chinese, Japanese or Korean string drew a box for EVERY character. jce_text.c already said so about U+0020 and the canvas already pre-rendered the i18n codepoint set, which does not help: the glyphs are not in the face. NOW: jce_font_add_fallback(font, fallback) builds a chain of up to JCE_FONT_MAX_FALLBACKS (4), and the shaper ITEMIZES -- the string is split into runs, each run the longest span one font covers, and each run is shaped with its OWN font. That is not an optimisation: HarfBuzz shapes with exactly one font, so a version that shaped the whole string with the primary and merely rasterised the missing glyphs elsewhere would put full-width CJK glyphs on Latin advances. Each shaped glyph carries the slot that produced it (JceShapedGlyph.font_slot) so the draw picks the right atlas, and the BASELINE stays the primary's ascender -- two faces opened at one point size do not agree on the top of their box, and using each glyph's own would make a mixed line ripple. The primary always wins when it covers the character, so adding a fallback cannot change a string that already rendered. AUTHORED AS DATA, not code: JceProject.ui_font_fallbacks is a ';'-separated list applied by jce_ui_canvas_set_font_fallbacks, called at all THREE sites beside jce_ui_canvas_set_default_font -- both editor viewports and jce_default_main.inc.h -- so a chain that worked in the editor and not in the shipped exe is not expressible. Fallbacks descend the SAME three-tier ladder as the font they back (project asset root, active VFS, canvas pak); that ladder moved into engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_ui_canvas_resources.c so both halves read one copy of it. MEASURED ON PIXELS, D3D11, editor Game view in Play, on a fixture whose primary provably lacks the characters: Caveat.ttf (752 glyphs; U+4E2D and U+6587 absent, checked with fontTools) drawing the Chinese string '中文游戏引擎' at 72px, with JCE.ttf (6,952 glyphs, both present) as the fallback. Both fonts already ship in this project, so the measurement does not depend on a face that is only on one machine. Fallback on vs off changes 10930 px (1.289% of envshot's viewport region), peak 109/255, and the capture shows six crossed boxes replaced by the six characters. THE CONTROL IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE FRAME: a second label reading 'Engine' -- which the primary DOES cover -- changes exactly 0 px, so the chain filled in rather than took over. NOISE FLOOR: 0 px in both halves between two captures of one build, which is also the determinism the shaper promises. GATED by tools/lint/check_text_shape_cached.py rule 3: jce_text.c's draw path must READ the shaped glyph's font_slot. A draw that ignores the tag pulls every fallback glyph out of the PRIMARY's atlas -- right spacing, right line breaks, and a tofu box for every CJK character, i.e. a regression that reads as a missing font rather than as a missing line of code. Negative control verified to turn it red. Itemization itself is covered headlessly in tests/renderer/test_jce_text_shape_cache.c (13/13), including the failure that is silent by construction: HarfBuzz reports clusters relative to the buffer it was handed, so a second run whose offset was not added back decodes from the start of the string and every fallback glyph comes out as some other character WITH THE COUNT AND THE ADVANCES STILL RIGHT.
features.compared: Godot 4's Font.fallbacks is the same shape -- an ordered array consulted per character. Unity's TextMeshPro keeps a fallback list plus per-asset scale and baseline offsets. Unreal's composite fonts map by character RANGE, which is more expressive than a flat list. JCE has the core capability at Godot's level; the two named gaps are per-fallback baseline and scale offsets, and range-based mapping. Neither Unity nor JCE falls back to a SYSTEM font automatically -- the list is authored either way.

features.feature: Outline, glow and soft shadow on text, from the distance field
features.compared: Unity TextMeshPro outline/glow/underlay, Godot FontVariation outline, UE Slate text outline
features.evidence:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-08, the same day this row was split out of ui.text.sdf-font. Outline and drop shadow, both authorable, both from the field that already exists.
WHY THE FIELD MAKES THEM CHEAP, which is why they belong here and not on a material: once a glyph is stored as distance rather than coverage, an OUTLINE is a SECOND THRESHOLD on the number the face already read, and a SHADOW is that same read at an offset. Any other route -- a second draw, a second atlas, a blur pass -- spends a pass to produce what one already-loaded value answers. That is why TextMeshPro, Godot's MSDF fonts and Slate all put them on the field.
WHAT PLAIN TEXT PAYS: two compares. Both effects sit behind branches on UNIFORMS, which is uniform control flow -- every fragment in a draw takes the same side, so there is no divergence and the shadow's SECOND TEXTURE READ does not happen at all for a label without one. On the low-end target this engine aims at, an unconditional second sample would have been the whole cost of the feature charged to labels that never asked for it.
MEASURED in Play, a 400px label drawn from the 256px atlas ceiling:
  noise floor (two identical captures)   0 px -- the capture is deterministic
  OUTLINE 6px vs plain    48606 px (4.44%), mean 6.00, peak 221
  SHADOW 10px vs plain    33269 px (3.04%), mean 4.94, peak 234
THREE CONTROLS, ALL AT ZERO PIXELS, and they are the reason this is 'parity' and not 'it renders something':
  a shadow OFFSET of 10px with ALPHA 0 changes NOTHING -- so the alpha really is the gate, the second sample really is skipped, and a scene that predates these keys (alpha defaults to 0) is untouched;
  a BITMAP label with outline AND shadow set changes NOTHING -- the effects are ignored without a distance field, deliberately, because a coverage atlas has no distance to threshold twice;
  and the same outline measurement after the API was restructured came back byte-identical (48606 px, 6.000, 221), so that refactor was pure.
THE API CHANGED MID-IMPLEMENTATION, AND THE GATE IS WHY. The style started as a SETTER, copying jce_font_set_sdf_spread next door. The dedup audit caught it: global-state 859 -> 861, two new file-statics. Folding them into one object did not help -- the old s_text_xf beside them was a POINTER and had never been counted, so the fold was cosmetic. The real answer was that the neighbour was the wrong one to copy: a spread MUST be a mode because it is consumed when the font is OPENED and there is no draw call to hang it on, while a style is consumed by the draw and can simply be an argument. jce_text_draw_styled_view_xf takes it, borrowed for the call exactly like the transform beside it. Count back to 859 at baseline, honestly rather than by choosing an uncounted type -- and the 'a style left set is worn by the next label' hazard the setter's own comment had to warn about is now impossible.
AND A SECOND GATE CAUGHT THE FALLOUT: renaming the symbol left an exemption naming a function that no longer exists, and check_editor_consumption refused it. A stale exemption is a permanent silent hole.
UNITS ARE PIXELS OF THE DRAWN GLYPH, because that is the only unit an author can see. The renderer converts to the field's distance units, and that conversion needs the atlas spread and the draw scale -- an author has neither. Same derivation as the smoothing width, which is why they sit together in the code.
NOT CLAIMED: glow (an outline with a wide, soft falloff), per-character styling, and TextMeshPro's underlay/bevel/bump set. Those are more thresholds on the same value rather than new machinery, but none of them is authorable today and this row does not imply they are.
COMPARED: Unity TextMeshPro outline + underlay, Godot FontVariation outline, UE Slate text outline.

features.feature: SDF text (crisp at any scale)
features.evidence:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-08. Glyphs can be rasterised as a signed distance field and drawn by a shader that recovers the outline per fragment, so one atlas stays crisp at any size instead of softening as it is scaled.
THE ROW'S PREMISE WAS HALF RIGHT, AND THE OTHER HALF WAS A DIFFERENT BUG. 'Text scales by resampling the atlas' is true of jce_text_draw_scaled, but the UI canvas re-rasterises per pixel size and draws at scale 1.0, so it never magnified -- EXCEPT above the atlas ceiling. uc_get_font clamps rasterisation to 256px (correctly: a CJK set at 400px is an enormous atlas) and the draw then used 1.0 anyway, so a label authored at fontSize 400 came out at 256px -- 36% smaller than asked for, silently. Fixing that is what makes magnification reachable from authoring at all, so the two landed together: every measured extent is now scaled by requested/actual, which is exactly 1.0 for every label at or below the ceiling and therefore moves nothing already authored.
NO DERIVATIVES, DELIBERATELY. The usual SDF shader takes its filter width from fwidth(); dFdx/dFdy are not in GLSL ES 1.00 without OES_standard_derivatives and this engine's floor is ES 2.0 / desktop GL 2.1. The width arrives as a uniform the CPU already knows, and fs_text_sdf is on the essl1 allowlist -- the low-end target this engine is aimed at gets the feature rather than being the reason not to ship it.
MEASURED, with a per-mode floor and an honest control:
  400px label, magnified 1.56x from the 256px ceiling:
      bitmap  3944 edge px / 39978 stroke px = 0.099
      SDF     1368 edge px / 42745 stroke px = 0.032   -> 0.32x the edge
  180px, dscale exactly 1.0 (no magnification at all):
      SDF edge = 0.83x the bitmap's -- still slightly tighter, not softer
  Run-to-run spread across independent captures of the same mode: EXACTLY 0.0000, so none of this is noise. Stroke area differs by under 7%, so it is not 'SDF drew a thinner glyph' either.
THE COST, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: at 22px the same string came out with 41 near-white pixels against the bitmap path's 10 -- the field has no hinting, so body text renders visibly BOLDER, not crisper. That is why the flag is opt-in and off by default, and the Inspector says so at the checkbox. Unity's TextMeshPro is opt-in for the same reason.
THREE DEFECTS FOUND GETTING HERE, none of them the feature's own idea:
  (1) THE SMOOTHING WIDTH WAS OUT BY EXACTLY TWO. The first version used 0.5/(spread*scale), which reads right and spreads the edge over TWO screen pixels; at 1:1 that measured 2.34x the bitmap path's edge -- SOFTER, the opposite of the feature's claim. Deriving it instead of tuning it gives 0.25/(spread*scale), and the arithmetic and the measurement agreed on the factor. A version tuned until it looked better would have landed on a number with no reason behind it.
  (2) THE UNIFORM WAS CREATED ON ONLY ONE OF TWO RENDERER INIT PATHS. jce_renderer.c initialises separately for the real backend and for NOOP, and u_sdfParams went into the NOOP one. A zero uniform handle is a VALID handle belonging to some other uniform, so the write landed somewhere unrelated rather than failing -- and the symptom was not missing text but a grey slab behind every glyph, which reads as a font bug. Found by capturing the screen rather than by reasoning about it.
  (3) THE ATLAS PACKS GLYPHS INTO ALPHA, not red. The shader's first draft sampled .x, which is the constant 255 the blit writes for white -- every glyph would have been a solid block. Reading .w means the packing is untouched: a distance field lands in the same channel coverage already used.
WHY 'parity' AND WHAT IS STILL NOT CLAIMED. All of it is authorable and round-trips: JceUITextComponent.sdf, the Inspector checkbox with the trade-off stated at the point of choice, 15 locales, and the same code path in the editor Game View and the shipped exe. What TextMeshPro has beyond this is the effects the field makes cheap -- outline, glow, soft shadow, per-character bold -- which are shader work on top of a field that now exists, not a second rasteriser. Recorded as ui.text.sdf-effects rather than left implied by this row's 'parity'.
COMPARED: Unity TextMeshPro (SDF), Godot 4 MSDF fonts, UE Slate distance-field fonts.
features.compared: Unity TextMeshPro is SDF by default; UE Slate uses SDF; Godot has MSDF fonts

features.feature: A string is shaped once, not once per frame
features.evidence: A SEPARATE ROW FROM ui.text.batching ON PURPOSE, and the split is the point: batching is about SUBMITS and this is about the CPU before them. That row went to parity while every visible string was still being shaped from scratch every frame, and a one-draw-call line of text that costs a full HarfBuzz shape per frame is only half the capability. THE STATE THIS ENDS: jce_text_draw_scaled_view and jce_text_measure each did hb_buffer_create -> add_utf8 -> guess_segment_properties -> hb_shape -> hb_buffer_destroy on EVERY call. Shaping is a pure function of (font, string) -- `scale` multiplies the returned 26.6 values, it is not an input to HarfBuzz -- so a label whose text has not changed had one right answer and recomputed it every frame; and because a UI measures before it draws, TWICE per frame per visible string, with two HarfBuzz buffer allocations. NOW: engine/src/renderer/jce_text_shape.{h,c}, a direct-mapped 256-slot table keyed by (owner, bytes), holding the decoded codepoint and the 26.6 offsets/advance per glyph. Direct-mapped because a hit must do nothing but compare -- an LRU does bookkeeping on the path that has to stay cheap. The codepoint is decoded AT SHAPE TIME from the cluster, so a cached run does not refer into the caller's buffer and the per-frame utf8 decode goes with the per-frame shape. Strings over 512 bytes take a single scratch slot and re-shape: the key IS the string, so an uncapped key is an uncapped allocation driven by whatever the game renders. jce_font_close forgets the font's runs, because the key is its address and the next allocation can land there. MEASURED, tests/renderer/test_jce_text_shape_cache.c (9/9): the second lookup of an unchanged string returns the SAME storage and does not increment the HarfBuzz counter; and a timed ratio over 200k iterations of 10 UI labels puts a cache hit at 14.3x / 19.0x / 20.0x cheaper than the code it replaced across three runs, against a 2x threshold. Every one of those is a LOWER BOUND: the test shapes with hb_font_get_empty(), the cheapest shape HarfBuzz can do -- no cmap, no GSUB, no GPOS, no kerning -- and a real font does strictly more work per shape and none per hit. SIX MUTATIONS were injected and the suite re-run against each; three die. The three survivors are recorded in the test's own header rather than left to be found: one is not a defect (equivalent code), one is unreachable because the owner is in the hash as well as the comparison, and one -- reading every glyph's advance from glyph 0 -- is invisible only because every advance in the reachable fixture is zero, and is the kind of failure that stacks every character on one pixel the first time the editor opens. GATED by tools/lint/check_text_shape_cached.py: nothing under engine/src may call hb_shape or hb_buffer_create except the cache, and jce_text.c must still call it -- rule 1 alone is satisfied by a renderer that shapes nothing. Both negative controls verified to turn it red. The gate exists because tests/ is gitignored on this branch and because the regression it guards (a third entry point, or 'simplifying' one back to a local buffer) produces identical pixels. jce_text_shutdown logs the hit/miss split so the claim is checkable in a real run and not only in a test; note that envshot KILLS the editor rather than shutting it down, so that line appears for a shipped game exe and not in a capture log.  ||  2026-09-08, same day: the cache also ITEMIZES. A font chain has a primary and fallbacks and HarfBuzz shapes with exactly one font, so the split into per-font runs happens here rather than in the draw loop -- it is an input to what the cache key answers, not an output, and the same bytes against a different chain are a different run (the chain's generation is part of the key for that reason). See ui.text.font-fallback-chain.
features.compared: Unreal caches shaped text in FShapedTextCache (keyed by text range + font, with an explicit flush) precisely so Slate does not re-shape unchanged strings; Unity's TextMeshPro rebuilds a text mesh only when the string, font or settings change; Godot's TextServer shaped buffers are owned by the control and re-shaped only when dirtied. All three treat shaping as the expensive half of text rendering. JCE now does too, with two named differences: the table is fixed-size and direct-mapped rather than an LRU (a collision evicts rather than probes), and the key is the whole string rather than a range, so a paragraph edited at its end re-shapes entirely.
