features.feature: Bake static lighting into lightmaps and mix with realtime
features.evidence:
There is a baker, but it cannot produce per-object lightmaps. JceLightmapBakeDesc (engine/include/jce/renderer/jce_lightmapper.h:53-62) takes ONE receiver plane -- origin, u_axis, v_axis, normal, width, height -- so a bake covers a single quad, described in the header comment as 'the terrain floor'; occluders are boxes and spheres only (:27-35). The editor panel confirms the scope: editor/src/panels/jce_panel_lightmap_bake.cpp:1-19 says it maps (u,v) to (x,z) at the scene bounding box's minY and writes an AO floor PNG, and the only lightmapper call in the whole panel is jce_lightmapper_bake_sh9 for a single probe at :528. Nothing consumes a lightmap at draw time: grep for 'lightmap' across engine/shaders returns only comments referring to the SH9 convention, there is no s_lightmap sampler, JceMeshRenderer has no lightmap_index or UV2 field (engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_scene.h:76-137), and no light has a bake mode -- grep for shadowmask, shadow_mask, mixed_lighting, bake_mode and light_mode across engine/ and editor/ finds no such field. The engine's actual static-lighting answer is SH9 probes (jce_lightmapper.h:89-105 plus jce_scene_light_probe.c:26).
REFUTED 2026-09-20 -- 'absent' was wrong, and by a wide margin. engine/include/jce/renderer/jce_lightmapper.h is a real CPU baker: directional + point lights with shadowing against box and sphere occluders, spotlights clipped to a cone, writing an RGBA8 irradiance map. It is CONSUMED: editor/src/panels/jce_panel_lightmap_bake.cpp:528 calls jce_lightmapper_bake_sh9 from an editor bake panel, and engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_scene_light_probe.c:26 calls jce_lightmapper_sh9_dering at runtime. So both halves an 'absent' verdict denies -- the bake and a consumer -- exist.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING is the second half of the row's title: MIXED lighting. There is no baked/realtime blend mode (Unity's Baked / Mixed / Realtime per light, with shadowmask), and the baker's own header says 'No SH / probe support yet' for the direct path. The gap is a mode, not a subsystem.
features.compared: Unity: Progressive Lightmapper bakes per-object lightmaps into UV2 with Baked/Mixed/Realtime light modes and Shadowmask. UE: Lightmass (or Lumen) with static/stationary/movable lights and per-object lightmap resolution. Godot 4: LightmapGI bakes per-mesh lightmaps with light bake modes Disabled/Static/Dynamic. JCE has probe-based indirect only; a shipped scene cannot bake sun shadows or bounce onto its geometry, and there is no mixed mode where baked shadows hand off to realtime at a distance.

features.feature: Imported blendshape animation curves play back at runtime
features.evidence:
Built-but-unwired, and I traced both ends. engine/src/renderer/jce_gltf_loader.c:1226-1303 explicitly "un-drops" the glTF "weights" animation channel and builds a JceMorphWeightTrack per node; jce_morph_weight_track_sample is implemented at engine/src/middleware/animation/jce_morph.c:335 and published at engine/include/jce/middleware/animation/jce_morph.h:179. The ONLY runtime consumer, sr_resolve_morph_weights (engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_sr_anim.c:2052), passes the track argument as NULL at :2086 with the comment "track = NULL (no clip channel sampled yet)". A repo-wide grep for jce_morph_weight_track_sample returns the definition, the header, and one comment in engine/src/renderer/jce_model.h:90 -- zero call sites. The missing reader is sr_resolve_morph_weights: it must fetch the model's track via jce_model_morph_anim_track (engine/src/renderer/jce_model.h:91, itself uncalled and not in the public header) and pass it where NULL is today. Net effect: an imported facial-animation clip moves nothing; only the static per-instance JceMorphWeightsComponent does anything.
REFUTED 2026-09-20 -- 'absent' was wrong. The whole chain exists and is wired: jce_morph.h declares JceMorphWeightTrack with the glTF key-major layout and STEP/LINEAR interpolation; engine/src/renderer/jce_gltf_loader.c:1314 CREATES a track per imported animation; engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_sr_morph.c:236 SAMPLES it every frame. That is exactly 'imported blendshape animation curves play back at runtime', which is what the row asked for.
features.compared: Unity plays glTF/FBX blendshape weight curves through the Animator/Animation clip like any other float curve. UE morph target curves ride on the anim sequence and are evaluated by the anim graph every frame. Godot imports glTF morph weight tracks into the AnimationPlayer as ordinary value tracks. All three animate blendshapes from imported clips out of the box; JCE imports the data and then never reads it.

features.feature: Create and keyframe an animation clip inside the editor
features.evidence:
THE FORMAT EXISTS 2026-09-21; the authoring UI does not.
WHAT WAS STRUCTURALLY WRONG, and it was not the panel. jce_anim_clip_create had exactly two call sites in the whole tree -- jce_gltf_loader.c:1201 and jce_model_importer.cpp:1254 -- and there was NO SERIALISER ANYWHERE. A JceAnimClip could therefore only arrive by importing a model, and nothing could persist one: no clip shipped without its rig, no shared locomotion library, no hand-authored clip. JceSkeletalAnimator names its clips by string (clip_name, clip_names[8]) and both resolvers in jce_sr_anim.c scanned the MODEL and returned NULL if the name was not inside it. Building the keyframe UI on top of that would have produced a clip the editor can draw and nothing can keep.
WHAT NOW EXISTS. engine/include/jce/middleware/animation/jce_anim_clip_io.h (in the api_animation.h umbrella): exactly three functions -- parse, serialize, and a free for the string serialize returns. There is deliberately no load() and no save(): the first draft had both, and chasing check_editor_consumption's +4 instead of exempting it showed the VFS loader had ZERO callers and that save() was a second way to write the same bytes. The runtime reads PAK-FIRST through its own path resolver and then the host path, mirroring sr_anim_load_sm -- a host-only read returns NULL in a single-exe build with no loose cooked tree, so the first draft was an editor-only feature that would have failed silently in every packaged game. Both directions live in ONE file with the wire key names spelled once as constants, because a reader and a writer of one format in two places are two statements about it. Target and interpolation are written as NAMES, not the internal enum integers, so the values stay free to change; an unknown name degrades to a stated default rather than to whatever the switch's default branch happens to be.
BOTH HALVES HAVE A PRODUCT CONSUMER, which is the whole point. WRITER: the Animation Clip Editor's Export clips button writes the focused rig's clips beside its skeleton, and it reports PER CLIP rather than a total -- a refused clip leaves a name that resolves at author time and not at run time. (Not in jce_cook: that tool compiles with JCE_MODEL_IMPORTER_COOK_ONLY precisely so it does not link jce_animation or jce_renderer.) READER: both clip resolvers in jce_sr_anim.c now fall back to `<skeleton dir>/<name>.animclip.json`, so the name an author already types reaches a clip beside the rig. No new component field -- adding one would have made every existing scene's clip reference the old way of doing it -- and the writer and the reader agree on the path by construction rather than by documentation.
LIFETIME. A file clip has no other owner (the model owns its own), so it is cached on SrAnimInstance and released at BOTH instance-lifecycle sites, the model swap and the slot reclaim, which is where the retarget map and the override controller are already released. A miss is cached as a miss: without the negative entry a name in neither place stats the filesystem every frame for every entity.
COVERAGE. tests/middleware/animation/test_jce_anim_clip_io.c. Every failure this format can have produces a clip that PLAYS -- a dropped channel samples to the rest pose, a quaternion written with three components reads back with w=0, a missing duration plays frame one forever -- so the refusals are asserted as hard as the round trip: a clip with no usable channel is refused rather than returned empty, because an unplayable clip is indistinguishable from a character that is supposed to be standing still.
WHY NOT PARITY: THE AUTHORING UI IS STILL ABSENT. The Animation Clip Editor authors the frame-EVENT sidecar only; its own header says legacy float/vec3 tracks are dropped, and it counts them into a user-facing banner rather than dropping them silently. Keyframing a bone pose on a timeline -- set a pose, record it at time t, scrub, tangent handles -- is the remaining work, and it is now possible to build because what it produces can be saved and played.
features.compared: Unity's Animation window records and keyframes any property, including bone transforms, into an AnimationClip asset that exists independently of any model. UE's Sequencer and Anim Editor bake and edit AnimSequence assets. Godot's AnimationPlayer authors an Animation resource saved on its own. JCE now matches on the ASSET half -- a clip is a file that can be written, shipped, hand-edited and referenced by name -- and is behind all three on in-editor keyframing.

features.feature: Curves drawn in the curve editor drive something at runtime
features.evidence:
CLOSED 2026-09-20 as far as a script is concerned; still behind on the two halves below.
WHAT NOW EXISTS. engine/include/jce/resource/jce_curve.h (in the api_resource.h umbrella) defines JceCurveKey {t,v,tan_in,tan_out,interp} and JCE_CURVE_LINEAR/CUBIC/CONSTANT, with jce_curve_parse/load/destroy, channel_count/name/index/keys/key_count, eval, time_min/time_max and the keyless jce_curve_eval_keys. engine/src/resource/jce_curve.c reads the panel's own document -- including a pre-channels file (top-level keys) and out-of-order keys, both of which the panel accepts -- through <jce/os/core/jce_json.h>, the same facade the panel writes with.
ONE EVALUATOR AND ONE KEY READER, not two of each: the panel's eval_channel now forwards to jce_curve_eval_keys, and its load_curve takes keys and channel names from jce_curve_parse, keeping only the authoring extras (visible, colour, tMin/tMax/vMin/vMax) that JceCurve deliberately does not carry.
REACHABLE FROM GAMEPLAY. JceScriptHost.curve_eval + the generated jce.curve_eval(path, channel, t) in all seven languages; nil when the path, the document or the channel is missing, so a curve that evaluates to 0 and a curve that is not there are never one reading. The runtime caches the parsed curve per JceRuntime (RT_CURVE_CACHE_MAX 64), so a call inside on_update costs a name compare, not a JSON parse.
COVERAGE. tests/os/resource/test_jce_curve.c (11 cases; the load-bearing one asserts a tangent yields the same SLOPE at any key spacing, which is what an unscaled Hermite silently breaks) and tests/application/test_jce_runtime_curve.c (the real runtime host table; its point is sampling a curve where the authored value is ZERO, the only sample where a lossy `float curve_eval(...)` binding is distinguishable from this one).
WHY NOT PARITY, two named gaps. (1) There is no curve-typed AUTHORED FIELD: JceScriptParamKind is NUMBER/BOOL/TEXT/ENTITY, so an author points a script at a curve by typing its path into a TEXT param rather than picking the asset and editing it inline. (2) No built-in system samples a curve -- particles, paths and post-process all still take scalars. The audio rolloff gap is NOT counted here; it is its own row, audio.attenuation.custom-rolloff-curve.
ONE OF THE TWO NAMED GAPS CLOSED 2026-09-22, and the row stays BEHIND for the other. Gap (2) was "no built-in system samples a curve -- particles, paths and post-process all still take scalars". JceAudioSourceComponent.rolloff_curve is now the first built-in consumer: an AudioSource takes an authored volume-over-distance curve instead of one of the four analytic attenuation models, evaluated per voice per frame through rt_curve_fetch -- the SAME cache jce.curve_eval uses, made non-static rather than duplicated. See audio.attenuation.custom-rolloff-curve, which this closed.
GAP (1) IS UNCHANGED and is what still holds this row: there is no curve-typed AUTHORED FIELD. JceScriptParamKind is still NUMBER/BOOL/TEXT/ENTITY, so a script author still points at a curve by typing its path into a TEXT param instead of picking the asset and editing it inline. The audio field is a fixed component field that happens to hold a path; it is not the general 'this script parameter is a curve' type Unity's AnimationCurve is. And one built-in consumer is not the set Unity has -- particles, paths and post-process still take scalars.
features.compared: Unity's AnimationCurve is a serialisable FIELD TYPE any MonoBehaviour exposes, edited inline with the curve widget and sampled with curve.Evaluate(t); particle, audio and post-process systems consume curves without a script. UE's Curve Float/Vector assets are evaluated by Blueprints, timelines, material parameter collections and Niagara. Godot's Curve resource is sampled with curve.sample(t) from any script and consumed by GPUParticles and Path3D. JCE now matches the Godot script path -- an authored curve asset a script can sample -- and is behind all three on the field type and on engine-side consumers.

features.feature: Attach a prop or entity to an animated bone
features.evidence:
WAS ABSENT.  Nothing in this engine could attach an entity to a bone -- no
weapon in a hand, no jetpack on a spine, no torch held by an NPC.  A grep for
socket / attach_bone / bone_attach across engine/include returned only network
sockets.

THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN AND HAD NO CONSUMER.  jce_skeleton.h:92
has stated the recovery since it was written:

    joint_global = skin_matrix[i] * inverse(jce_skeleton_get_inverse_bind(skel, i))

A palette entry is `global * inverseBind` -- it moves a VERTEX and is not a
pose, which is why having the palette is not the same as knowing where a bone
is.  Nothing in the tree used that sentence.  jce_skin_bone_world() is it,
with the model-to-world root folded in, and it costs ONE 4x4 inverse per
QUERY: the palette is already computed and nothing new is stored per frame.

THE MATH IS IN A PURE HELPER BECAUSE THE FEATURE OTHERWISE COULD NOT BE
TESTED.  Standing up a JceSceneRenderer needs a graphics device -- no test in
this tree has ever created one -- so an accessor hung off the renderer would
have shipped unverifiable.  jce_skin_palette.h is "pure math, no bgfx" and its
tests run headless.  4 cases, and the load-bearing one is that a bone which
has MOVED reports where it moved to: the bind pose is a plausible-looking
answer, and a helper that ignored the palette would pass every rest-pose test
while pinning a weapon to the T-pose forever.

THE PASS RUNS IN THE RENDERER, NOT THE RUNTIME, and that is the design rather
than convenience.  sr_update_bone_attachments is called immediately after
sr_update_skinned_anims and before anything draws.  A runtime-side pass would
necessarily read LAST frame's palette, so a sword would trail the hand holding
it exactly while it is being swung -- visible precisely when it matters.

UNITY ATTACHES BY PARENTING, because there a bone IS a Transform.  Here bones
live in the palette and are not scene entities, so the offset has to be a
FIELD rather than the entity's own Transform: the pass overwrites that
Transform every frame, and an author who positioned the weapon with the gizmo
would watch their offset be consumed by its own output.

CONSUMES jce_scene_solve_local_pose from earlier the same day, which is what
makes an attachment on a PARENTED entity land correctly -- the socket is a
consumer that proves that primitive rather than a second copy of it.

WIRED EVERYWHERE, and one of them was found by a gate rather than by me:
the component struct, four accessors, the flecs DECLARE/DEFINE pair, the REG
row, parse/serw, the loader's src_id -> new_id remap (whose refs64[5] was
EXACTLY full, so the sixth ref would have written one past a stack array),
the editor descriptor table, the Add Component defaults, the Inspector drawer
and 7 i18n keys across 15 locales.  test_jce_editor_component_registry caught
the missing editor descriptor -- "engine components with no editor descriptor
(they cannot be added or edited in the Inspector): BoneAttachment".

MEASURED: jce.py test, including 4 pure cases for jce_skin_bone_world and 3
save/load cases for the component.  The round-trip one asserts the reference
points at the SAME ENTITY BY NAME, not that it is non-zero -- a stale id is
non-zero too, and in a scene with more than one entity it is a valid id for
the wrong object, which is the exact failure the remap exists to stop.

NOT MEASURED: a rendered frame showing a sword in a hand.  That needs a
device, a rigged model and a clip, and this machine is being hard-frozen to a
black screen.  The pass itself is therefore verified by construction and by
its inputs, not by a picture -- stated here rather than left for someone to
assume otherwise.
features.compared:
Unity: parent a GameObject to a bone Transform; the animator writes the bone
in LateUpdate and the child follows because it IS a child.  Unreal: named
SOCKETS on a skeletal mesh, with an offset transform per socket, plus
AttachToComponent.  Godot: BoneAttachment3D, a node that copies a bone's
global pose onto itself each frame -- which is the closest analogue to what
this does, and for the same reason: Godot's bones are not nodes either.

features.feature: 3D joints can be motorised or spring-driven to a target
features.evidence:
SHIPPED 2026-09-20.  A 3D joint can now be DRIVEN, and the four things the comparison names -- a powered door, an elevator, a turret, a suspension -- are each expressible and each measured.

THE SURFACE.  JceConstraintDesc gained use_motor / motor_target_velocity / motor_max_force for HINGE and SLIDER (Unity's HingeJoint.motor, Godot's HingeJoint3D motor), plus jce_physics_constraint_set_motor so the target can change while the game runs -- an authoring-time-only motor is a door that is either always opening or never opening.  JceConfigurableJointDesc gained a per-axis drive (JceJointDriveMode: off / velocity / spring, with target, spring, damper and max force, indexed 0..2 linear and 3..5 angular), which is Unity's xDrive / angularXDrive.  Both reach the authored component, the serialiser and the Inspector; the runtime tracks typed-constraint handles (JointEntry) so a script's comp_set on JceConstraintComponent reaches the solver on the next fixed tick.

THE UNITS, which are the part that would have shipped wrong silently.  Bullet is not consistent: btHingeConstraint::enableAngularMotor takes a maximum IMPULSE (btHingeConstraint.cpp:559 puts it straight into the solver row's limit) while btSliderConstraint::setMaxLinMotorForce and btRotationalLimitMotor::m_maxMotorForce take a FORCE the solver divides by the step rate itself (btSliderConstraint.cpp:510, btGeneric6DofConstraint.cpp:777).  One of three wants an impulse.  The conversion lives in one function, and test_max_force_is_a_torque_not_an_impulse measures it: under a 3 N*m opposing load an unjointed control reaches -35.9999 rad/s, a 0.05 N*m motor reaches -35.4000 (its contribution is +0.6 rad/s, exactly 0.05 N*m integrated over 2 s on an inertia of 0.1667) and a 50 N*m motor holds +2.0000, the commanded speed.  Passing the torque where an impulse belongs would have made the weak motor 60x stronger and nothing would have said so.

TWO REPAIRS FOUND ON THE WAY.  (1) cfg_apply_axis took a `limit` parameter and NEVER USED IT -- case 1, which the internal header defines as LIMITED, fell through to the LOCKED branch -- so every LIMITED axis of a configurable joint behaved as LOCKED and the authored linear_limit / angular_limit_deg did nothing, while the Inspector drew them and the scene file stored them.  test_jce_configurable_joint's limited-axis case stayed green throughout, because every assertion it made (never exceeds L, more constrained than the free reference) is equally true of a locked axis; it now also asserts the axis REACHES its limit, which is the only property that tells LIMITED from LOCKED.  (2) btGeneric6DofSpringConstraint::enableSpring writes m_enableMotor as well as m_springEnabled, so calling it after the motor state with want_spring false turned the velocity motor straight back off -- found by instrumenting, after the probe showed the bridge WAS reached with the right arguments and the axis still did not move.

WHAT UNITY STILL HAS: slerpDrive (a single rotational drive in quaternion space), freeSpin, and one drive carrying a position target AND a velocity target simultaneously.  The last is deliberate here: naming the mode makes 'driven to a position' and 'driven at a velocity' two authored states and an unset drive a third, where Unity's shape leaves a misconfigured drive and a disabled one looking identical.
features.compared: Unity HingeJoint has a JointMotor (targetVelocity, force) and ConfigurableJoint has xDrive/yDrive/zDrive/slerpDrive with spring, damper and maximumForce plus targetPosition/targetRotation.  UE physics constraints expose Linear and Angular Drives with strength/damping/target.  Godot's HingeJoint3D has motor/enable and target_velocity, and Generic6DOFJoint3D exposes per-axis motors and springs.  All three can build a powered door, elevator, turret or suspension from a joint -- and so can JCE as of 2026-09-20.  The remaining deltas are slerpDrive, freeSpin, and Unity's single drive struct carrying a position and a velocity target at once.

features.feature: Per-clip import settings: format, quality, mono, sample rate
features.evidence:
PARTIALLY CLOSED 2026-09-21, and the part that is missing is an ENCODER rather than a setting.
WHAT WAS WRONG. The entire cook-time policy for sound was one hardcoded size heuristic in tools/jce_cook.c (`sz < 2 * 1024 * 1024`), with no per-asset override in either direction: a 2.1 MB footstep set stayed encoded and paid a decode on every trigger, and a 1.9 MB ambience loop was expanded to raw PCM in the PAK.
WHAT NOW EXISTS. engine/src/resource/jce_audio_import_settings.{h,c} reads `<clip>.import.json` (kind 2) beside the asset, exactly as jce_model_import_settings does for kind 1, and carries three settings that each move real bytes: cook_mode (AUTO / ALWAYS / NEVER, overriding the heuristic in BOTH directions), force_mono, and a target sample_rate. The cook decision is one pure function, jce_audio_import_should_cook, called by both tools/jce_cook.c's should_cook and the in-process cooker, so the heuristic and the override cannot disagree in two places. The conversion runs in jce_cook_audio through ma_data_converter -- miniaudio already performs the decode, so there is one resampler rather than two answers to what 48k -> 22.05k sounds like -- and it runs AFTER the decode and BEFORE the info chunk is built, so the header describes the samples actually written (a clip whose header says 48000 over 22050 bytes plays at half speed and nothing errors).
AUTHORING. editor/src/panels/jce_panel_import_presets.cpp gained PK_AUDIO with the three controls, the .wav/.ogg/.mp3/.flac/.opus/.m4a/.aac classifier, preset persistence, the apply-to-folder match, the scan filter and 10 i18n keys in all 15 locales. Without it the sidecar would be a format nothing can author -- the mirror of a curve format nothing could read.
COVERAGE. tests/os/resource/test_jce_audio_import_settings.c: the defaults ARE today's behaviour (a clip with no sidecar cooks byte-identically), the heuristic at both sides of its edge, the override in both directions, NULL settings behaving as defaults (the bundle packer passes NULL), every refusal path landing on the defaults rather than on zeros, and an out-of-range cook_mode degrading to AUTO.
WHY NOT PARITY: FORMAT AND QUALITY ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT. This engine has no audio encoder. jce_cook_audio decodes to s16 PCM and writes it, and JceAssetAudioInfo.format is 0 (PCM_S16) at every write site, so a Compression Format control would have exactly one reachable value and a Quality slider would reach nothing at all -- a control that cannot change the output is worse than a missing one, because it looks like the decision it never makes. The panel states that in a line of text instead. Closing the row means adding an encoder (Vorbis or Opus at cook time plus a format tag the runtime honours), which is a codec unit, not a settings unit.
features.compared: Unity's AudioClip importer offers Load Type, Compression Format (PCM/ADPCM/Vorbis), Quality, Sample Rate Setting and Force To Mono per clip and per platform. UE's Sound Wave has compression quality, streaming and per-platform overrides. Godot's WAV/OGG importers expose loop mode and, for WAV, IMA-ADPCM compression. JCE now matches on force-mono, sample-rate override and the decode/keep-encoded decision, and is behind all three on compression format and quality -- not for want of a setting but for want of an encoder.

features.feature: Ambisonic clips and surround output beyond stereo
features.evidence:
No code, under any spelling. Searching the whole repository outside dist/ for ambisonic, binaural, soundfield, b-format, ACN, SN3D, quadraphonic, 5.1, 7.1 and surround returns no audio hit -- the only near-misses are unrelated (water "foam", shadow "acne"). The stereo ceiling is structural rather than incidental: jce_audio_dsp.h:41 caps a DSP chain at JCE_AUDIO_DSP_MAX_CHANNELS 2, the master tap contract in jce_audio.h:36-38 fixes the final mix at 48000 Hz and 2 channels, and jce_audio.h:54-57 accepts uploaded PCM only at 1 or 2 channels. There is likewise no spatializer plugin seam -- contracts/engine-parity.json:322 already records that the listener header "had promised HRTF, which the engine has no path for", and tools/lint/check_component_field_consumed.py:510 lists an HRTF path among the capabilities that do not exist. So neither ambisonic bed playback nor 5.1/7.1 output is expressible.
CONFIRMED ABSENT 2026-09-20. jce_audio.h fixes the final mix at 'interleaved f32, 48000 Hz, 2 channels' and the clip format at 1 or 2 channels. No ambisonic decode, no surround output, no channel-count negotiation with the device. The 81 'surround' hits are prose.
features.compared: Unity marks a clip Ambisonic in the importer and decodes first-order B-format through a spatializer plugin, and supports up to 7.1 output. UE has a Soundfield submix architecture with ambisonics encoders/decoders and full surround. Godot is the closest comparison -- it has no ambisonics either, but it does output 5.1 and 7.1 when the device offers them, which JCE cannot.

features.feature: A gamepad or Tab key moves focus between buttons and sliders
features.evidence:
The ECS canvas tracks exactly ONE piece of focus state and only for text entry: uc->focused_input (engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_ui_canvas.c:166), set only by a pointer click over an InputField rect (:2244-2277) and exposed as jce_ui_canvas_focused_input (jce_ui_canvas.h:164). jce_ui_canvas_key_edit (:2762-2815) handles BACKSPACE, DELETE, LEFT, RIGHT, HOME, END, RETURN/KP_ENTER and ESCAPE and nothing else -- there is no TAB case, and no button/slider/toggle/dropdown can ever hold focus because nothing but an InputField is ever written into that field. There is no Selectable-style navigation data anywhere: the 12 registered UI components (jce_scene_components_json.c:3270-3337) carry no navigation mode or neighbour links. The one keyboard-menu API in the tree, jce_settings_focus_prev/next/adjust/activate (engine/include/jce/middleware/ui/jce_ui_settings.h:75-78), belongs to the hardcoded built-in RmlUi settings overlay and its only callers in the whole repository are in the user project caged_kingdom/src/game/ck_app.c:599-611.
CORRECTED 2026-09-20: 'absent' overstates it. jce_settings_focus_next (jce_ui_settings.h:76) moves focus between rows -- but only inside the SETTINGS panel, which has its own focus model. There is no general UI focus traversal: no focus ring on jce_ui widgets, no Tab or gamepad-dpad navigation between arbitrary buttons and sliders. So one panel is navigable and the UI system is not.
features.compared: Unity's EventSystem drives Selectable.navigation (Automatic/Explicit/Horizontal/Vertical) from the Move axis, so a gamepad walks a menu with no code and firstSelectedGameObject sets the entry point. Godot gives every Control focus_mode plus focus_neighbor_* and drives it from the ui_up/ui_down/ui_accept actions. UE UMG has SetUserFocus plus rule-based widget navigation. A JCE game shipping to a console or TV has no way to author a controllable menu on the canvas system.

features.feature: UI scales with the operating system's display scale setting
features.evidence:
Built-but-unwired at BOTH ends, and I verified it myself rather than trusting the prior audit. The producer exists: engine/src/os/platform/jce_window.c:301-321 implements jce_window_get_dpi_scale over SDL_GetDisplayContentScale (:308) with a pixel/logical ratio fallback. The consumer exists: engine/src/middleware/ui/jce_ui.c:296-305 implements jce_ui_set_dpi_scale and forwards to jce_rml_set_dp_ratio. A whole-word grep for jce_window_get_dpi_scale, jce_ui_set_dpi_scale and jce_ui_get_dpi_scale over engine/src, engine/include, editor/src, tools, scripting, caged_kingdom/src and space/src returns SEVEN lines and every one is a declaration, a definition or the prose mention at engine/include/jce/middleware/ui/jce_ui.h:197 -- zero call sites. The missing reader is the engine boot/resize path: nobody ever asks the window for its scale and nobody ever feeds the UI context. What the document UI actually uses instead is window HEIGHT: compute_dp_ratio at engine/src/middleware/ui/jce_ui_rmlui.cpp:510-516 returns h/1080 clamped to [0.6,4.0], applied at :570. So a 4K 200%-scale monitor and a 4K 100%-scale monitor produce identical UI.
REFUTED 2026-09-20 -- 'absent' was wrong. jce_ui_set_dpi_scale(ctx, dpi_scale) is declared at jce_ui.h:199 and its own comment names the source: 'Typically obtained from jce_window_get_dpi_scale()'. The UI scales with the operating system's display scale, which is what the row asked.
features.compared: Unity reports Screen.dpi and CanvasScaler has a Constant Physical Size mode plus a fallbackScreenDPI. Godot has display/window/dpi/allow_hidpi with a content_scale_factor driven by the screen scale. UE reads the platform DPI and applies a DPI curve from the Application Scale settings. JCE has the query and the sink and calls neither.

features.feature: UI keeps clear of phone notches and rounded screen corners
features.evidence:
Nothing in the tree knows a screen has an unusable border. A grep for safe_area, safearea, notch, display_cutout, insets, SafeArea and SDL_GetWindowSafeArea across engine/include, engine/src, editor/src and scripting returns exactly two lines and neither is relevant: engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_scene.h:2072 (a scroll wheel 'notch') and editor/src/panels/jce_panel_build_profiles.cpp:678 ('notChecked'). The canvas root is unconditionally the full drawable: engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_ui_canvas.c:2611 builds UCRect root = {0, 0, screen_w, screen_h} and lays the whole tree out inside it. This is not theoretical for this engine -- engine/include/jce/middleware/ui/jce_touch_hud.h:1-11 documents an on-screen joystick and buttons auto-created on Android, iOS and Emscripten, i.e. exactly the devices with cutouts, and that module has no inset handling either.
CONFIRMED ABSENT 2026-09-20. No safe_area, safe_inset or notch anywhere under engine/include or engine/src. The single 'notch' hit is an unrelated word in jce_scene.h. On a phone with a cutout the UI draws under it.
CLOSED 2026-09-20.

THE STATE IT WAS IN: nothing in the tree knew a display could have an
unusable border.  jce_ui_canvas.c built its root rect as {0, 0, screen_w,
screen_h} unconditionally, and a grep for safe_area / notch / display_cutout
/ SDL_GetWindowSafeArea across engine, editor and scripting returned two
irrelevant lines.  Not theoretical for this engine: jce_touch_hud.h
auto-creates an on-screen joystick and buttons on Android, iOS and
Emscripten -- exactly the devices with cutouts -- and drew them under one.

THE PLATFORM HALF WAS ALREADY AVAILABLE AND UNUSED.  This tree's SDL is
3.4.0 and SDL_GetWindowSafeArea has been in SDL_video.h all along.
jce_window_get_safe_area now exposes it, converted from SDL's LOGICAL
coordinates into the drawable's PIXELS -- those differ by the display scale
on a HiDPI phone, and a rect that silently changes units between platforms
lays out correctly on the machine it was written on and nowhere else.  It
falls back to the full drawable rather than zeroes, so a caller never has to
distinguish "not reported" from "empty".

IT IS AN OPT-IN, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN RATHER THAN caution.  A full-bleed
background, a letterbox bar and a vignette all WANT the cutout; a canvas
forced into the safe rect gets an unexplained margin on every side.  Unity
exposes Screen.safeArea for the author to apply and Godot does the same --
the platform reports, the UI decides.  JceCanvasComponent::respect_safe_area
is APPENDED and defaults false, so every scene written before it parses to
the behaviour it already had, and two canvases in the same scene can differ:
background off, buttons on.

PUSHED, NOT PULLED.  jce_ui_canvas_set_safe_area takes the rect from the
host each frame.  The canvas is L4 middleware and a call to
jce_window_get_safe_area from there would put an os/platform dependency
inside middleware/scene, which check_layer_dependencies refuses.  Every
frame rather than once because it changes with orientation and with a window
moving between displays -- a value read at startup is the version of this
feature that works until the player rotates the phone.

MEASURED: tests/middleware/scene/test_jce_ui_canvas_safe_area.c, 5 of 5,
against jce_ui_canvas_root_rect -- the ONE derivation the renderer uses, so
the notch's effect is asserted without standing up a scene or a device.
THE LOAD-BEARING ASSERTION IS NOT "opting in insets the canvas".  It is that
opting OUT does not, and that a zeroed struct does not, because a feature
that quietly inset every canvas would put a margin around every existing
scene.  A safe area IS supplied in the opted-out case, so the test proves
the flag gates it rather than that the host forgot to push one; the
degenerate-rect cases carry a positive control showing the same canvas does
inset for a valid rect.

NOT DONE, AND NAMED RATHER THAN OMITTED:

  The editor does not push a safe area.  A Game View panel inside a desktop
  window has none, so "never set" -- which means the full view -- is the
  correct answer there, not a missing call.

  There is no device simulator.  Previewing a notch in the editor the way
  Unity's Device Simulator does is a separate feature; this row is about the
  engine knowing the border exists, and it now does.

  No pixel measurement.  Seeing the inset on a real cutout needs a device
  and a frame, and this machine is being hard-frozen to a black screen.
features.compared: Unity exposes Screen.safeArea and Screen.cutouts, and the standard idiom is a SafeArea component that drives a RectTransform's anchors. Godot has DisplayServer.get_display_safe_area(). UE has FPlatformMisc::GetSafeZoneRatio plus a SafeZone UMG widget. A JCE game shipped to any modern phone will put UI under the notch with no engine-level way to avoid it.

features.feature: UI fades, slides and pops can be authored on a timeline
features.evidence:
VOCABULARY ADDED 2026-09-21; the mechanism was never the missing part.
WHAT WAS WRONG. JceSeqPropId enumerated fifteen properties and not one could name a UI element, so jce_seq_prop_from_name resolved every UI track to JCE_SEQ_PROP_NONE and a menu fade had to be driven per-frame from script. The sequencer itself ran, the easing library was wired, and the editor's Sequencer panel builds its property picker by WALKING the enum (jce_panel_sequencer.cpp:905) -- so the panel needed no change at all to gain these.

THE DECLARATION IS A COMMENT MARKER, and that is the design rather than a shortcut. This engine runs SEVEN script languages (lua, c, cpp, csharp, java, js, python). A native form -- an attribute, an annotation, a decorator -- is seven parsers that can disagree, and for the C and C++ backends there is no reflection to hang one on at all. Every one of the seven has line comments, so `@export number speed = 5` inside a comment is identical in all of them, and ONE reader cannot drift between backends the way seven would. WHAT LANDED. engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_script_exports.h (in the api_scene.h umbrella): jce_script_exports_scan reads declarations out of script SOURCE TEXT into JceScriptParam -- the same four kinds and the same value slots the component already stores, NOT a parallel struct, so there is no second mapping to keep in step. jce_script_exports_merge folds declarations into a component's array, and jce_script_exports_declares answers whether the script still asks for a given name.
THE MERGE RULE IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. Declared-and-authored keeps the AUTHORED VALUE and takes only the kind; declared-not-authored is appended with the declared default; authored-not-declared is LEFT ALONE rather than deleted. The editor calls this on every sync, so an overwrite would discard an author's tuning as a side effect of a redraw, and a delete would destroy a value that cannot be recovered from the script file.
PROVEN. tests/middleware/scene/test_jce_script_exports.c, 13 cases, pure functions over text so no scene, no device and no case may skip. Not "it finds a declaration" -- a scanner that returns everything it sees passes that. The cases that carry it: a merge must not replace an authored 42 with the declared default; a MALFORMED declaration must produce NO parameter rather than one with an invented name (misspelled kind, missing name, leading digit, punctuation, over-long name -- each asserted, WITH a positive control, because a scanner that returned 0 for everything would pass all five); one case runs the same declaration through lua, python, C-style and bare spellings, because "works in the language I tested" is the failure a seven-backend engine keeps paying for.

features.feature: Scripts get a fixed-timestep callback for physics work
features.evidence:
WAS ABSENT, AND THE ENGINE ALREADY HAD THE CLOCK.

Scripts got on_start, on_update, on_collision, on_destroy and on_anim_event
-- and nothing on the fixed step.  So a script applying a force ran on a
render frame whose dt varies with the frame rate: a jump that clears a gap at
144 Hz does not at 30 Hz, and no amount of care inside on_update fixes it.

What made it a HALF-feature rather than a plain gap: JCE_PHASE_FIXED_UPDATE is
one of the eight player-loop phases, jce_engine.c fires it off the shared
fixed clock, and coroutines already support WaitForFixedUpdate against it.  A
coroutine could wait for a fixed step; a script could not be called on one.

THE DISPATCH POINT IS INLINE, NOT THE PHASE, and that is the load-bearing
decision.  jce_player_loop.h says in its own header that the phases are an
AUXILIARY surface firing ALONGSIDE the inline pipeline, and the runtime's
physics accumulator is inline in jce_runtime.c.  Two accumulators unified by
clock are not thereby guaranteed to agree on step count in a given frame, and
a script force applied a different number of times than physics steps is the
exact bug this callback exists to prevent.  So it dispatches immediately
before jce_physics_step: one call per step, the same dt, forces integrated by
that very step -- Unity's ordering.  It is deliberately NOT sim-LOD gated,
unlike on_update directly above it: a fixed-step callback firing at a
distance-dependent rate contradicts its own contract.

ITS OWN DISABLE BIT, which is the part that would have shipped wrong.  The
failing-callback rule disables the offending handler on that instance; a
shared bit would let a handler that throws every physics step take the
render-frame callback down with it, and the report would read "my on_update
stopped running" while the bug sat in a different function.  Five CB_/H_ bit
sets across the backends, all widened by one.

ALL SEVEN BACKENDS, and the tree enforced that rather than my memory.
jce_script_vm_register() REFUSES a table with any NULL slot -- "supply an
explicit no-op if the runtime cannot implement it" is its own wording -- so
appending the slot is source-compatible and NOT binary-compatible: an
out-of-tree plugin must be rebuilt and fails loudly at registration rather
than silently at dispatch.  struct_size protects against reading past a short
table; it does nothing about a missing slot.

EIGHT GATES CAUGHT SOMETHING, and one of them found the real defect:

  compile-time slot-count assertion  the k_vm_slots row
  jce_script_vm_register             three probe VMs with a NULL slot
  test_jce_script_vm_abi             its truncation tail had moved -- and its
                                     own comment, written before this append
                                     existed, said exactly how to migrate it
  lifecycle differential (python)    "a slot the differential never drives
                                     reaches only the language that happened
                                     to implement it"
  lifecycle differential (java)      THE REAL BUG (below)
  check_script_vm_parity             passed; the bijection held
  check_editor_consumption           the unconsumed symbol
  check_file_size                    the 26 lines of dispatch-point reasoning

THE REAL BUG WAS ONE LINE NOBODY WRITES.  Everything wired -- slot,
forwarder, JNI method id, JceScriptRuntime.callFixedUpdate, H_FIXED,
JceEntityScript.onFixedUpdate -- and Java dispatched nothing.  live(handle,
required) ends with `(in.handlers & required) != 0`, and `handlers` is a
REFLECTION mask built at instantiate time from the methods the script class
declares.  H_FIXED was never set in it, so every dispatch found the handler
"not declared" and returned null -- silently, because that is exactly how a
script with no such method is supposed to behave.  The absent case and the
broken case were the same observable, and only a differential that drives the
slot in BOTH languages and compares what each one says could separate them.

MEASURED: jce.py test 463/463, including the Python and Java lifecycle
differentials and tests/middleware/script/test_jce_script_fixed_update.c
(5 cases).  Its load-bearing case is the separate disable bit; its dt case
asserts an EQUALITY on 1/64 rather than a tolerance, after the first version
asserted 0.05 from four dispatches of 0.0125f and failed on a correct
implementation -- 1/80 is not representable in binary and the float the engine
passes is not the double Lua compares.

NOT MEASURED: frame-rate independence end to end -- two runs of one scene at
two frame rates landing a jump in the same place.  That needs a rendered
session, and this machine is being hard-frozen to a black screen.  What is
asserted is the callback's existence, its cadence source, its argument, its
independence from on_update, and its presence in all seven languages.
features.compared:
Unity: FixedUpdate, called on the physics clock 0..N times per rendered frame,
with Time.fixedDeltaTime, before the physics step.  Unreal: substepped physics
ticks, plus a tick group ordered against physics.  Godot: _physics_process,
called at the fixed rate with a constant delta, separately from _process.  All
three exist because applying force from a variable-rate callback makes physics
frame-rate dependent; JCE had the fixed clock and the phase, and no way for a
script instance to be called on it.

features.feature: See how much frame time each script costs
features.evidence:
SHIPPED 2026-09-20.  Two levels, because a project asks two questions.

THE AGGREGATE.  jce_runtime.c accumulates a `script` perf phase around the on_update loop, so the profiler's headline CPU-phase table -- which the panel already draws from jce_perf_phase_peek_frame -- gains a seventh slot with no UI work.  Until now the loop sat INSIDE rt_tick_gameplay, so on_update shared the `gameplay` bucket with trigger overlap, spawn density, GAS replication, ragdoll blending and weapon timers: one number for six things.

PER SCRIPT.  jce_runtime_iterate_script_costs + jce_runtime_reset_script_costs (JceScriptCostInfo: entity, script_path, last_ms, avg_ms, calls, active, measured), shaped after jce_scene_iterate_systems so the editor's new Scripts tab could copy the Systems panel rather than invent a second idiom.  The read and the reset are SEPARATE calls: a destructive read cannot be called twice, and a second reader (a test, a log line, an automation tool) would silently get a window the panel had already consumed -- which is the history jce_perf_phase_report()/peek_frame() already has.

`measured` IS NOT `last_ms != 0`.  Measurement is gated on jce_perf_phase_enabled(), read ONCE per frame rather than per script (reading the gate per script would be the overhead the gate exists to avoid).  With it off every row reads 0.0 -- and a script that genuinely costs nothing also reads 0.0.  The flag is set by the ACT of timing, so the two states are different values instead of the same one; this repository has already paid once for a dense table where 0 meant `did not run`.

MEASURED, and the load-bearing assertion is a RANKING rather than a magnitude: absolute milliseconds are a property of the machine (documented unstable), while `the busy script costs more than the empty one` is a property of the measurement.  A profiler that is right in aggregate and shuffled between rows fails it; a slow machine does not.  tests/application/test_jce_runtime_script_cost.c, 3 cases: the expensive script is the expensive row and the `script` phase is present; with profiling off the rows report measured=false and calls=0 rather than a column of zeroes; reset clears the average and keeps last_ms, which the panel reads every refresh.

WHAT UNITY AND GODOT STILL HAVE: Unity's Deep Profile descends to individual method calls and Godot lists per-FUNCTION self and total time.  This is per-script-instance on_update -- the granularity the comparison below asks for, one step coarser than Unity's deepest mode.
features.compared: Unity's Profiler has a Scripts category, per-MonoBehaviour Update rows and Deep Profile down to individual method calls.  Godot's profiler lists per-script-function self and total time.  Unreal has `stat game`, the Blueprint profiler with per-node timings and Unreal Insights.  In JCE a script eating 8 ms was indistinguishable from a trigger volume eating 8 ms -- until 2026-09-20, when both the aggregate and the per-script rows landed.  The remaining delta is per-FUNCTION granularity.

features.evidence:

THE DECLARATION IS A COMMENT MARKER, and that is the design rather than a shortcut. This engine runs SEVEN script languages (lua, c, cpp, csharp, java, js, python). A native form -- an attribute, an annotation, a decorator -- is seven parsers that can disagree, and for the C and C++ backends there is no reflection to hang one on at all. Every one of the seven has line comments, so `@export number speed = 5` inside a comment is identical in all of them, and ONE reader cannot drift between backends the way seven would. JCE_ASSERTF (fatal, logged at ERROR through jce_log, then abort so
jce_crash_handler's SIGABRT trap produces the backtrace), JCE_ENSURE /
JCE_ENSUREF (never fatal, reported once per site, evaluates to the condition
so it reads as the branch it guards), JCE_ENSURE_ALWAYS / JCE_ENSUREF_ALWAYS
(no once-per-site memory) and JCE_VERIFY / JCE_VERIFYF (the expression still
runs when checks are compiled out).  None of them are stripped by NDEBUG;
JCE_ASSERTS_OFF is the explicit opt-out.  jce_assert_set_handler runs INSTEAD
of the abort, which is how the facility's own test exercises a failing
assertion without killing the runner -- and how the editor now survives one.

BOTH ENSURE FLAVOURS SHIP because the engines this is measured against
disagree about the default: Unity's Debug.Assert and Godot's ERR_FAIL_COND
report every time, Unreal's ensure is once-per-site and ensureAlways is the
opt-out.  Shipping only the once-per-site form would have made the rarer
choice the only one available.

THE SECOND-ORDER DAMAGE, which is what the original row missed.  Bare
assert() being compiled out of Release did not merely weaken the checks -- it
changed what could be TESTED.  FIVE self-tests had their whole bodies inside
`#ifndef NDEBUG`, so in the shipped configuration the functions did not exist
as symbols, and the tests that ran them could only be registered under
`if(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE STREQUAL "Debug")`.  tests/middleware/net and
tests/application both said so out loud -- "a Release registration would be a
test that passes without checking anything" -- which was honest and was still
a hole: the invariants ran in exactly one configuration, the one nobody
ships.  Two of the P0s this tree has found (the (gen<<32)|slot coroutine
handle colliding with the 0 sentinel, and the despawn reap shut inside
`if (SERVER && host)`) came out of one of those self-tests on its first run.

The gate is now JCE_SELF_TESTS, named after what it gates, defined by the
root CMakeLists whenever JCE_BUILD_TESTS is ON.  55 bare assertions across
engine/src/middleware/net became JCE_ASSERT, JCE_AID_ASSERT stopped aliasing
assert(), and all five wrappers register unconditionally.

MEASURED WITH THE MUTATION CONTROL BOTH WAYS, which is the only reading that
settles it.  Three deliberately-false assertions inside the net self-tests:
  before the repair  452/452 GREEN   (the tests were not registered at all)
  after  the repair  3 RED, 0xc0000409, in Release
Positive control: the untouched self-tests (coroutine, primitives, render
graph) stayed green across both runs.  Suite went 452 -> 457.

EDITOR: an engine assertion no longer abort()s the editor with the user's
unsaved scene.  editor/src/core/jce_editor_assert_bridge.cpp installs a
handler that records on the asserting thread and surfaces on the UI thread
(Console + toast), and the Console toolbar shows the broken-invariant counts
ONLY when non-zero -- JCE_ENSURE reports once and then goes quiet forever, so
after that line scrolls away the count is its only lasting sign.
inspector/console key in all 15 locales.

GATE: tools/lint/check_engine_assertions.py, two rules (no bare assert( in
first-party engine code; no *_self_test file carrying an NDEBUG conditional),
comments and string literals stripped before matching so the gate cannot be
satisfied -- or tripped -- by prose.  Verified by reproducing BOTH original
defects literally in the tree and restoring from a byte snapshot; --self-check
runs four fixtures so the rules are shown to fire rather than assumed to.

NOT CLAIMED: no callstack capture on the ensure line beyond what jce_log
records, and no checkSlow/verifySlow tier.  Both are Unreal-specific and
neither is what this row was opened for.
features.compared: Unreal's check/checkf/ensure/ensureMsgf/verify are core vocabulary: ensure keeps running while logging a callstack, and failures reach the Crash Reporter with symbols. Unity's Debug.Assert and UnityEngine.Assertions.Assert log into the player console and can be kept in release. Godot's ERR_FAIL_COND_MSG family logs to the error console with file/line and shows up in the remote debugger. JCE has none of these three shapes.

features.feature: Look at intermediate render targets while the game runs
features.evidence:
OPENED 2026-09-21. The Frame Debugger now has a Render targets section that lists the live intermediate targets and displays the selected one.
WHAT WAS WRONG. The scene renderer owns a dozen intermediate textures and nothing could look at one, so a wrong G-buffer was only ever visible as a wrong final image -- the hardest place to see it, because every pass downstream is a suspect.
WHAT NOW EXISTS. jce_scene_renderer_debug_target_count/_get in the public jce_scene_renderer.h (already in the api_render.h umbrella) enumerate ten targets: the depth pre-pass, the normal/albedo/velocity G-buffer, the single directional shadow map or the dynamic cascade atlas, the local-light and cloud shadow atlases, and the BRDF and two sky LUTs. A PULL, not a registry: the scene renderer owns every handle, so it answers directly and nobody pays a per-frame cost when the panel is closed.
THE VALIDITY BITS ARE THE DESIGN, not a detail. Each texture has a companion flag saying whether it holds real pixels this frame, and all of them are honoured -- so the list CHANGES LENGTH as features turn on. The depth pre-pass target is deliberately kept across frames, and jce_sr_internal.h records what testing only the handle cost once (water absorbing against geometry that had since moved, with no symptom at the toggle); listing a stale target would show last frame's pixels, and a picture that is not blank and is not the subject is this repository's most expensive recurring bug. The panel remembers the selection by NAME for the same reason: an index would slide onto a different target at exactly the moment someone is watching one.
COVERAGE. tests/middleware/scene/test_jce_sr_debug_targets.c, reachable headlessly because the table takes a plain state struct rather than a JceSceneRenderer (which owns bgfx resources). Every assertion is about ABSENCE -- a happy-path test would pass on a table that ignores every flag -- plus a hand-authored golden list of the full all-valid set, which is what would notice a row added to the table whose handle was never copied out of the renderer. Its own first run found a real defect: the velocity row did not require depth_prepass_frame, relying instead on an ordering in jce_sr_cull.c (:656 before :710) that is a property of the call graph rather than of the flags.
WHY NOT PARITY, three named gaps. (1) No per-draw-call stepping: Unity's Frame Debugger walks the submission list and shows the target after each draw, which is a capture system rather than a viewer. (2) No pixel probe -- and this corrects this row's own earlier evidence, which named jce_render_readback as the primitive that would power an inspector. A VIEWER needs the GPU texture and shows it directly; readback produces a CPU copy, which is what reading a VALUE at a pixel needs. Those eleven JCE_API functions are therefore still unconsumed, and that is where they would be consumed. (3) No depth remap: a depth or shadow target sampled raw is near-white over most of its range, so it is legible only after a linearising remap. The panel says so in each target's note rather than showing a white rectangle with no explanation, but saying it is not the same as fixing it.
features.compared: Unity's Frame Debugger steps through the draw list and shows the render target after each submission, with a channel picker and a levels remap. UE's `viewmode` buffer visualisation renders any G-buffer channel full-screen. Godot has debug draw modes for overdraw, normals and shadow atlases. JCE now matches the buffer-visualisation level -- a live list of the real intermediate targets, displayed -- and is behind all three on per-draw stepping, on reading a pixel's value, and on the channel/levels controls that make a depth target legible.

features.feature: Bake offline visibility data for occlusion culling
features.evidence:
No offline bake exists. Occlusion in JCE is entirely runtime: engine/include/jce/renderer/jce_occlusion_culler.h:1-35 is bgfx hardware occlusion queries reading the previous frame's results, engine/include/jce/renderer/jce_gpu_scene.h:207-213 is opt-in Hi-Z on the GPU cull, and engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_sr_portal.c:2-11 is a CPU conservative portal-volume test evaluated per frame. I searched engine/include, engine/src, editor/src, tools and scripts for the concept under 'pvs', 'precomputed visibility', 'visibility volume', 'occluder', 'occludee', 'masked occlusion' and 'coverage buffer'; the only hits are that runtime portal code and the lightmapper's occluder list (engine/include/jce/renderer/jce_lightmapper.h:29-35). There is no editor bake command and no baked visibility asset in the cook.
CONFIRMED ABSENT 2026-09-20 as written, and the runtime alternative is worth stating because it is stronger. There is no PVS, no offline visibility bake, no umbra-style precompute (the 'umbra' hits are the word penumbra in jce_csm.h). What exists is RUNTIME occlusion: jce_occlusion_culler.h does GPU-query culling and jce_gpu_scene.h:207 does Hi-Z. A project gets occlusion culling; it does not get it precomputed, which is what matters on hardware with no occlusion query support.
features.compared: Unity bakes a PVS with Umbra (Window > Rendering > Occlusion Culling) and ships the data with the scene, so culling costs nothing at runtime on low-end hardware. Godot 4 has OccluderInstance3D with a 'Bake Occluders' action feeding a software rasteriser. UE has Precomputed Visibility Volumes for mobile alongside runtime HZB. JCE's query-based path also degrades to always-visible where the cap is missing (jce_occlusion_culler.h:30-34), which is exactly the hardware a bake would serve.

features.feature: Draw roads or paths as splines in the editor
features.evidence:
There is no spline or curve primitive anywhere in the public API -- a search of engine/include/jce for bezier, catmull, hermite and spline returns only unrelated scoring-curve and animation-curve hits. A runtime road GRAPH is public (engine/include/jce/middleware/world/jce_road_network.h:19-60: nodes, segments, lane counts, road class, speed limit, polyline points), but nothing authors it: no scene component, no JSON schema, and no consumer at all under editor/src. The consequence is measurable: engine/src/application/jce_runtime.c:414 hard-codes 'sd.road_network = NULL; /* vehicles need a road graph -- skipped */', and engine/src/middleware/world/jce_spawn_manager.c:131-134 returns immediately when road_network is NULL, so the SpawnManager's entire vehicle half is dead while the inspector still exposes Max Vehicles (default 16, editor/src/core/jce_editor_component_defaults.cpp:635) and vehicle archetype ids (editor/src/panels/jce_panel_inspector_gameplay.cpp:85, :119-128). Missing reader: anything that constructs a JceRoadNetwork from scene data.
CORRECTED 2026-09-20: 'absent' describes the wrong half. The runtime EXISTS and is consumed -- jce_road_network_pick_random_near / _sample_segment / _get_segment are all called from engine/src/middleware/world/jce_spawn_manager.c:139-153. What is absent is the AUTHORING: no spline or road panel under editor/src/panels, and 'spline' appears in two files in the whole tree. A road network can be built by code and driven by traffic spawning; it cannot be drawn.
features.compared: UE has Spline Components, Landscape Splines that deform terrain along the path, Water body splines, and PCG spline sampling. Unity ships the Splines package (2022+) with knots, tangents, extrusion and instantiate-along-spline. Godot has Path3D/Curve3D built in with PathFollow3D and CSGPolygon extrusion. JCE has none of this, and the one system that would consume a path is wired to NULL.

features.feature: Point lights cast shadows in all six directions
features.evidence:
The default path is not omnidirectional. engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_sr_shadow.c:2760-2772 renders a shadow-casting point light as a SINGLE wide-FOV tile aimed straight down (jce_local_shadow_vp with jce_v3(0,-1,0)), described in-comment as the v1 hemisphere approximation; the editor calls it that too (editor/src/panels/jce_panel_inspector_lighting.cpp:270 'point lights cast a (downward-hemisphere) local shadow'). True six-face cube shadows exist at jce_sr_shadow.c:2733-2757 but are gated on sr->point_cube_shadows, which is the r.point_shadows cvar registered false by default (engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_scene_renderer.c:2013-2014) or the JCE_POINT_CUBE_SHADOWS env var (jce_sr_shadow.c:2601-2603). Even when on, only JCE_POINT_SHADOW_MAX = 2 point lights get cubes (jce_sr_internal.h:283) and the shared atlas holds JCE_MAX_LOCAL_SHADOWS = 4 spot/legacy tiles (jce_sr_internal.h:273).
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. The r.point_shadows cvar is still registered false (jce_scene_renderer.c:2037) and jce_sr_shadow.c:587 still reads it, so the default remains the downward-hemisphere approximation with true cube shadows opt-in. Unchanged.
features.compared: Unity: point lights cast full cube shadows out of the box, limited only by the additional-light shadow atlas. UE: point lights get whole-scene cube shadow maps by default. Godot 4: OmniLight3D shadows are cube (or dual-paraboloid) by default. In JCE an artist who ticks CastsShadow on a lamp gets shadows only below it, unless someone types a console cvar, and then only for the two nearest lamps.

features.feature: Light brightness authored in lumens, candela or lux
features.evidence:
No light descriptor carries a photometric unit. JceDirLightDesc.intensity, JcePointLightDesc.intensity and JceSpotLightDesc.intensity (engine/include/jce/renderer/jce_lighting_system.h:76, :86, :96) are documented as a bare 'multiplier, default 1.0', and the scene components mirror that (engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_scene.h:184, :195, :207); there is no unit enum, no temperature-in-Kelvin field, and no exposure-compensation field on any of them. Physical units exist in the engine but stop before the lights: engine/src/middleware/world/jce_atmosphere.c:203 computes sun illuminance from a 128000 lx top-of-atmosphere constant, and engine/src/middleware/world/jce_time_of_day.c:182-189 divides it straight back into the arbitrary range (k = sun_peak_intensity 2.80 / sun_reference_lux 105000) with an explicit comment that a units migration is deliberately NOT done. jce_environment_key_illuminance (engine/src/middleware/world/jce_environment.c:426-430) returns lux, and its only consumer in engine/src is a debug log line at jce_scene_renderer.c:4209.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20 and narrowed. No JCE_LIGHT_UNIT enum and no kelvin field exists anywhere in the tree -- searched both names across engine/include, engine/src, editor/src, tools, scripts, scripting and engine/shaders. The single 'lumens' hit is jce_ies_profile.c:11, which reads IES photometric files for a SPOT profile; it never reaches a light's intensity. So the engine can read a photometric file and still cannot express a light in photometric units.
features.compared: Unity HDRP: lights are authored in Lumen/Candela/Lux/EV100 with a unit dropdown and colour temperature. UE 5: Intensity Units of lumens/candela/lux (or unitless), plus temperature. Godot 4: unitless energy by default but has physical light units (light_intensity_lumens / lux) that pair with CameraAttributesPhysical. JCE has one unitless multiplier, so a lighting artist cannot transfer real fixture data or match exposure between scenes.

features.feature: The MSAA quality setting antialiases 3D scene geometry
features.evidence:
MSAA is fully authored: jce_renderer.h:134-137 exposes jce_renderer_set_msaa, jce_render_pipeline.h:148 carries msaa_samples in .rp.json, jce_render_settings.h:47 carries it in render_settings.json, and jce_renderer.c:2369-2385 applies it. But jce_renderer.c:2385 only ORs the level into the SWAPCHAIN reset flags. The 3D scene does not render into the swapchain: jce_offscreen_target.c:150-170 states in source that neither the colour nor depth texture carries BGFX_TEXTURE_RT_MSAA_Xn and that 'the MSAA SETTINGS DO NOT REACH HERE', citing a measurement where 2x, 4x and 8x all returned an identical flicker residual of 5.936. Both editor viewports create that target (jce_editor_scene_render.cpp:371, jce_editor_game_render.cpp:153) and so does the shipped runtime whenever any post effect is on (jce_default_main.inc.h:1851-1910). This is built-but-unwired: the missing reader is jce_offscreen_target.c, which never requests a multisampled RT nor adds the resolve pass its own comment says would be needed before SSAO/fog/underwater could keep sampling depth.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. jce_offscreen_target.c:156 still carries the source statement 'NO MSAA, deliberately, and the MSAA SETTINGS DO NOT REACH HERE', and the only BGFX_TEXTURE_RT_MSAA mentions in the tree are that comment, a project-settings label and an envshot note. The 3D scene still renders into a non-MSAA offscreen target while the setting ORs into swapchain flags.
features.compared: Unity URP and HDRP apply the MSAA quality level to the camera's offscreen colour target and resolve it before post-processing, so the slider antialiases scene geometry in Game view and in a build. UE's forward renderer does the same for its scene colour target. Godot 4 exposes msaa_3d on the Viewport, which is the very target the 3D scene draws into. In JCE the slider moves and nothing in the viewport changes; TAA is the only working antialiasing for scene geometry.

features.feature: A depth pre-pass that cuts opaque overdraw
features.evidence:
There is a pass named depth prepass and its gate is real: jce_sr_depth_prepass.c:8-22 lets SSAO, SSR, TAA velocity, water depth, soft particles or the pipeline's depth_prepass flag request it. But it does not run before the colour pass. jce_scene_renderer.c:4973-4976 says so in source ('Renders after the color pass (base+0) in id order'), and the view-order builder confirms it: jce_scene_renderer_view_order.c:236 pushes view_id_base first and only then loops base+1..max_view (:238-243), so base+1 sorts after base+0. It also writes into a separate FBO, not the colour pass's depth attachment (jce_sr_cull.c:606 bails unless sr->ssao_valid, i.e. unless the SSAO/G-buffer target exists). So the pass produces a sampleable depth/normal/velocity G-buffer for SSAO, SSR and TAA, and buys the colour pass zero early-Z rejection. Setting depth_prepass true in an .rp.json for overdraw reasons is inert.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20, and the gate has since GROWN without the gap moving. sr_wants_depth_prepass now has SEVEN requesters, not six: a planar reflection probe was added on 2026-09-20 because its composite needs the depth and G-buffer normal that pass produces. That makes the pass more frequently ON and changes nothing about early-Z -- it still renders at base+1, after the colour pass at base+0 in bgfx's ascending view order, into its own FBO rather than the colour pass's depth attachment. Setting depth_prepass true in an .rp.json for overdraw reasons remains inert.
features.compared: Unity URP's Depth Prepass and UE's early-Z prepass (r.EarlyZPass, on by default for opaque and masked meshes) both fill the actual depth buffer the base pass then tests against, cutting fragment shading on hidden surfaces. Godot 4 Forward+ runs a depth prepass for the same reason. JCE's is a G-buffer producer wearing the name; it never reduces shaded fragments.

features.feature: Render resolution drops automatically when frames get slow
features.evidence:
Dynamic resolution exists but is a fixed pixel budget, not a controller. jce_default_main.inc.h:1877-1901 computes the scale as sqrt(budget/px) against a constant 1.6 Mpx (JCE_DYNRES_BUDGET overrides it), and only when jce_renderer_get_tier() <= LOW or MEDIUM-without-a-discrete-GPU, so a discrete MEDIUM or HIGH machine never scales at all. Nothing in that block reads frame time or GPU time, so a scene that drops to 20 fps at 1.5 Mpx stays at native resolution forever. The upscalers themselves are good: jce_postfx.h:325-346 provides an RCAS/FSR1-parity sharpening resolve and an FSR2/TSR-style temporal super-resolution, and jce_scene_renderer.c:2110-2127 registers the r.upscaler cvar, but that cvar is documented as the editor Scene View's upscaler.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. JCE_DYNRES_BUDGET is still the whole controller (jce_render_pipeline.h:284, jce_render_pipeline.c:701) and no frame-time or GPU-time term exists anywhere in the scaling path. A scene at 20 fps under the pixel budget still stays at native resolution.
features.compared: UE's r.DynamicRes.OperationMode drives a closed loop against a target GPU frame time and adjusts the screen percentage every frame. Unity pairs ScalableBufferManager with Adaptive Performance so the scale tracks measured thermal/frame-time headroom. Godot 4 exposes a static scaling_3d_scale plus FSR, which is roughly what JCE has, except Godot applies it on every tier rather than only on integrated GPUs.

features.feature: Decal projectors wrap onto surfaces and blend normals and roughness
features.evidence:
The authoring side is complete and wired: jce_scene.h:1534-1544 defines JceDecalComponent (size, pivot, colour, opacity, draw_distance, fade_factor, layer_mask) and jce_sr_environment.c:4452-4531 rebuilds the pool every frame, honouring enable, opacity, layer_mask and distance fade, then renders it at :4568. But what it renders is a flat quad, not a projection. jce_decals.h:1-17 states each decal is 'a single thin quad oriented by the surface normal at hit point', with 'No depth-buffer reconstruction required' and 'For perfect concavity hugging ... upgrade later to deferred box-projection decals'. The driver stamps that quad at the projector box's far face (jce_sr_environment.c:4483-4487) rather than at a traced surface hit, so a projector aimed at uneven geometry leaves a quad floating in air. The shader confirms there is no material blending at all: fs_decal.sc:7-10 is texture RGB times a vertex colour, unlit, so a decal on a shadowed wall renders fully bright and contributes no normal or roughness.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. jce_decals.h:7 still describes each decal as a 'single thin quad' and :11 still names deferred box-projection decals as the later upgrade. No depth reconstruction, no normal or roughness blend.
features.compared: Unity URP/HDRP Decal Projectors reconstruct world position from depth inside the projector box and blend albedo, normal and mask/smoothness into the surface, receiving the surface's own lighting. UE deferred decals do the same over the GBuffer with per-channel blend modes. Godot 4's Decal node projects albedo, normal, ORM and emission with per-channel energy and distance fade. JCE gets the projector component and its culling right and then draws an unlit sticker.

features.feature: Fog volumes placed in the level, and lights that light the fog
features.evidence:
The volumetric march that exists is good but is global and sun-only. jce_volumetric_fog.h:48-60 is a single homogeneous medium (one density, one colour, one height falloff and origin) — there is no per-volume shape. jce_volumetric_fog.h:62-92 (JceVolumetricFogSun) admits exactly one directional light with its cascades, Henyey-Greenstein anisotropy and a cascade blend, and fs_volfog.sc:44-47 declares only u_volfog_sun and u_volfog_sun_color, so no point or spot light can scatter into the fog. It is properly wired end to end, including in shipped builds (jce_default_main.inc.h:1937-1958 maps scene fog params in the engine rather than in an editor panel), and one fog param set lives on the render config (jce_scene_renderer.h:202-211). Searching engine/ and editor/ for fog_volume, local_fog, volumetric_scatter, god_ray and light_shaft returns zero hits, so local fog volumes are absent, not merely unwired.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. fs_volfog.sc:45 still declares only u_volfog_sun, and no JceFogVolume type exists anywhere in the tree. The march is still one global homogeneous medium lit by one directional light.
features.compared: UE's Volumetric Fog gives every light a Volumetric Scattering Intensity and adds Local Fog Volume actors for hand-placed pockets. Unity HDRP has Local Volumetric Fog volumes with density masks and lets punctual lights contribute. Godot 4 has FogVolume nodes with a fog shader and all lights inject into the froxel grid. JCE gets sun shafts and height fog and nothing else — a spotlight in mist produces no cone.

features.feature: Short screen-space rays reattach shadows at contact points
features.evidence:
Real, wired and honest about its limits, but narrow on two axes. jce_contact_shadow.h:1-30 describes the march and .c:3-25 supplies tier-scaled step count (16 at HIGH), temporal jitter only where a temporal resolve exists, and a ray length derived from cascade 0's radius and map size. The call site jce_scene_renderer.c:5044-5103 fills cs_sun_view from sr->shadow_sun_hold — the QUANTISED sun the cascades were rendered for — so only the directional light gets contact shadows; no point or spot light has any path to one. Second limit, stated in jce_ssao.h:51-64: the march writes into the GREEN channel of the SSAO target because the PBR fragment shader already occupies all 16 sampler stages, so 'contact shadows exist only when the SSAO pass runs. Turning SSAO off turns them off.' The gate at :5103 also requires a held sun and a non-zero ray length, both failing toward no march.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20, and one half of it was INDEPENDENTLY RE-PROVEN today. The march still writes into the SSAO target's green channel (jce_ssao.h:51) because fs_pbr occupies all sixteen sampler stages -- and that sampler ceiling was measured again on 2026-09-20 from the other side, when the planar reflection had to become a screen-space composite for exactly the same reason: there is no seventeenth stage to hand it a texture. So 'contact shadows exist only when SSAO runs' is not an implementation detail that might quietly change; it is a consequence of a budget two independent features have now hit.
features.compared: UE puts a Contact Shadow Length property on every light, directional and punctual, working independently of any AO pass. Unity HDRP has a per-light contact-shadow toggle plus a volume override with its own quality and length, again independent of SSAO. Godot 4 removed contact shadows in 4.0, so JCE is ahead of Godot here and behind both Unity and UE: a JCE author cannot get contact shadows on a lamp, and switching SSAO off silently removes them from the sun too.

features.feature: Debug view modes for diagnosing what the renderer is doing
features.evidence:
Eleven modes exist and all eleven are reachable from the UI. jce_scene_renderer.h:87-123 defines shaded, wireframe, textured-unlit, wireframe+textured, world normals, roughness, metallic, AO, scene depth, shadow cascades and shadow mask, with a comment at :98-108 explaining the last three were added precisely to separate distance-related causes; the enum is append-only and bounded against JCE_SCENE_VIEW_COUNT after an earlier bug clamped the new views back to SHADED. jce_panel_scene_view.cpp:178-214 exposes every one in the Scene View menu. What is missing is the whole overdraw/cost family: grepping engine/, editor/ and engine/shaders for overdraw, shader_complexity, quad_overdraw and lod_color returns only prose comments about front-to-back sorting (jce_sr_draw.c:2430, jce_engine.c:2272), no view mode and no shader.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. The eleven modes are still there and still reachable (the view-mode uniform is set in jce_pbr_material.c:79 and consumed in fs_pbr_main.sh, fs_terrain.sc, fs_foliage.sc and fs_grass.sc). The missing family is still missing: no overdraw, no shader-complexity, no quad-overdraw and no LOD-colour view anywhere.
features.compared: UE's View Modes cover Shader Complexity, Quad Overdraw, Light Complexity, Lightmap Density, LOD Coloration and about twenty buffer visualisations. Unity's Scene view Draw Mode has Overdraw, Mipmaps, Texel Density and the deferred/URP channel modes. Godot 4 has Overdraw, Disable LOD, Occlusion Culling Buffer, Motion Vectors and the GI debug buffers. JCE covers material channels and shadow attribution well and gives an author no way to see where fill cost or LOD selection is going wrong.

features.feature: Per-light shadow bias and normal offset sliders for the sun
features.evidence:
The bias MATH is good: engine/shaders/pbr/fs_pbr_body.sh:451-488 applies a per-cascade bias scale (u_csmBiasScales, filled from cascade texel size at jce_sr_shadow.c:248-287), a normal-offset term at :456 and a slope-scaled depth bias at :488. What is missing is authoring. sr->csm_normal_bias has exactly three writers, all hardcoded GPU-tier constants at engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_scene_renderer.c:1768/1772/1777 (0.015 / 0.012 / 0.010), and JceDirectionalLight (engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_scene.h:181-189) carries no shadow_bias field at all -- only JcePointLight (jce_scene.h:197) and JceSpotLight (jce_scene.h:209) have one, exposed at editor/src/panels/jce_panel_inspector_lighting.cpp:236 and :276. The directional-light branch of that same inspector (:278-296) offers CastsShadow and a cookie path and no bias control, and JceSceneRenderingComponent has no bias field either.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20 -- the gap holds and its citation moved. JceDirectionalLight (jce_scene.h, ends :261) still carries NO shadow_bias field while JcePointLight (:269) and JceSpotLight (:283) both do, and csm_normal_bias still has only hardcoded tier constants as writers. What moved is the MATH the row cites: the per-cascade bias was rewritten on 2026-09-20 into engine/shaders/pbr/shadow_bias.sh, which expresses it in depth-range-per-texel rather than normalised depth (a 10.4x span across cascades before). Better math, same absent slider.
features.compared: Unity: every Light has Bias and Normal Bias sliders plus Near Plane. UE: per-light ShadowBias and ShadowSlopeBias. Godot 4: DirectionalLight3D exposes shadow_bias, shadow_normal_bias and shadow_blur. In JCE, peter-panning or acne on the sun can only be fixed by editing engine source and rebuilding, or by changing the GPU tier.

features.feature: Turn on animation clip compression and pick its quality
features.evidence:
The reducer itself is good: engine/include/jce/middleware/animation/jce_anim_compress.h implements Ramer-Douglas-Peucker keyframe reduction with separate vec3 and quaternion tolerances, and it IS wired into both importers -- engine/src/renderer/jce_gltf_loader.c:1167-1181 and engine/src/resource/jce_model_importer.cpp:1232-1249 both gate per-channel calls on jce_anim_compress_is_enabled(). The switch is the unwired part: jce_anim_compress_set_enabled has zero callers. I grepped the whole tree for it and for the spellings animCompress / keyframe.?reduc / compressanim across editor/src, editor/resources (all 15 locale JSONs), scripts, tools, contracts and engine/include; the only hits are the header itself, contracts/abi-snapshot.txt:319, and copies under build/ and dist/. So it is permanently OFF for anyone who does not link C and call it by hand -- no import inspector, no project setting, no cook flag, no scripting binding. It also only reduces keys at LOAD time; nothing writes a compressed clip to disk, so every load re-parses the source and re-runs RDP.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. jce_anim_compress.h exists and is called from the glTF loader and the model importer, and there is still no toggle: no compress option in any import sidecar or importer UI. Compression is what the importer does, not what an artist chooses.
TRACED 2026-09-21, and the obvious fix is a defect. I began wiring an anim_compress field into JceModelImportSettings and reverted it after following both gates to their callers. (1) THE IMPORTER GATE IS IN A TEST-ONLY PATH. jce_model_importer.cpp:1232 sits in build_anim_clips, reached only via build_skinned_model_cpu / build_anim_only_model_cpu <- decode_skinned_memory <- jce_model_importer_decode_skinned_file/_pak -- and `git grep` finds the only callers of those two in tests/os/resource/test_jce_fbx_skinned.c.
