No product path reaches it. (2) THE ONLY PRODUCT-REACHABLE GATE IS THE RUNTIME ONE. jce_gltf_loader.c's gate is inside extract_animations, reached from jce_gltf_load <- jce_model_load_gltf <- jce_runtime.c:663, which is the SHIPPED RUNTIME loading a model out of the PAK. So a process-global "compression is on" -- which is the only switch the current API offers -- would run RDP on every animation channel of every model load in a packaged game: CPU in the hot load path, and repeated lossy reduction of data already reduced. That is strictly worse than the feature being off. (3) THE REAL IMPORT STEP EXISTS AND HAS NO GATE. Models deliberately pass through jce_asset_cooker unchanged (its default branch says so at length, and records that this was mis-chased once already as a missing MESH branch); the offline model step is `jce_cook --convert-model` -> jce_bundle_mesh_convert.cpp, which normalises on .glb and contains no compress call at all. SO THE ROW CANNOT BE CLOSED BY ADDING A SETTING. It needs the reducer moved to the offline converter, where a lossy transform is run once and written to disk, and the runtime gate retired -- which is also what fixes the "every load re-runs RDP" note above. Sized as a unit of its own rather than a toggle.
features.compared: Unity exposes Anim. Compression (Off/Keyframe Reduction/Optimal) plus rotation/position/scale error fields per clip in the Model import inspector and bakes the result into the imported asset. UE ships an automatic compression pipeline with ACL bit-packed quantized codecs, per-sequence overrides, and on-disk savings measured in multiples. Godot has per-animation import compression stored in the scene file. JCE has the algorithm and neither the authoring surface nor the on-disk bake.

features.feature: Play one clip on differently-proportioned character rigs
features.evidence:
This one is genuinely wired end to end, just narrow. engine/src/middleware/animation/jce_anim_retarget.h documents a bind-pose-relative transfer R_dst_local = R_dst_bind * conj(R_src_bind) * R_src_anim with root translation scaled by the bind-pose height ratio. The runtime path is sr_anim_try_retarget (engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_sr_anim.c:2112-2208), invoked from the main animator update at :2449; the map is cached per instance and rebuilt when either skeleton changes (:2144-2153). The authoring field is JceSkeletalAnimator.retarget_source_skeleton, serialised as "retargetSource" (engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_scene_components_anim.c:33-35, 371-374) and edited at editor/src/panels/jce_panel_inspector_animation.cpp:48-56. Two real limits: correspondence is BY BONE NAME ONLY (jce_anim_retarget_map_create looks each dst joint's name up in src), and the header states at :24-28 that it is deliberately NOT on the public <jce/api_animation.h> surface, so a game can only reach retargeting through that one scene string.
REFUTED 2026-09-20 -- BOTH stated limits are now false, and neither was noticed when they stopped being true.

'Correspondence is BY BONE NAME ONLY': the engine now has a second, ROLE-based path. jce_humanoid.h defines 22 humanoid bone roles, jce_humanoid_map_build auto-detects them from joint names across three rigging conventions (Unreal, Blender, Khronos), and jce_humanoid_retarget_clamped transfers pose by ROLE with muscle-space clamping, twist redistribution, effector preservation and hinge-direction clamping for knees and elbows. It is driven every frame from engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_sr_anim_retarget.c:204.

'Deliberately NOT on the public <jce/api_animation.h> surface': jce_humanoid.h is included at api_animation.h:31. A game reaches role-based retargeting from C without touching a scene string.

The name-based jce_anim_retarget.h path this row describes still exists and is still name-only; it is no longer the only one. See animation.humanoid-rig, which measures the role-based path and closed to parity on 2026-09-20.
features.compared: Unity's Humanoid avatar retargets through a normalised muscle space, so rigs with different bone names and hierarchies interoperate, with a per-bone Avatar Configuration editor to fix bad mappings. UE's IK Retargeter maps named chains, retargets with FK+IK passes, and has a preview/edit window. Godot 4 uses BoneMap plus SkeletonProfile with an explicit remap UI. JCE has no name-mismatch remapping UI, no muscle space, no IK correction pass, and no public API.

features.feature: Physics material friction/bounce combine modes affect contacts
features.evidence:
Built-but-unwired. jce_physics_material.h:29-42 declares AVERAGE/MIN/MAX/MULTIPLY plus friction_combine and restitution_combine; jce_physics_material.c:81-100 implements the Unity precedence rule; the editor viewer lets an author pick both (editor/src/viewers/jce_fv_physmat.cpp:177-197); the loader/saver round-trips them (jce_physics_material.c:137-140, 158-161). The only path from an asset into the simulation is jce_physics_body_set_material (engine/src/middleware/physics/jce_physics.c:799-812, called from engine/src/application/jce_rt_physics.c:61-69 for the authored physmat_path), and it forwards ONLY dynamic_friction + restitution to Bullet, dropping static_friction and both combine modes — its own comment concedes Bullet then runs its fixed multiply/max combine. jce_physics_material_combine() has no caller anywhere in engine/src, editor/src, scripting or tools. The missing reader is a contact-time combine in the body-material application path.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20 at the source line. jce_physics_body_set_material still carries its own admission: 'v1: feed dynamic_friction + restitution directly to Bullet, which runs its own per-contact combine. Static friction is recorded in the asset for future use'. The authored AVERAGE/MIN/MAX/MULTIPLY never reaches a contact.
CLOSED 2026-09-21. jce_physics_material_combine() has a caller now, and it is the contact itself. A combine is a function of the PAIR, so it cannot be pre-baked into per-body values -- it has to run at contact time, and Bullet routes every added contact through ONE global pointer, gContactAddedCallback. THAT HOOK EXISTED AND WAS ARMED IN THE WRONG PLACE: inside jce_bullet_body_create_heightfield, guarded by `smooth_internal_edges`, so a world with no smooth heightfield had no contact callback at all. A combine written into it and left there would have reached nothing in most scenes and worked perfectly in the terrain scene anyone would have tested it in. It is installed at world create now. THE MODES RIDE ON THE BODY: the callback is a free function with no world pointer and Bullet offers no object->world mapping, and a file-scope world pointer would be a new global. It is not needed -- Bullet already stores friction and restitution per body, so the only missing state is two 2-bit modes, packed into btCollisionObject::setUserIndex2 (unused in this tree). Stored +1 so ZERO means "no material was ever applied", distinct from AVERAGE which is a real authored choice; CF_CUSTOM_MATERIAL_CALLBACK is set only on bodies that carry one, so nothing else pays per contact. EXTRACTED RATHER THAN --raise: check_file_size reported jce_physics_bullet.cpp "newly a god file" at 3103 lines. jce_physics_bullet_contact.cpp now holds the hook, the chaining, the encoding and both riders (internal-edge smoothing, and this combine), and the old file is 2994. The boundary was already documented next door: jce_physics_bullet_con_query.cpp exists for the same gate twice and its header records that the better cut is the one that keeps a mechanism's installation with what it does -- which is exactly what the heightfield-armed hook was violating. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, NAMED: a body carrying a material now uses the authored rule, so a DEFAULT material means AVERAGE where it used to mean Bullet's multiply. A body with no material is untouched. Both halves are asserted. tests/middleware/physics/test_jce_physmat_combine.c, 4 cases, headless: the rule pinned against jce_physics_material_combine itself rather than a hardcoded number; THE MODE REACHING THE SOLVER (same push, same friction values, only the mode differs -- MIN(0.2,0.8)=0.2 against MAX=0.8 cannot slide the same distance unless it arrived); no-material unchanged; and a default material being AVERAGE rather than MULTIPLY. MUTATION-CONTROLLED BEFORE THE COMMIT, not after: dropping the modes in jce_bullet_body_set_material -- the pre-change behaviour exactly -- fails precisely the two behavioural cases, each with the message that describes the reverted state, while the pure-rule case and the no-material control still pass. The negative control also failed on its FIRST run and was wrong about the code: the no-material arm applied no material, so neither body received the test's friction values at all (JceBodyDesc.friction defaults to 0.5), comparing 0.5*0.5 against 0.2*0.8. Two variables moved and the pre-written message accused the engine. Friction now goes on the body desc in both arms.
features.compared: Unity's PhysicsMaterial has frictionCombine/bounceCombine with exactly this precedence and PhysX honours them per contact pair. UE physical materials have a Friction Combine Mode / Restitution Combine Mode that Chaos applies. Godot 3D has no combine mode at all (bounce/friction are per-body), so JCE matches Godot but is behind Unity/UE despite shipping the whole authoring surface.

features.feature: Ragdoll bones have per-joint swing and twist limits
features.evidence:
The ragdoll itself is wired end-to-end — jce_runtime.c:632-668 builds one per authored component, drives it pre-step and publishes the pose post-step (jce_runtime.c:2018-2081), and blend_weight is re-read from the component every tick (jce_runtime.c:2787-2797) so a death trigger can collapse it. But every joint it creates is the same unlimited ball joint: jce_ragdoll.c:228-245 sets type GENERIC6DOF with lower_limit == upper_limit == 0 and the in-code comment states 'angular axes are left free (Bullet's default 6DOF angular limits)'. The authoring component (jce_scene.h:2430-2436, JceRagdollComponent) carries only enable, blend_weight, radius and height_scale — no per-bone limits, mass, shape choice or collision layer. So elbows and knees hyperextend and heads rotate freely.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. jce_ragdoll.c still builds every joint as GENERIC6DOF with lower_limit and upper_limit both 0.0f and the comment still says 'angular axes are left free (Bullet's default 6DOF angular limits)'. Every ragdoll joint is an unlimited ball joint; an elbow can still fold backwards.
CLOSED 2026-09-22. Ragdoll joints are bounded per bone, and NOTHING NEW WAS INVENTED -- all three pieces already existed with no reader for this purpose. jce_humanoid_bone_from_joint_name maps a joint's NAME to a humanoid role. jce_humanoid_muscle_limits gives that role a twist range and a swing cone -- literally "per-joint swing and twist limits", this row's own words, sitting in the animation layer and read only by the retarget clamp. And jce_physics_configurable_joint_create already takes per-axis angular limits. The ragdoll built an unlimited GENERIC6DOF while all of that sat one call away.
AUTHORED: JceRagdollComponent.joint_limit_scale, with an inspector control and i18n in all 15 locales, round-tripping as "jointLimitScale". 0 means the engine default of 1.0 -- the same convention radius and height_scale in that component already use, and a DELIBERATE departure from "a zeroed field means what the engine did before", because what it did before was the defect. Preserving it would have left the fix off for everyone who already has a ragdoll. A NEGATIVE value is the explicit opt-out, expressible precisely because a scale cannot otherwise be negative.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, and the engine had already written the reason down: a single symmetric cone per axis, not a swing/twist split. jce_humanoid.h states it where the muscle limits are declared -- "a cone cannot say 'a knee bends forward and not back': that needs a hinge AXIS, and a hinge axis is not derivable from a rest pose where the leg is straight". The bodies are built at bind world transforms and the constraint frames follow them, so which local axis runs down the bone differs per rig. The cone is max(swing, |twist|), the LOOSER of the two, never tighter than the muscle table permits on any axis. It does not stop a knee bending the wrong way; it does stop every joint rotating without bound, which is what "heads rotate freely" meant. Claiming the split without the axis would be the more precise-sounding lie.
A bone whose name matches no humanoid role stays unlimited whatever the scale says: a tail, a cape bone or a prop is not a limb and has no muscle range to borrow.
PROVEN, and the test took three wrong answers to get right -- recorded because each was a different way for an instrument to be wrong. It first read 178.8 degrees against a 90-degree bound and looked completely unwired. (1) The limit VALUE: capped below Bullet's +-pi/2 Euler boundary, no change. (2) The MEASUREMENT: it read each body's WORLD rotation, but a joint limit constrains the RELATIVE rotation, and a free-floating chain tumbles as one rigid unit -- both bodies reach ~180 degrees while the joint never moves. Fixed; still 179. (3) The PUSH. Torque 4.0 on a 0.05 m capsule is enormous for that inertia, and an iterative solver under a torque far past what the joint can resist blows through any limit. At 0.05 it reads 101.7 degrees against the 90-degree bound, against an unlimited control at 180.
WHAT SEPARATED THEM WAS WRITING THE TEST THE UNDERLYING FEATURE NEVER HAD. tests/middleware/physics/test_jce_configurable_joint.c exercised LIMITED on LINEAR axes only: ang_motion appeared solely as LOCKED and angular_limit_deg solely as 0.0, in a feature whose header advertises per-axis Locked/Limited/Free on both kinds of axis. The angular case is now there -- FREE twin 179.5 degrees, LIMITED twin 34.0 against a 20-degree limit, under an identical sustained torque. The feature was fine; the instrument was over-driving it, and no test existed that could have said so.
tests/middleware/animation/test_jce_ragdoll_joint_limits.c, 3 cases. "The chain stays connected" is NOT one of them -- that was already true and is exactly what the old unlimited ball delivered. The bound compared against is read from jce_humanoid_muscle_limits rather than written as a literal, so re-tuning that table cannot leave the assertion checking a number nobody uses.
WHAT IS STILL DIFFERENT FROM UNITY AND UE: neither the hinge DIRECTION (a knee that bends one way only) nor per-bone mass, shape choice or collision layer is authored. Unity's ragdoll wizard writes CharacterJoints with a configured axis; UE authors a PhysicsAsset per body. Both need a configuration step this engine does not have -- and jce_humanoid.h says so about its own limits rather than letting a reader assume otherwise, which is why this row can close on "bounded per bone" without pretending to more.
features.compared: Unity's ragdoll wizard generates CharacterJoints with swing1/swing2/twist limits and a configured axis; UE authors per-body constraints in a PhysicsAsset. JCE takes each bone's angular range from its humanoid role (jce_humanoid_muscle_limits) and applies it as a symmetric cone per axis, scaled by an authored joint_limit_scale. The remaining difference is the hinge DIRECTION -- neither engine's asymmetric "bends forward, not back" is expressible without the configured axis this engine lacks -- plus per-bone mass, shape and collision layer, which are still uniform.

features.feature: Soft bodies and cloth collide with the scene's real colliders
features.evidence:
engine/src/middleware/physics/jce_cloth.cpp:5-16 states the soft simulation runs in a SEPARATE secondary btSoftRigidDynamicsWorld so the rigid world is untouched, and that rigid-vs-cloth response is one-way (cloth feels the rigid pose, the rigid body is unaffected). The only geometry a soft body can touch is a hand-mirrored static proxy: jce_softbody_add_static_box (jce_softbody.h:90-94, jce_cloth.cpp:473-499), and the runtime mirrors ONLY box colliders on non-dynamic entities (engine/src/application/jce_rt_physics.c:955-984 — it early-returns for a DYNAMIC rigidbody and returns unless jce_scene_get_box_collider succeeds). Sphere, capsule, convex-hull, mesh and terrain colliders, and every dynamic body, simply do not exist for the soft world; the code comment at jce_rt_physics.c:993 calls terrain trimesh mirroring a follow-up.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. jce_cloth.cpp still states the soft simulation runs in a secondary btSoftRigidDynamicsWorld and that rigid-vs-cloth is one-way, and jce_softbody_add_static_box is still the only geometry a soft body can touch. Cloth cannot collide with a mesh collider, a capsule, or anything dynamic.
INCREMENT 2026-09-21, STILL BEHIND. jce_softbody_add_static_sphere and _add_static_capsule join the box, and rt_softbody_mirror_static now mirrors all three primitives, each gated on its own enable flag. Shape coverage now MATCHES Unity Cloth, which collides against Sphere and Capsule colliders only. STATUS UNCHANGED because the row's basis is that "in all three a cloth or soft body drapes over the actual level geometry": convex-hull, mesh and terrain colliders are still invisible to the soft world, and so is every DYNAMIC body -- the soft simulation runs in a separate btSoftRigidDynamicsWorld and rigid-vs-soft is one-way by construction. Godot's SoftBody3D collides with the same physics world as everything else; that is the gap, and three primitives do not close it. THE WIRING SHIPPED UNREACHABLE FOR ONE RUN AND A MUTATION FOUND IT. rt_softbody_mirror_static opened with `if (!jce_scene_has_box_collider) return;` so the sphere and capsule branches could never execute -- built-but-unwired, produced fresh while closing a built-but-unwired row. The API-level test could not see it (it calls jce_softbody_add_static_* directly); a mutation removing the runtime branches SURVIVED, which is what prompted tests/application/test_jce_runtime_softbody_colliders.c, which counts what the runtime actually mirrors and failed on its first run. A second mutation (capsule forced onto the X axis) also survived, because the only capsule case asked for axis 0 -- the mutation was a no-op against its own rig. Both are red now. ALSO RECORDED because it cost more than the feature: the first rig dropped the soft ball on the APEX of a 2 m sphere, an unstable equilibrium it rolls off, landing low -- numerically identical to falling through. The positive control was a BOX at the same place, which passed because a box has a flat top and cannot fail the way a sphere does. Control and subject differed in two variables, so a passing control "proved" the shape was at fault; a tessellated convex hull was written and failed too before the rig was re-examined. With the proxies at radius 20 (locally flat) all three pass and the engine was right the whole time. NEXT INCREMENT: mesh/terrain mirroring, which jce_rt_physics.c already names as a follow-up, and which is the one that would let cloth drape over level geometry rather than over the primitives an author remembered to place.
features.compared: Unity Cloth collides against assigned Sphere/Capsule colliders on the character and Godot's SoftBody3D collides with the same physics world as everything else (collision_mask over all layers, static and rigid alike). UE Chaos Cloth collides against skeletal-mesh physics assets and, in newer versions, environment collision. In all three a cloth or soft body drapes over the actual level geometry; in JCE it can only rest on an axis-aligned box that a static entity happened to author.

features.feature: Cloth simulated on a character's skinned garment mesh
features.evidence:
JceClothDesc (engine/include/jce/middleware/physics/jce_cloth.h:40-62) is defined purely as a regular grid patch: four corners, res_u/res_v, mass, kLST/kAST/damping, iterations and a pinned-index list. Line 42 of the same header says outright '(Mesh-from-asset variant is a documented follow-up.)'. The whole pipeline is grid-shaped downstream too: the component is authored, simulated on spawn (engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_scene.c:3243-3281) and rendered in-game by rebuilding a transient grid mesh from the solver nodes (engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_sr_environment.c:3706-3775, which returns early unless res_u >= 2 && res_v >= 2 and node_count == res_u*res_v). So flags and banners work, but a cape, skirt or coat authored on a skinned mesh has no route in.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. jce_cloth.h:42 still says '(Mesh-from-asset variant is a documented follow-up.)' and JceClothDesc is still a res_u x res_v grid patch. Cloth on a character's coat is not expressible.
features.compared: Unity's Cloth component sits on a SkinnedMeshRenderer and simulates its actual mesh with painted per-vertex max-distance constraints. UE Chaos Cloth is painted onto skeletal-mesh sections in the Clothing tool. Godot's SoftBody3D takes any MeshInstance3D mesh and pins vertices by group. JCE's cloth is at roughly the level of a standalone flag primitive.

features.feature: 2D collision layer matrix decides which 2D layers collide
features.evidence: SHIPPED 2026-09-21. The 32x32 2D grid in Project Settings was editable, persisted and written into builds, and reached NOTHING. Measured before: jce_physics2d.c contained ZERO uses of b2Filter / categoryBits / maskBits, JceBody2DDesc had no layer field, JceRigidBody2DComponent had no physics_layer, jce_editor_play.cpp forwarded only gravity2d out of JceProjectPhysics2D, and jce_build_manager.cpp:595 wrote the 3D matrix into the build with no 2D counterpart. An author set "Player does not collide with Pickups", saved it, shipped it, and every 2D pair still collided -- with no error, looking like level design rather than a bug. GAP, NOT DECISION: the 3D sibling has been wired since P3-C.2 and no comment anywhere claims the 2D side was deliberate. (Contrast editor.assets.thumbnail-previews, also zero-caller, where the source AT THE CALL SITE says "disabled by user request" -- a no-caller finding has to be read at the call site before it is called debt.) WHAT NOW EXISTS. jce_physics_layers gains a SECOND matrix beside the 3D one, sharing the 32 layer names: jce_physics2d_set_layer_collides / _get_layer_collides / _get_layer_collision_mask. Separate matrices because JceProjectSettings already authors both and the physics debugger draws both grids -- one shared matrix would delete a distinction the authoring surface already exposes, which is Unity's split too. JceBody2DDesc and JceRigidBody2DComponent each gain physics_layer (APPENDED; 0 = Default, so every existing scene keeps its behaviour), the runtime passes it at spawn, and jce_physics2d.c resolves it to b2ShapeDef.filter in one place (layer_filter). b2DefaultShapeDef() gives categoryBits=1, maskBits=UINT32_MAX -- so an UNFILTERED 2D world is behaviourally identical to a fully-permissive matrix, which is exactly why the authored grid changing nothing was invisible. THE SHIP PATH IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS: "matrix2d" is an additive key in jce.physlayers.v1 (schema unbumped -- an added optional key cannot break an existing file, and an old reader ignores it), and jce_build_manager now CALLS jce_project_settings_push_physics_layers instead of inlining a second copy of that loop. Without both, the grid would work in Editor Play -- which pushes straight into the cache -- and revert to all-collide in every packaged build. TESTED, six cases, three of which exist because something went wrong while writing it: colliding layers still stop a falling box (the control, without which every negative assertion is green for the wrong reason); non-colliding layers let it through; a shape added AFTER creation inherits the body's layer; the 2D and 3D matrices are independent in BOTH directions; a document with matrix2d restores it; a document WITHOUT matrix2d stays PERMISSIVE rather than zeroing -- absent is not empty, and zeroing on absence would drop every 2D body through the world on the first load of an older project. The third case is the one the gates could not have found: the first draft recorded slot_layer only inside a setter that had NO CALLER, so jce_physics2d_body_add_box always read 0, landed on Default and collided with everything -- this unit's own defect rebuilt on the two-step construction path. That setter is deleted; a public symbol with no consumer is the thing this unit is about.
features.compared: Unity's Physics 2D settings carry their own Layer Collision Matrix that Box2D honours through category/mask bits, and Physics2D.Raycast takes a layerMask. Godot 2D bodies have collision_layer/collision_mask and every 2D query takes a collision_mask. In JCE two 2D bodies on nominally non-colliding layers still collide, and jce_physics2d_raycast (jce_physics2d.h:150-152) takes no filter argument at all, so a 2D game cannot exclude anything from a ray.

features.feature: Character controller is carried by moving platforms
features.evidence:
The character is a mass-10 dynamic capsule with rotation locked and, critically, m_friction = 0 (engine/src/middleware/physics/jce_physics_bullet.cpp:2030-2046 — the comment says horizontal motion is velocity-driven). jce_bullet_character_move (same file, :2168-2237) recomputes the horizontal velocity absolutely each call: it accelerates v.x/v.z toward the commanded target at f->accel and calls setLinearVelocity, with no term for the surface it is standing on. The ground probe stores only a normal and booleans — JceBulletCharFeel (engine/src/middleware/physics/jce_physics_bullet_internal.hpp:111-125) has fields for accel, air_control, step_height, max_slope_cos, filter group/mask, grounded/touching/jumping and ground_normal, but no ground-body handle or platform velocity. Frictionless plus velocity-overwritten means a character on a moving kinematic platform is neither dragged by friction nor given the platform's velocity; it slides off.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. No platform or ground-velocity term exists anywhere in jce_physics_bullet.cpp. The character's horizontal velocity is still recomputed absolutely each call with no contribution from the surface under it, so a moving platform slides out from under the player.
CLOSED 2026-09-21 (9fe279c1). The ground probe now keeps the body whose normal wins its 5-ray fan, and jce_bullet_character_move adds that surface's velocity AT THE CONTACT POINT to the commanded velocity, so walk_dir == 0 converges on the platform's own motion. getVelocityInLocalPoint rather than getLinearVelocity, because a platform spinning about its own centre has zero linear velocity and still carries a rider; gated on GROUNDED rather than on touching anything, because a face too steep to walk on supports no locomotion and must impart none. NOT conserved on leaving -- the term goes to zero when the feet lift and the capsule decays toward the bare walk command at accel*air_control, which is UE's bImpartBaseVelocity switched off, asserted rather than assumed so the behaviour and its comment cannot drift apart. tests/middleware/physics/test_jce_character_platform.c, five cases: the platform's derived velocity is asserted BEFORE anything about the character (it is computed by Bullet's saveKinematicState, not by this code); a STATIC platform must carry nothing, which is the only case separating a ride from a drift; a spinning platform; leaving; and a 60-degree face carrying nothing. Four mutations, all red: carry removed; getLinearVelocity; platform_vel never cleared; and gating on any hit instead of on grounded -- that last one SURVIVED the first four cases, which is why the steep-face case exists. The controller moved to engine/src/middleware/physics/jce_physics_bullet_char.cpp in the same commit: the carry took jce_physics_bullet.cpp to 3,056 lines and check_file_size called it newly a god file.
features.compared: UE's CharacterMovementComponent tracks a movement base and imparts base velocity and rotation (UpdateBasedMovement, bImpartBaseVelocity*). Godot's CharacterBody3D applies platform velocity automatically via platform_on_leave / get_platform_velocity. Unity's CharacterController also does not do this by itself, but its capsule has real friction and OnControllerColliderHit exposes the hit collider, so the usual script workaround is available; in JCE the frictionless capsule and the absent ground-body reference remove even that.

features.feature: Distinct continuous-collision modes behave differently
features.evidence:
Wired but weaker than advertised. jce_physics.h:428-433 offers four modes (DISCRETE, CONTINUOUS, CONTINUOUS_DYNAMIC, CONTINUOUS_SPECULATIVE) and they do reach the simulation from authoring — jce_rt_physics.c:1563-1572 applies rb->ccd_mode, threshold and swept radius at spawn for non-static bodies. But jce_physics_body_set_ccd_mode (engine/src/middleware/physics/jce_physics.c:879-892) branches only on DISCRETE vs not-DISCRETE; every continuous mode calls jce_bullet_body_set_ccd with the same JCE_CCD_DEFAULT_MOTION_THRESHOLD and auto-derived sphere radius, which becomes one setCcdMotionThreshold/setCcdSweptSphereRadius pair (jce_physics_bullet.cpp:1538-1556). The chosen enum survives only in a 1024-entry process-static side table so the getter round-trips through save/load (jce_physics.c:825-877). Four authored modes, two real behaviours — the header admits the aliasing at :416-426.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20 at the branch. jce_physics_body_set_ccd_mode still reads 'if (mode == JCE_CCD_DISCRETE) { ... } else { ... }' -- one branch for all three continuous modes. CONTINUOUS, CONTINUOUS_DYNAMIC and CONTINUOUS_SPECULATIVE are bit-identical in effect, so three quarters of the authored enum is decoration.
features.compared: Unity's four CollisionDetectionMode values are genuinely different in PhysX: Continuous sweeps against static only, Continuous Dynamic also sweeps against other continuous bodies, and Continuous Speculative uses cheap speculative contacts and is the recommended default because it also works on kinematic and rotating bodies. UE distinguishes CCD from the separate speculative-contact path. A JCE author who picks Speculative expecting the cheap mode silently gets full swept CCD cost, and one who picks Continuous Dynamic expecting dynamic-vs-dynamic sweeps does not get it.

features.feature: 3D joints break when their torque limit is exceeded
features.evidence: SHIPPED 2026-09-21, and the root cause was NOT the missing query. break_torque was authored (jce_panel_inspector_physics.cpp:576), parsed and serialised (jce_scene_components_physics.c:357), copied into the runtime's ConfigJointEntry -- and read by nothing. Adding a per-axis feedback query was necessary and did not fix it: the reading stayed a flat 0.0000 N*m while the joint was holding an authored 50 N*m. WHY: jce_bullet_constraint_create called enableFeedback(true) AND setJointFeedback(...); jce_bullet_configurable_joint_create called only enableFeedback(true). enableFeedback makes Bullet accumulate m_appliedImpulse -- ONE combined scalar, which is exactly why break_FORCE worked on that path for its whole life -- but the SEPARABLE force and torque are written only if the constraint owns a btJointFeedback, and without setJointFeedback that storage is NULL. The query returned at `if (!fb) return 0.0f` and never reached the arithmetic. Half a feature, wired to the neighbouring creator, on the only joint type that HAS a break_torque. REPAIRED so the omission is unrepresentable rather than merely fixed: both creators now end at a shared con_register() that does enableFeedback, storage install, addConstraint and registry together, and there is exactly one addConstraint left in jce_physics_bullet.cpp. SECOND DEFECT, independent and also real: Bullet's single-body ctor is btGeneric6DofSpringConstraint(btRigidBody& rbB, ...) -- the body you pass becomes side B and side A is the shared static getFixedBody(). So for every WORLD-ANCHORED joint (connected_body == 0, which is most authored joints) m_appliedTorqueBodyA describes the immovable world. The query reads both sides and takes the magnitude, which is one answer to one question regardless of which ctor built the joint. THE THRESHOLDS ARE INDEPENDENT BY CONSTRUCTION: rt_cfg_joint_breaks tests break_force and break_torque under separate guards, so an unset break_force cannot silently disable break_torque. That regression is invisible at the scene defaults (the parser defaults BOTH to 1e30, so a nested version still enters), which is why the breaking test case writes breakForce:0 explicitly -- the 0 is the assertion, not decoration. UNITS ARE MEASURED, NOT REMEMBERED: this Conan package ships Bullet headers only, so whether the solver divides by the timestep before storing is not readable here, and guessing wrong is a 60x error whose symptom is indistinguishable from the original defect. tests/application/test_jce_joint_break_torque.c reads the raw value under a known applied torque and brackets it at [0.25x, 4x], which separates torque from angular-impulse with room to spare. EVIDENCE IS A NUMBER MOVING, NOT A GREEN SUITE: two of the original five cases passed VACUOUSLY while the reading was zero -- "a torque under the threshold does not break it" is trivially true when nothing can ever break. Two two-body cases were added because they are the ones that would have PASSED all along: the two-body ctor puts the user's body on side A, so a suite containing only those would have gone green over a break_torque that never fires in the common configuration.
features.compared: Unity's Joint.breakForce and breakTorque are both enforced and fire OnJointBreak. UE constraints have separate Linear Breakable (force) and Angular Breakable (torque) thresholds, both enforced by Chaos. Godot has no built-in breakable joints at all. So JCE's force half is at Unity/UE parity and ahead of Godot, but the torque half is a field that shows in the inspector, saves to disk and does nothing.

features.feature: Moving sources pitch-shift as they pass the listener
features.evidence:
Built-but-unwired. The Doppler plumbing is complete and reachable: jce_audio.h:293 declares jce_audio_set_doppler_factor, jce_audio.c:2074-2082 pushes it onto every live ma_sound, and jce_rt_audio.c:499-501 feeds it from the AudioListener component's doppler_factor every frame. But Doppler needs velocities and nothing ever supplies one. jce_rt_audio.c:454-476 memsets the JceAudioListener and then writes only position/forward/up, leaving listener velocity {0,0,0}; and jce_audio_voice_set_velocity (declared jce_audio.h:314, implemented jce_audio.c:2103-2110) has no caller anywhere in engine/, editor/ or scripting/ -- a repo-wide search outside dist/ returns only the header, the implementation and contracts/abi-snapshot.txt:664. With both velocities pinned at zero, miniaudio's Doppler ratio is 1.0 no matter what the factor is set to. The missing reader is a per-frame velocity feed (transform delta or rigidbody velocity) into jce_audio_voice_set_velocity and JceAudioListener.velocity.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. No listener velocity is ever written in jce_rt_audio.c, and jce_audio_voice_set_velocity has no caller outside jce_audio.c's own definition. The Doppler factor is authored, pushed to every live ma_sound every frame, and multiplies a velocity that is always zero.
CLOSED 2026-09-20.  The feature was complete except for the one number it
multiplies.

WHAT WAS ALREADY THERE: jce_audio.h:293 declares jce_audio_set_doppler_factor,
jce_audio.c pushes it onto every live ma_sound every frame, and jce_rt_audio.c
feeds it from the AudioListener component's doppler_factor.  What was missing
is that miniaudio's Doppler ratio is computed from RELATIVE VELOCITY, and both
velocities were zero: jce_audio_voice_set_velocity (public since the feature
landed) had no caller anywhere in engine/, editor/ or scripting/, and the
listener's own velocity was left at {0,0,0} by the memset in jce_rt_audio.c.
So the authored factor was read, pushed and multiplied by zero -- a knob that
moved and changed nothing, which is the shape a user reports as "Doppler does
not work" and a developer cannot find, because every line of it is present.

WIRED: the scene carries positions, not velocities, so the runtime
differentiates.  rt_audio_velocity() in jce_rt_audio.c is the ONE derivation,
used for the listener and for every spatial voice; VoiceEntry and JceRuntime
each gained a last_pos plus a has_last_pos flag.

THREE REFUSALS, and they are the feature rather than defensive padding:

  no previous position -> zero.  Without it the FIRST frame of every sound
      differentiates against an implicit origin: a source 100 m out at 60 fps
      reads as 6000 m/s, so every sound pitch-bends the moment it starts.

  faster than sound -> zero.  A scene load, a camera cut, a respawn.  The
      Doppler model divides by (c - v), so past c it does not exaggerate, it
      INVERTS.  A cut is not motion and must not be heard as any.

  dt <= 0 -> zero.  A paused frame hands miniaudio an infinity otherwise.

AND A RECYCLED VOICE SLOT STARTS WITH NO PREVIOUS POSITION.  Slots are reused
as voices end and every other field at that site is assigned, so the missing
assignment would have been silent: a new sound would differentiate against
wherever the previous occupant stood.  Three metres apart at 60 fps is 180
m/s -- UNDER the teleport clamp, so that guard would not have caught it.  It
would simply be a wrong pitch on the frame a sound starts, in a scene where
sounds start constantly.

MEASURED: tests/application/test_jce_audio_doppler_velocity.c, 5 of 5.  It
LINKS rt_audio_velocity rather than recomputing the formula -- a test that
derives the answer a second way asserts against its own arithmetic, and this
tree has paid for that (a hinge axis disagreed with its own clamp by 22
degrees).  The teleport case carries its own positive control: 300 m/s, fast
but subsonic, must still come back as 300, because a clamp that swallowed
that would be a mute button on exactly the sounds Doppler exists for.

NOT MEASURED AND NOT CLAIMED: that a moving source is audibly pitch-shifted.
That needs a real audio device and a listener, and this machine's audiodg.exe
crashed five times today.  The claim here stops at "both ends of the Doppler
pair now receive a correct velocity every frame, and the three cases where
there is no honest velocity return zero".
features.compared: Unity computes Doppler automatically from AudioSource and AudioListener transform deltas each frame and exposes a per-source dopplerLevel (0-5). UE derives Doppler from the audio component's owner velocity and offers a Doppler attenuation setting with a scale. Godot's AudioStreamPlayer3D has doppler_tracking (idle-step or physics-step) that samples the node's own motion. In all three a moving siren audibly shifts pitch with no extra code; in JCE it cannot.

features.feature: Music automatically ducks under dialogue via sidechain
features.evidence:
Built-but-unwired, and the last hop is precisely identifiable. jce_audio_mixer.h:141-206 defines a full sidechain: JceAudioDuckParams (key bus, threshold, ratio, attack, release, floor), set/clear/get, an envelope advanced by jce_audio_mixer_duck_advance(m, frames, key_peak_fn, user), and resolve_volume_ducked(). The editor authors it, jce_audio_mixer_config.h:12-22 parses the "sidechain" JSON block, and jce_rt_audio.c:193-208 rt_apply_mixer does push jce_audio_mixer_resolve_volume_ducked() onto each device bus every frame -- so the consumer side is correct. What never happens is duck_advance: its only caller in the repository is tests/middleware/audio/test_jce_audio_routing.c:167,176,189,214,234,301, and that test feeds a synthetic key level (synth_key_peak), not the real mix. Worse, there is no way to supply a real one: grepping engine/include/jce/middleware/audio/ for peak/rms/level finds no bus-level meter in the public API at all. So duck_gain stays 1.0 for the entire life of any Play session or shipped game. The missing reader is a per-block key-bus peak feed from the live audio device into duck_advance.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20, and the missing hop is exactly where the row said. jce_audio_mixer_duck_advance exists at jce_audio_mixer.c:520 and has NO caller anywhere in engine/src -- so the envelope that resolve_volume_ducked reads is never advanced. The consumer side is correct and the producer never runs.

SHARPENED 2026-09-20 while trying to close it: the missing hop is NOT a forgotten call. jce_audio_mixer_duck_advance(m, frames, key_peak, user) needs a per-bus PEAK LEVEL, and jce_audio.h has no level, peak or rms reader for a bus at all -- so there is nothing to pass as key_peak. Closing this needs a per-bus meter (a tap node in the miniaudio graph), which is a small subsystem rather than a wire. The envelope, the curve, the JSON, the editor and the consumer side are all already correct and waiting on that one input.
TRACED 2026-09-21, and the missing piece is not the feed. The row above says the gap is "a per-block key-bus peak feed from the live audio device into duck_advance", which is what jce_audio_mixer.h:153 tells a reader to believe: "The exact same envelope+curve math runs in the live miniaudio node, so it can be driven offline over a synthetic key envelope in a unit test." THAT SENTENCE IS FALSE AND IT IS THE ONE THAT STOPS YOU LOOKING -- it says the live path is handled and the offline driver is merely its test twin. Measured across the whole repository: grep -i for duck|sidechain in engine/src/middleware/audio/jce_audio.c returns 0; `git grep -l duck_advance -- engine/src/` returns jce_audio_mixer.c and nothing else; `git grep -l JceAudioDuckParams` returns only contracts/*, editor/src/panels/jce_panel_audio_mixer.cpp, the header, and jce_audio_mixer.c. No file in the audio BACKEND (jce_audio.c, jce_miniaudio_impl.c) mentions ducking in any form, and there is no ma_node for it. So the envelope+curve math exists exactly ONCE, in the pure model, and the duck gain is permanently 1.0 in every shipped game. THE TAIL IS ALREADY WIRED, which is what makes this worth stating precisely: jce_audio_mixer_resolve_volume_ducked IS applied at jce_rt_audio.c:206 and does reach jce_audio_bus_set_volume. Only the head is absent. And the comment one line above it -- "duck gain is 1.0 for buses without a sidechain, so this is a no-op for them" -- is accurate and currently true for EVERY bus, including the ones that have a sidechain. WHY THAT SENTENCE IS PLAUSIBLE RATHER THAN CARELESS, found by searching for the THING instead of the words: the audio backend has exactly two ma_node_vtables, g_reverb_vtable and g_dsp_vtable, both in jce_audio.c. The second runs jce_audio_dsp_chain_process, and jce_audio_dsp.c DOES contain a live compressor with attack_ms/release_ms executing on the real audio thread. So "envelope+curve math runs in a live miniaudio node" is ALMOST true -- there is live envelope math in a live node. What does not exist is that math being the DUCK math, or being driven by a key bus: grep for duck|sidechain|key_bus|jce_audio_mixer in jce_audio_dsp.c returns ZERO. A maintainer checking the claim casually finds a live compressor with attack/release and stops. The sentence has a decoy sitting next to it. SO THE UNIT IS: build the live node (the reverb node in jce_audio.c is the established template, and every bus is already a ma_sound_group and therefore a ma_node), feed it, and correct the header sentence -- not "add a peak feed" to a consumer that was never built.
CLOSED 2026-09-21. The duck now runs on the real mix, and the missing piece turned out to be one number rather than a subsystem. THE MEASUREMENT: jce_audio_bus_get_peak(audio, name) (jce_audio.h) reports the peak |sample| a named bus put out since the caller last asked -- POST-FADER, read-and-clear. It is metered inside dsp_node_process in jce_audio.c, the insert node that already existed for FEATURE 5.1: that node is already spliced group -> dsp -> reverb/endpoint by one pair of functions, already copies the whole block, and is already torn down in one place, so metering costs one compare per sample and NO new lifecycle. The peak is published as raw float bits in an SDL_AtomicInt under a CAS-max loop; for non-negative IEEE-754 floats the bit pattern orders exactly as the value does, so max-of-bits is max-of-floats with no round-trip, and `>` never holding for NaN means a NaN sample is skipped instead of pinning the meter. A metering-only bus simply carries an empty chain, which that node has always handled as a plain copy. THE WIRE: jce_audio_duck_pump(audio, mixer, dt) (jce_audio_duck_pump.h/.c, new) samples each key bus's meter and advances every installed sidechain; rt_apply_mixer calls it once per frame, between jce_audio_mixer_update and the bus-volume push that was already reading the duck gain. Authored sidechains reach it through the path that already existed -- rt_init_mixer -> jce_audio_mixer_apply_config -> set_sidechain at 48 kHz -- so the block length is dt at that same rate and the attack/release coefficients mean what they say. IT IS ITS OWN FILE BECAUSE NEITHER HEADER MAY OWN IT: jce_audio_mixer.h's central claim is "Engine-agnostic -- no miniaudio/FMOD coupling", which is exactly what lets the follower be driven offline and be step for step the code that runs live, so a function there taking a JceAudio* would make that sentence false -- the same species of false sentence this row exists to record. Putting it in jce_audio.h would give the backend a dependency on bus bookkeeping it does not need. It is also ONE function because the first draft was two: the runtime had the sampler inline and the test had a second copy whose own comment called it a model of the first, an arrangement that cannot catch a defect in the sampler because the copy can carry a fix the runtime does not. ONE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, and it is the part a test at volume 1.0 would never have caught: duck_advance used to multiply the reported key level by the key's full resolved VOLUME. Against a post-fader meter that squares the key's gain -- exact at 1.0, 6 dB wrong at 0.5 -- and "works, mis-calibrated at non-unity" is the failure class this ledger keeps finding. It now folds in only the key's MUTE/SOLO state, which is what its own comment already said it did and is the half a post-fader meter genuinely cannot carry (a muted bus is still metered). Every existing caller is a test at key volume 1.0, where the two are identical. THE FALSE SENTENCE IS GONE: jce_audio_mixer.h no longer claims "the exact same envelope+curve math runs in the live miniaudio node". It now says where the math lives (here, once), what the backend supplies (the measurement), who closes the loop (rt_apply_mixer), and records what the old sentence cost. PROVEN WITHOUT A DEVICE, which needed two more symbols and is the reason no case in this unit can skip: jce_audio_create_offline() builds an engine the shared output device does not pump, and jce_audio_render_offline() pumps it from the caller instead, running the REAL node graph -- voices, bus groups, insert nodes. render_offline REFUSES a device-pumped engine rather than warning about it, because two pumps on one graph race for the same read cursors and a comment is the one thing a caller can be sure of not reading. TWO DEFECTS THE BUILD FOUND THAT READING DID NOT, both in this change rather than in the old code. (1) jce_audio_render_offline returned zero frames on a graph with NOTHING attached to its endpoint -- miniaudio has no silence to mix there, so it produces none -- and every other case had created a bus first, so every other case had a node. It now silence-fills and then reads over it, which is what the shared device callback does and is what makes the master tap gapless; the offline pump has no business being less reliable than the thing it stands in for. (2) duck_advance calls back once per installed sidechain, and TWO TARGETS MAY SHARE ONE KEY -- Music and SFX both ducking under Voice is the ordinary configuration. rt_mixer_key_peak read the read-and-clear meter on every callback, so the first target consumed the key's peak and the second got what arrived in the microseconds after it: nothing. It would have shipped as "that one bus just doesn't duck", silent, and only in projects with a second sidechain on the same key. It now memoises per pump: one read per key per frame, shared. The hazard is written in this commit's own header text -- the exemption line for jce_audio_bus_get_peak says a second reader would be a bug -- and was walked into one file away. tests/middleware/audio/test_jce_audio_bus_meter.c, 10 cases: the meter reads zero with nothing playing (the negative control without which a meter reporting a constant would look like success), rises with a voice and returns to zero when it stops, HALVES when the fader halves (a ratio, so the engine's channel conversion cancels and the case is about the fader alone -- a pre-fader meter reads the same number twice), clears on read, rejects nonsense, and refuses the device-pumped engine. Then the row itself: a loud voice on the key bus pulls the target down through the live meter and the target recovers when the key falls silent. Two targets sharing one key duck by the SAME amount (asserted as agreement, not as "both below 1", because both-ducked passes with one of them barely moving). Plus a MUTATION CONTROL built at key volume 0.25 -- restore the `*= resolve_volume(key)` line and only that case fails -- and the mute/solo half that was deliberately kept.
features.compared: Unity's Duck Volume effect is a real sidechain: you route a send from the key bus into the ducking effect and the compressor listens to that signal at mix time. UE has a submix-based sidechain compressor and a first-class Audio Modulation ducking system. Godot's AudioEffectCompressor has a `sidechain` property naming another bus, evaluated inside the audio thread. All three actually measure the key bus.

features.feature: Aux send/return taps a bus into a parallel effect bus
features.evidence:
Built-but-unwired. jce_audio_mixer.h:92-138 defines the full console-style aux send model (set_send/get_send/remove_send/send_count/send_at plus resolve_send returning resolve_volume(src) * amount), the editor authors sends per bus (editor/src/panels/jce_panel_audio_mixer.cpp:180, :754, :773) and jce_audio_mixer_config.h:11-13 parses the "sends" array back at Play start. Nothing then routes any audio. jce_audio_mixer_resolve_send (engine/src/middleware/audio/jce_audio_mixer.c:442-447) has no caller outside its own header, implementation and contracts/abi-snapshot.txt:613; and the device side offers no send at all -- jce_audio.h:183-194 gives only bus_create, bus_set_volume and voice_set_bus, so device buses are flat children of Master with a single gain each and no parallel tap exists to carry a send into. The missing reader is device-side send routing (a second output edge per bus group) plus the runtime call that would drive it.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. jce_audio_mixer_resolve_send (jce_audio_mixer.c:442) still has no caller outside its own definition and header. Sends are authored per bus in the editor, parsed back at Play start, and route no audio.
TRACED 2026-09-21, and there is a hazard IN FRONT of this row that had to be removed before any routing could be wired. jce_audio_mixer_set_send (jce_audio_mixer.c:382) guarded exactly one case: `if (!bus_valid(m, src) || !bus_valid(m, dest) || src == dest) return false;` -- DIRECT SELF-SEND ONLY. A->B followed by B->A was accepted, and so was any longer ring. It has been harmless for precisely one reason: nothing routes a send's audio, so an authored ring is bookkeeping that jce_audio_mixer_resolve_send reads once and nobody walks. That is the same shape as jce_cvar_at in the console row -- a structure nobody reads cannot be wrong yet, and "cannot be wrong yet" is indistinguishable from "is correct" until someone adds the reader. THIS ROW IS THE READER: an aux send is a parallel edge in the audio graph, the device side of it is a second output edge per bus group, and a ring in that graph has no bottom to recurse to -- a hang, not a wrong number. The refusal landed first and on its own, in the bookkeeping layer that knows the graph, with five cases and no device. The load-bearing one is NEGATIVE: a diamond is not a ring (two buses may both send into a third, and a chain may fan out, without anything returning to its source), because without it a guard that refused EVERYTHING would pass every positive assertion. Public behaviour change: the second half of a ring now returns false, and a caller that used to get true should surface the refusal rather than drop the author's click. WHAT REMAINS IS THE ROW ITSELF and it is unblocked. The device side offers no send at all -- jce_audio.h gives bus_create, bus_set_volume, voice_set_bus and (since 688edb33) bus_get_peak, so device buses are flat children of Master with a single gain each and no parallel tap. The shape is group -> [dsp] -> splitter -> out0 -> reverb/endpoint and out1 -> dest bus group, with the send level on the splitter's second output bus; ma_splitter_node_init is present in this miniaudio (verified, not assumed from the docs). AND ITS INSTRUMENT NOW EXISTS, which it did not this morning: jce_audio_create_offline + jce_audio_render_offline + the POST-FADER jce_audio_bus_get_peak (all from 688edb33) prove a send carries signal into a parallel bus with no device -- play on A, send A->B at 0.5, and B's meter must read while B has no voices of its own, with the same scene minus the send as the negative control.
CLOSED 2026-09-21. The missing reader this row names -- "device-side send routing (a second output edge per bus group) plus the runtime call that would drive it" -- now exists. A bus's terminal feeds a ma_splitter_node with 1 + JCE_AUDIO_BUS_MAX_SENDS outputs: output 0 is its normal path, outputs 1..8 are sends whose per-output bus volume IS the send amount. jce_audio_bus_set_send / _get_send are the device API, the splitter is created lazily so a bus with no send has a graph byte-identical to before, and rt_init_mixer now walks send_count / send_at for every mirrored bus and calls it -- which finally gives jce_audio_mixer_resolve_send the caller it never had outside its own header and implementation. resolve_send rather than the raw amount, so a send obeys the same mute and solo the direct path does. EIGHT sends per bus, deliberately the same cap as the mixer's JCE_AUDIO_MAX_SENDS: a device routing fewer than the panel can author would be the same partial wiring the row was opened for. A second destination ADDS a send the way a console strip feeds several returns; repeating one destination re-scales its slot; zero retires it. TWO DEFECTS FOUND WHILE WIRING IT, both now pinned. Standing up a bus's insert chain AFTER a send existed re-spliced group -> dsp -> endpoint and orphaned the splitter, so the send kept reporting its amount through get_send and carried no audio -- the dsp now targets the splitter when one exists, and the order-independence case is the only one that creates the source's dsp at all. And a self-send is refused at the DEVICE layer, not only by the mixer's ring check: that edge feeds the node its own input comes from and the first pull through it does not return. tests/middleware/audio/test_jce_audio_bus_send_device.c measures the DESTINATION bus's meter, because a send is a parallel tap and the source's level is unchanged either way. Its first case is the negative control that a bus with no voice and no send reads silence; without it every later case is satisfied by buses that are not isolated. Three mutations red: the send edge never attached, the amount treated as on/off, and the dsp re-pointed at the endpoint. REMAINING, stated rather than folded in: the amount is applied once at Play start, so a send authored to change over time (an automation lane) is not expressible, and there is no per-send pre/post-fader choice -- resolve_send is post-fader by construction. ALSO CLOSED HERE, because the send would otherwise have been inert where it matters: rt_mixer_read_config now falls back to the mounted PAK. That fallback was itself unreachable at first: jce_default_main only sets mixer_config_path when the file exists ON THE HOST, so a packaged exe passes NULL and the early return killed the PAK branch in exactly the configuration it was written for. tests/application/test_jce_runtime_mixer_from_pak.c leaves the path NULL on purpose and asserts the DEVICE-side send amount, so one assertion covers PAK find, decompress, parse, bus mirror and routing.

features.feature: Long music streams from disk instead of loading fully decoded
features.evidence:
CLOSED 2026-09-21. jce_audio_load_streaming (jce_audio.c:1492) is a second load path that decodes nothing up front, and JceAudioSourceComponent.load_type selects it per clip -- authored in the inspector as a Load Type combo (jce_panel_inspector_audio.cpp:30-41, i18n in all 15 locales), serialised as "loadType" (jce_scene_components_audio.c:33,110), and honoured by the shipped runtime at jce_rt_audio.c:1089. Each VOICE owns its own ma_decoder, so two voices on one clip keep independent cursors.
WHERE THE BYTES LIVE, which is the whole point of the row. Three strategies, picked by where the clip is rather than by the author -- so the wrong choice is not expressible: (a) no pak, i.e. a loose project -- ma_decoder_init_file reads the file incrementally and NOTHING is resident; (b) a STORED pak entry -- the encoded bytes are already in the archive blob, so the slot borrows the pointer and takes a jce_pak_acquire reference, costing ZERO extra bytes. This is the normal case in a shipped single-file exe: jce_archive_writer keeps ZSTD only when it beats 95% (compress_keep, jce_archive_writer.c:213) and .ogg/.mp3 never do; (c) a re-compressed pak entry -- expanded once and held, i.e. compressed-in-memory, which is the best available for that entry. A five-minute stereo track therefore costs 0 bytes rather than ~50 MB of s16, and no up-front decode, in the build a player actually runs.
PROVEN, not asserted. test_jce_audio_streaming_clip, 7 cases, offline engine so no case may skip. The discriminators are not "it makes sound" (the old decompress-on-load path does too): get_pcm_data returns NULL for a streaming sound and non-NULL for the same payload loaded normally; jce_pak_refcount rises by one for a STORED entry and NOT for a compressed one (negative control, with each fixture asserting it actually got the pak flag it was built for); and a host-path clip goes silent once its file is DELETED, with a control proving the engine still plays a freshly loaded clip. Mutation: disabling the borrow (if (0 && ...)) reddens the borrow case alone -- "Expected 2 Was 1" -- and leaves the other six green.
WHAT IS STILL NOT HERE: Unity exposes Compressed In Memory as a third named option the author picks. JCE derives it instead, so a clip in a re-compressed archive entry cannot be forced to stream, and a clip on disk cannot be forced to stay resident. UE's Prime (warm the cache without retaining) has no equivalent. Both are authoring knobs, not capability: the memory and the up-front decode this row exists to measure are gone.
features.compared: Unity's AudioClip Load Type offers Decompress On Load, Compressed In Memory and Streaming, chosen per clip in the importer. UE streams Sound Waves through a streaming cache with a per-asset Loading Behavior (Retain / Prime / Stream). Godot's AudioStreamOggVorbis and AudioStreamMP3 decode incrementally during playback by default. JCE now has the per-clip choice and decodes incrementally on both the loose and the packaged path; it derives the in-memory-vs-disk half from where the asset lives instead of making the author pick.

features.feature: Important sounds survive when the voice pool runs out
features.evidence:
Voice stealing exists and is reasonable, but it is age-only with no author control. jce_audio.c:35 fixes the pool at JCE_MAX_VOICES 64, and alloc_voice (jce_audio.c:1382-1428) tries an unused slot, then reclaims any voice that has stopped, then steals: it picks the lowest play_seq among non-looping voices first so background music is not cut, falling back to the oldest voice overall when everything loops. There is no priority anywhere to weight that choice -- JceAudioSourceComponent (engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_scene.h:937-954) carries clip_path, volume, pitch, spatial_blend, loop, play_on_awake, the four attenuation fields and mixer_bus, and nothing else; the inspector that draws it (editor/src/panels/jce_panel_inspector_audio.cpp:9-84) exposes no priority either. So a critical one-shot (a boss cue, a line of dialogue) is stolen by whatever plays after it, purely because it is older.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. JceAudioSourceComponent carries no priority field -- the two 'priority' hits in jce_scene.h are render_priority (transparent sort order) and a reverb zone's. Stealing is still age-only, so an author cannot protect a voice.
CLOSED 2026-09-21 (fd2bea68). JceAudioSourceComponent gains `priority` (APPENDED at the struct tail), the inspector edits it, and rt_finish_audio_source passes it to the new jce_audio_play_priority so the value reaches ALLOCATION -- the only moment it can matter, since the pool is consulted when the voice is created. HIGHER IS MORE IMPORTANT and 0 is normal, matching Unreal's FSoundBase::Priority and inverting Unity's, because this struct is zero-initialised and every scene saved before the field existed carries a 0. alloc_voice now evicts the LEAST IMPORTANT voice (priority, then one-shot over loop, then age) AND refuses to let a strictly-lower-priority sound steal at all, returning JCE_VOICE_INVALID when nothing is stealable -- both halves, because choosing a better victim still evicts the boss cue once every voice is a boss cue. tests/middleware/audio/test_jce_audio_voice_priority.c, seven cases on the offline engine: a pool-exhaustion self-check so the rest provably reach the stealing path, the protection, a NEGATIVE CONTROL that ordinary voices are still stolen (without it the protection cases also pass on a build that refuses everything), priority-beats-age with the protected voice deliberately the OLDEST, the refusal including that an EQUAL priority still gets in, set_priority on a live voice, and the victim ordering. That last case exists because a mutation replacing the ordering with plain age SURVIVED the other six: the refusal guard was carrying all of them, since their incoming sound is at NORMAL and the protected voice outranks it. Both mutations are red now. jce_audio_play_priority and the two setters are also stubbed in the JCE_NO_AUDIO branch, which nothing compiles. Remaining gap vs Unreal: no Concurrency GROUPS -- priority is per-voice, with no per-category cap or group resolution rule.
features.compared: Unity gives every AudioSource a Priority (0-255, 0 = never steal) and virtualises the lowest-priority voices past the real-voice budget. UE assigns each sound a Priority and a Concurrency group with an explicit resolution rule (stop oldest / stop lowest priority / stop quietest / prevent new). Godot has no per-source priority but lets you cap polyphony per player and per bus. JCE sits at roughly Godot's level and behind Unity and UE.

features.feature: Author a custom volume-over-distance curve per source
features.evidence:
CLOSED 2026-09-22. JceAudioSourceComponent.rolloff_curve names an authored curve document; the runtime evaluates it at the listener distance in metres and multiplies the source's authored volume (rt_audio_rolloff_gain in jce_rt_audio.c). Authored in the inspector as a Curve Editor asset field with i18n in all 15 locales, round-trips as "rolloffCurve" (jce_scene_components_audio.c), and reaches the live voice through the same per-frame loop that already pushes position, velocity and occlusion.
THE PATH IS THE SWITCH, and that is a design decision rather than an omission: there is no CUSTOM entry in attenuation_model, because one would let a scene say CUSTOM with no curve, or name a curve while the model says INVERSE, and then something has to decide which half to believe. Naming a curve forces the engine-side model to NONE, so the analytic law and the curve can never both attenuate the same source.
IT REUSES THE CURVE STACK RATHER THAN ADDING ONE. jce_curve.h, the parser, the evaluator and the per-runtime parsed-curve cache all already existed for jce.curve_eval; rt_curve_fetch was made non-static so the audio path shares that one cache. Two caches would have meant two parses, two failure logs and two answers for one document.
PROVEN. tests/application/test_jce_runtime_audio_rolloff_curve.c, 4 cases, offline audio engine through JceRuntimeDesc.audio so no case may skip. "It gets quieter with distance" is NOT the assertion -- the analytic models already did that, and a control runs the identical geometry with no curve and must fall. MUTATION showed the two curve cases carry DIFFERENT halves: a curve flat at 1.0 must not lose level with distance (killed by leaving the analytic model on alongside the curve, 0.47 -> 0.02; NOT killed by stubbing the gain), and a curve falling to 0.0 at 20 m must silence the source there (killed by stubbing the gain to 1.0; NOT killed by the double-attenuation mutation). A fourth case fixes that a curve which will not load falls back instead of silencing -- "authored at zero" and "file missing" must not be one sound.
ALSO FIXED HERE, because this row named it: "jce_audio.h documents max_distance as ignored by INVERSE and EXPONENTIAL, so the field the inspector always shows is inert for the default model". The inspector now disables Max Distance for the models that ignore it and says why, and disables the whole analytic block while a curve is set. A live control that cannot affect anything, drawn identically to the ones that can, is the same defect class this ledger keeps finding.
WHAT IS STILL NOT HERE: Unity draws FOUR curves against distance on its AudioSource -- volume, spatial blend, spread and reverb zone mix. This is the volume one. The other three are tracked where they belong: spatial blend is audio.source.spatial-blend-continuous, and there is no spread or reverb-send curve. That is a count of curves, not a missing mechanism: the component field, the evaluator, the cache and the per-frame apply are all in place and a second curve is another field through the same path.
features.compared: Unity's AudioSource draws four editable AnimationCurves against distance -- volume (with Custom Rolloff), spatial blend, spread and reverb zone mix. UE's Sound Attenuation asset supports Linear/Logarithmic/Inverse/LogReverse/NaturalSound plus a Custom Curve asset, with separate curves for spatialization, air absorption and occlusion. Godot offers the same four analytic models as JCE plus max_db and a unit-size control, so JCE is at Godot's level and behind Unity and UE.

features.evidence:
The field is authored as a continuous value and consumed as a boolean. jce_scene.h:942 declares float spatial_blend, the inspector edits it with a 0..1 DragFloat in 0.01 steps (editor/src/panels/jce_panel_inspector_audio.cpp:19), and it round-trips through JSON as "spatialBlend" (engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_scene_components_audio.c:20, :96). FOUND 2026-09-20 WHILE CLOSING debug.assertions.engine-macro, recorded here
rather than fixed, because changing a test that sits next to a red one makes
it impossible to say afterwards which change turned it green.

tests/middleware/audio/test_jce_audio_master_tap.c self-ignores when
jce_audio_master_tap_set() cannot open a device -- but NOT when a device
opens and then delivers nothing.  On this machine audiodg.exe crashed five
times (13:10:06, 13:12:07, 13:12:10, 13:14:23, 13:14:56 local) and did not
restart, and the test then failed DETERMINISTICALLY -- 5760 frames where it
wants more than 7200, identical across ten runs, while CPU queue length was 0
and 8 GB of commit was free.  Every other audio test passed: this is the only
one that needs the device to actually call back over wall-clock time.

So the guard covers "no device" and misses "device present, not flowing",
which is the state a CI box with a dummy endpoint is in.  The fix is for the
tap test to treat zero forward progress as an ignore rather than a failure --
distinguishing it from a real regression by requiring that SOME frames arrive
before it judges the cadence.
INCREMENT 2026-09-21, STILL BEHIND. The one-bit quantisation this row names is gone: jce_audio_voice_set_spatial_blend scales the spatializer's attenuation floor (min_gain = 1 - blend), rt_finish_audio_source passes the authored float straight through instead of collapsing it with `> 0.5f`, and the editor's viewport gizmo now uses the same `> 0.0f` test as the runtime -- while it said 0.5 a source authored at 0.3 was spatial in the mix and had no gizmo, and the inspector revealed attenuation controls at > 0.0 that the runtime would never apply. Three thresholds for one field, now one. STATUS UNCHANGED because Unity's spatialBlend is "a true 0..1 crossfade between the 2D (fully panned by the mixer) and 3D (positional) contributions, and is itself curve-editable over distance". This blends the ATTENUATION axis only. Once spatialisation is on, miniaudio pans from the 3D direction, so a source at blend 0.5 is still fully panned by direction where Unity would half-pan it, and there is no per-distance curve. Saying "continuous" and leaving that unsaid would be the half-truth this ledger exists to prevent. NEXT INCREMENT: a true crossfade needs the 2D and 3D contributions mixed rather than one attenuation scaled -- in practice two voices per source, which doubles pool pressure and therefore interacts with audio.voice.priority-and-stealing. That coupling is the reason it is a separate unit and not a follow-up patch. tests/middleware/audio/test_jce_audio_spatial_blend.c measures a RENDERED LEVEL at a fixed distance across four blends and asserts monotonicity plus a real difference between the endpoints; its first case is the positive control that the offline graph makes sound at all, without which every comparison would be between two silences.
features.compared: Unity's spatialBlend is a true 0..1 crossfade between the 2D (fully panned by the mixer) and 3D (positional) contributions, and is itself curve-editable over distance. Godot's AudioStreamPlayer3D has no blend but its 2D/3D players are distinct node types, so the ambiguity does not arise. UE mixes a non-spatialized bed against the spatialized signal via attenuation's spatialization settings and a stereo spread. JCE quantises the author's intent to one bit.

features.feature: Canvas scales with screen size, biased toward width or height
features.evidence:
The scaler is wired and correct as far as it goes: engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_ui_canvas.c:2595-2601 takes screen_w/reference_resolution[0] and screen_h/reference_resolution[1] and sets fr.ui_scale = sqrtf(rsx*rsy), and :2609-2610 composes Canvas.scale_factor on top (the comment there records that scale_factor previously parsed, serialised and showed in the Inspector while NOTHING read it -- that gap is now closed). That ui_scale then genuinely reaches every length: font px (:941), layout-group padding/spacing/cell size (:1417-1429), slider handle size (:1180), scrollbar thickness (:1338) and size_delta/anchored_position (:492-495). What is missing is the match parameter itself: sqrtf(rsx*rsy) hardcodes match=0.5, and JceCanvasComponent (engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_scene.h:1856-1862) has render_mode, sort_order, reference_resolution, scale_factor and pixel_perfect but no match field and no scale-mode enum.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. No match_mode, match_width or screen_match field exists on any component. The scaler is permanently the geometric mean of the two axis ratios -- Unity's Match slider at 0.5 and nowhere else, so a UI cannot be pinned to width on an ultrawide.

CLOSED 2026-09-20. JceCanvasComponent gains match_width_or_height (appended), round-tripped as "matchWidthOrHeight", edited as a slider in the UI inspector with a tooltip in all 15 locales, and consumed by jce_ui_canvas_scale_for -- which is now the ONE derivation the renderer uses, exposed publicly so a test asks the engine instead of recomputing the formula. (A test that derives the answer a second way asserts against its own arithmetic; this tree has paid for that, with a hinge axis disagreeing with its clamp by 22 degrees.)

THE DEFAULT IS 0.5, NOT UNITY'S 0, so every scene written before the field existed parses to the geometric mean this engine already computed. And the scaler takes the sqrtf(rsx*rsy) path verbatim at exactly 0.5 rather than evaluating the pow() form.

THAT SHORTCUT IS LOAD-BEARING AND IT WAS MEASURED, not assumed. With the exact-0.5 branch removed, the first version of the test still PASSED -- on one fixture, powf(x,.5)*powf(y,.5) landed on the same bits as sqrtf(x*y). Sweeping 36 real reference/screen pairs (1920x1080, 1280x720, 375x812 ... against 2560x1080, 3840x2160, 1170x2532 ...) kills it: at least one pair differs in the last bit, which is a layout moving by a pixel in a project that changed nothing.

5 of 5 mutations red: drop the shortcut, swap the exponents, ignore match entirely (the previous state), scale a WORLD canvas, scale an unauthored reference resolution.
features.compared: Unity's CanvasScaler has three modes (Constant Pixel Size, Scale With Screen Size, Constant Physical Size), and in the second a Match Width-Or-Height slider from 0 to 1 that ships as an authorable value -- a portrait mobile UI is usually matched to width, not to 0.5. Godot has stretch modes canvas_items/viewport with aspect keep_width/keep_height/expand. JCE always uses the geometric mean, so a UI tuned for an ultrawide or a portrait phone cannot be biased.

features.evidence:

AND char_limit COUNTED BYTES while jce_scene.h calls it 'max chars'. A limit of 4 admitted one three-byte character and then the FIRST BYTE of the next. Insertion is now per character with TWO caps in two units: the buffer in bytes (text[256] is a fixed array) and char_limit in characters.

MEASURED headlessly through the real canvas: typing three CJK characters gives 9 bytes, backspace gives 6; a four-CHARACTER limit admits two CJK characters (6 bytes) where it used to truncate to 4 bytes mid-character.

4 of 4 mutations red, and one of them only after the tests were fixed: 'buffer cap checked in characters' SURVIVED the first round, because nothing filled the field -- and that mutant writes 255 three-byte characters into a 256-byte array. The test that kills it offers 600 bytes and asserts the result is a whole number of characters.

ONE MORE THING WORTH RECORDING: the first version of the test FAILED and the engine was right. The missing readers are (a) any script binding -- none of the 96 expose entries in contracts/script-api.json names it -- and (b) any gameplay caller in engine/src/application/.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20, and the unwired half is now measurable: jce_coroutine_* has NO caller anywhere under engine/src outside its own translation unit. So the full Unity-parity yield set -- WaitForSeconds, WaitForFixedUpdate, WaitForEndOfFrame, WaitUntil, next-frame -- exists in C, is public via api_runtime.h, and nothing in the engine or any script can reach it. The only wait a script can express remains a wall-clock float.
features.compared: Unity's yield returns WaitForFixedUpdate, WaitForEndOfFrame and WaitUntil(predicate) from any MonoBehaviour. Godot awaits arbitrary signals and `get_tree().physics_frame`. features.feature: Script raycasts can filter by layer and return every hit
features.evidence:
CLOSED 2026-09-22. Two host members appended to JceScriptHost and generated into all seven languages: jce.raycast_filtered (closest hit honouring a layer mask and the trigger skip, the same 8-values-or-0 shape jce.raycast already had) and jce.raycast_all (every entity along the ray, near to far).
NOTHING NEW WAS IMPLEMENTED BELOW THE BINDING, which is what made this cheap and is also what made it a real gap: jce_physics_raycast_filtered and jce_physics_raycast_all were already implemented down to Bullet, already took a JceQueryFilter, and already honoured the mask and the trigger skip. They had no script reader. The host implementations share rt_script_query_filter with the overlap queries rather than building a second JceQueryFilter, because two spellings of that is exactly how the ray and the overlaps came to disagree about the mask convention in the first place; layer_mask 0 means every layer in both.
hit_triggers IS SEPARATE FROM THE MASK because a trigger volume is not a layer -- Unity splits them the same way (layerMask vs QueryTriggerInteraction) and collapsing them would make "ignore triggers on layer 3" inexpressible.
PROVEN END TO END. tests/application/test_jce_runtime_script_raycast_filter.c runs a real Lua probe against a real Bullet world through the real runtime: the generated differential harness already proves the seven languages marshal these calls identically, but it cannot see the HOST glue -- filter construction, body->entity mapping, near->far order -- and glue is where this ledger keeps finding defects. Three kinematic boxes on layers 0/1/2 down +Z; raycast_all returns 3 with no duplicates; a mask selecting layer 1 hits the MIDDLE box at distance 9 rather than the nearer one at 4; a mask selecting layer 5, which nothing is on, misses. THE MASK ASSERTIONS ARE A PAIR: an ignored mask passes the selecting one and fails the empty one, a broken call fails the selecting one, so neither alone would do. MUTATION: forcing layer_mask to 0xFFFFFFFF reddens it with exactly the predicted signature -- miss_layer5 goes 1 -> 0 and the layer-1 distance collapses from 9 to 4.
A CHECKER WAS FIXED ON THE WAY. scriptgen_core.shape_is_type_compatible counted a const ARRAY INPUT as an output (`p.arity != 0`), so the entity_table shape -- which requires exactly one output -- rejected any query taking a ray while accepting the identical shape taking loose x/y/z. The file's own out_params() already had the correct rule and says it in a comment ("`const` decides direction"), and emit_api_json -- the published contract -- is built from it. Now both use it. Strictly narrower, so no entry that was refused becomes allowed; the 99 existing entries validating unchanged is the positive control.
WHAT IS STILL DIFFERENT: raycast_all returns ENTITIES, not full hit records, because the eight-value hit does not survive as an array shape across seven languages without inventing a per-language container -- re-query a specific one with raycast_filtered for its point and normal. And sweeps (jce_physics_sweep_sphere, Unity's SphereCast/CapsuleCast) are still unbound; that is a separate query, not a filter, and it is no longer what this row measures.
features.compared: Unity's Physics.Raycast takes layerMask and QueryTriggerInteraction and has RaycastAll/RaycastNonAlloc plus SphereCast and CapsuleCast. Unreal's LineTraceByChannel/ByObjectType/Multi and sweeps take channels and object types. Godot's intersect_ray takes a collision_mask plus exclude lists. JCE now has the mask, the trigger flag and the multi-hit ray in all seven languages; the sweeps remain unbound and are tracked as their own question.
