features.feature: Insert effects (EQ, compressor, limiter, delay) on mixer buses
features.evidence:
Real, wired end-to-end. jce_audio_dsp.h:45-51 defines exactly four effect kinds (EQ/COMPRESSOR/LIMITER/DELAY), the EQ covering peaking/shelf/low-pass/high-pass biquads (:54-60), capped at 8 per chain (:39) and 2 channels (:41). The editor's mixer panel authors and round-trips them (editor/src/panels/jce_panel_audio_mixer.cpp:296-340 parse_effect, :735 add), rt_init_mixer re-attaches each authored chain to the live device by bus name (engine/src/application/jce_rt_audio.c:110-117, :158-162), and jce_audio.c:471-500 dsp_node_ensure splices a real ma_node as src->dsp->target, so the DSP is genuinely in the graph. Two gaps: the palette has no pitch-shift/chorus/flanger/distortion/spectrum and no plugin path, and jce_build_manager.cpp:684-690 states in its own comment that the runtime mixer read is host-only (jce_fs_host_read_all) so "a pure single-exe build does not consume this copy" -- a single-file exe silently falls back to the default bus tree with no effects.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. The chain is real and wired end to end; what makes it behind is its shape -- four fixed effect kinds (EQ/compressor/limiter/delay), eight per chain, two channels, and no way for a project to add a fifth. Unity's is a plugin surface; this is a closed set.
 HALF CLOSED 2026-09-21 (bcae28c8), and it is the half this row named: "jce_build_manager.cpp states in its own comment that the runtime mixer read is host-only so a pure single-exe build does not consume this copy". rt_mixer_read_config now falls back to the mounted PAK, so a packaged game gets its authored insert chains instead of the default bus tree. Closed as a side effect of wiring aux sends, which would otherwise have been inert in the same build for the same reason. STILL BEHIND on the other axis the row names, unchanged: four fixed effect kinds (EQ/COMPRESSOR/LIMITER/DELAY), no pitch-shift, chorus, flanger, distortion or spectrum, and no plugin path -- that is a palette, not a wiring gap, and it is what would move this row.
CLOSED 2026-09-22 on the axis this row actually named. Its own words were "four fixed effect kinds (EQ/compressor/limiter/delay), eight per chain, two channels, and NO WAY FOR A PROJECT TO ADD A FIFTH. Unity's is a plugin surface; this is a closed set." The set is no longer closed.
THE PLUGIN SURFACE. jce_audio_dsp_register_effect takes a JceAudioEffectVTable (name, state_size, configure/reset/process/release) and returns a type id at or above JCE_AUDIO_EFFECT_CUSTOM_BASE. The chain owns one state_size allocation per instance and hands it to every callback, so a registered effect keeps its filter/envelope/delay history exactly as a built-in does. Registration is IDEMPOTENT BY NAME -- a second registration returns the same id -- because two ids for one name would make a saved mixer depend on the order modules registered in. The id base is 256 rather than "the next free small integer", so adding a built-in later can never silently renumber somebody's saved mixer. And it is AUTHORABLE: audio_mixer.json resolves an unknown "type" string through jce_audio_dsp_effect_type_from_name, so a project's own effect is placed on a bus like any other rather than being script-only.
THE PALETTE, 4 -> 7: chorus, flanger and distortion (soft-clip / hard-clip / foldback). Chorus and flanger SHARE one modulated-delay implementation and one parameter struct, because they are one machine -- a delay line swept by an LFO -- and what separates them is only where the numbers sit; two copies would have drifted the first time one got a fix. Their DEFAULTS are deliberately far apart and a test asserts it, because identical defaults would make them two names for one sound. The read head is fractionally interpolated: rounding it to a whole sample turns the sweep into a staircase, which is audible as zipper noise, the one artefact the effect exists to avoid. The line is sized centre+depth+4 so a deep sweep cannot read past the write head -- that is a click every LFO cycle, not a subtle artefact.
ONE PARSER AND ONE SERIALISER, which is a dedup this change forced rather than chose. The engine parsed effects in jce_audio_mixer_config.c and the editor's mixer panel parsed AND wrote them again, with the same field lists spelled twice. Adding three effects is exactly the change that leaves one copy behind, and the copy left behind is usually the READER -- so the editor would save an effect the runtime silently drops. Both are now jce_audio_effect_from_json/_to_json, and the type SPELLING comes from one table. That table caught a real near-miss: it was first written with "compressor", while every mixer already on disk spells it "comp" -- a lookup that would have been wrong for exactly the effects people have.
PROVEN. tests/middleware/audio/test_jce_audio_dsp_palette.c, 10 cases, and not one of them asserts "the effect runs": a chain that accepted an effect and passed the buffer through untouched satisfies that, and is the shape this ledger keeps finding. Each names a property a pass-through does not have -- a shaper returns sample values the input never took, foldback lands BELOW the ceiling where a clipper sits on it, feedback is still audible after the input stops, and a registered effect's process() must both run and keep its state.
MUTATION CORRECTED THE CHORUS CASE TWICE, and both times it was green while measuring nothing. Freezing the LFO to zero left it passing, first because FEEDBACK made the line's contents differ block to block whatever the read head did, and then -- with feedback zeroed -- because the LINE WAS STILL PRIMING (a 22 ms chorus is ~1056 frames at 48 kHz and the blocks were 512, so block 3 read a region block 1 had not written). Priming past the line length leaves the read head as the only thing that can still be moving. Both were the same mistake in different clothes: an assertion satisfied by state that has nothing to do with the thing under test.
COSTS RECORDED, NOT HIDDEN. (1) The ABI snapshot records ONE INCOMPATIBLE CHANGE: JceAudioEffectDesc's union gained two members. A tagged union whose job is to hold the parameters of whatever effects exist cannot gain an effect without changing, and the alternative -- parameters as tail members outside the union -- would grow every desc by 52 bytes and abandon the pattern. It does NOT cross the script C ABI (JceAudioEffectDesc appears zero times in jce_script_api.h), which is the one versioned, append-only boundary here; every other consumer is in-tree and rebuilt together, and the SDK installs atomically. (2) global-state 855 -> 856 for the registry, raised with its reason -- and it is ONE object rather than the array-plus-counter it started as, so it costs one entry instead of two and two globals cannot disagree.
WHAT IS STILL DIFFERENT: the built-in COUNT. Unity ships ~15 and Godot ~20; this ships 7. A project wanting a phaser or a spectrum analyser writes it rather than picking it from a list -- but it CAN, which is the difference between a short palette and a closed set, and it is the difference this row was recording.
features.compared: Unity's AudioMixer ships ~15 built-in DSP effects plus a native audio plugin SDK, with effect parameters exposed to snapshots and script. Godot exposes ~20 AudioEffect classes per bus. UE5 has submix effect chains and source effect chains. JCE ships 7 built-ins (EQ, compressor, limiter, delay, chorus, flanger, distortion) plus jce_audio_dsp_register_effect, so a project adds its own and authors it in audio_mixer.json by name like any built-in. The remaining difference is the size of the shipped palette, not whether the set can grow.

features.feature: Adaptive music layers in and out with game intensity
features.evidence:
An unusually complete director exists and reaches nothing. jce_music.h:1-203 specifies vertical stem layering with per-layer [enter,full] intensity bands and fade times, beat/bar-quantized horizontal transitions, and stingers; it is created and ticked by the runtime (engine/src/application/jce_rt_audio.c:803-841), has a MusicTrack scene component with an inspector (jce_scene.h:956-969, editor/src/panels/jce_panel_inspector_audio.cpp:88-104), and is exposed to all five scripting languages (contracts/script-api.json:536, :564). The break is the track data. rt_spawn_music builds the descriptor from jce_music_track_desc_default (rt_audio.c:816-817), and that function memsets the struct and sets layer_count = 0u (engine/src/middleware/audio/jce_music.c:85-94). The authored track_path is dropped: its only readers in the runtime are the two jce_log_write format arguments at rt_audio.c:824 and :830. So every director ever built has zero layers, drives zero mixer buses, and no stems are ever loaded or played. The missing reader is a track-config loader that parses track_path into JceMusicTrackDesc.layers[].
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. The director is created and ticked by the runtime, has a scene component and an inspector, and is exposed to the scripting languages -- and it has no track data to play: nothing in the tree authors or ships a layered music asset for it to read. An unusually complete subsystem whose input format has no producer.
features.compared: Godot 4.3+ ships AudioStreamInteractive (named clips with beat/bar-quantized transitions), AudioStreamPlaylist and AudioStreamSynchronized, all of which actually play audio. UE has MetaSounds plus Quartz for sample-accurate musical scheduling. Unity ships no adaptive music system at all and expects FMOD or Wwise, so JCE's *design* is ahead of Unity's -- but as shipped it makes no sound the way Godot's and UE's do.

features.feature: A script error reports the call stack that led to it
features.evidence:
Every Lua dispatch is a bare pcall with no message handler: engine/src/middleware/script/jce_script.c:694, 957, 996, 1025, 1054, 1068, 1091, 1115 and 1194 all pass 0 as the msgh index, so luaL_traceback is never installed and the error object stays the innermost "chunk:line: message". The single reporting funnel at :911-935 (report_dispatch_error) formats exactly `"%s error: %s"` from lua_tostring and emits it to the host log and LOG_ERROR. A grep for luaL_traceback or lua_getinfo across engine/src/middleware/script/ and scripting/ returns nothing. Python deliberately matches that: scripting/python/jce_script/vm.py:247-251 says "Deliberately not a full traceback: host.log takes a single line in Lua and the lifecycle differential compares those lines", with the real traceback going only to stderr (:330, :382).
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20 by count: eight lua_pcall sites in jce_script.c still pass 0 as the message-handler index, and luaL_traceback appears nowhere in the tree. A script error is still the innermost 'chunk:line: message' with no frames above it.
CLOSED 2026-09-20. All nine dispatch sites now go through script_pcall_tb, which installs a luaL_traceback message handler and removes it afterwards without disturbing the caller's stack layout -- the dispatchers here track their own indices by hand and say so in comments ('inst is under it'), so pushing a handler on top and passing its index would have shifted every one of them. The handler is INSERTED below the function and removed after, which leaves the stack in exactly the shape a pcall(..., 0) did.

THE HANDLER HAS TO RUN WHILE THE STACK IS STILL STANDING, which is why this could not be done in the error path: by the time pcall returns the frames are gone. The report buffer went 512 -> 2048 for the same reason and it is load-bearing -- truncating to 512 cut the trace back to its first frame, which is the one place a handler buys nothing.

MEASURED: a callback raising three frames deep now logs
  on_update error: raiser:2: deliberate failure
  stack traceback:
    [C]: in function 'error'
    raiser:2: in upvalue 'innermost'
    raiser:5: in upvalue 'middle_frame'
    raiser:9: in function <raiser:8>
tests/middleware/script/test_jce_script_stack_trace.c asserts the OUTER frame name, not the header: a handler that ran too late would still print 'stack traceback' over an empty trace. It also asserts a clean dispatch logs no traceback. 3 of 3 mutations red (no handler, handler without luaL_traceback, buffer back to 512).
features.compared: Unity prints the full C# stack trace into the console with each frame clickable. Godot prints a GDScript stack and shows a live stack view in its debugger. Unreal prints a Blueprint callstack or a native stack. In JCE, an error raised three helper functions deep in a Lua script reports the innermost line only, and the process log for the shipped game gets the same single line.

features.feature: Package a build for a platform other than the editor's own
features.evidence:
The editor's package path resolves its target at compile time, not from a user choice. editor/src/core/jce_dist_content_graph.cpp:57-74 returns the target platform from #if JCE_PLATFORM_* and jce_build_manager.cpp:1551 feeds exactly that into the content graph; jce_build_manager.cpp:2727-2731 likewise picks platform_tag by #if. Worse, jce_build_manager.cpp:1350-1370 shader_profile_unreachable() drops shader binaries by the same host #if, so a Windows editor strips essl/essl1/mtl out of any package it stages -- the mobile and web shaders cannot be in a package the Windows editor builds. Only the Bundle Browser exposes a real target choice (editor/src/panels/jce_panel_bundle_browser.cpp:761 combo -> :603 opts.target_platform), and it feeds the bundle packer, not the game package.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. The editor's target still resolves at COMPILE time through #if JCE_PLATFORM_*, so a Windows editor can only package for Windows. Choosing a target is not a setting; it is a rebuild of the editor.
features.compared: Unity's Build Settings switches the active build target and recooks assets/shaders for it from any host; Godot's Export dialog builds any preset's package from any desktop host; UE's BuildCookRun takes -platform= and -targetplatform= explicitly. In JCE the platform is baked into the editor binary.

features.feature: Ship a content patch instead of the whole build
features.evidence:
Built but unwired, at both ends. jce_bundle_pack_diff is declared public at engine/include/jce/resource/jce_bundle_pack.h:174 and implemented at engine/src/resource/jce_bundle_pack.c:2964; the writer emits a jce.bundle.diff document with added/updated/removed arrays at jce_bundle_pack.c:1437-1453. A full-tree grep for jce_bundle_pack_diff returns only the implementation, two comments, and the copies of the header already installed into dist/sdk/* -- no editor button, no jce.py subcommand, no test. The missing readers are equally concrete: nothing anywhere parses JCE_BUNDLE_DIFF_KEY_ADDED/UPDATED/REMOVED, and jce_bundle_loader.c:176 merely tolerates kind=="patch" in a catalog without ever applying a delta. The lower-level pieces exist too and are just as unused: jce_archive_delta_apply (engine/include/jce/resource/jce_archive.h:266) has callers only in tests/os/resource/test_jce_archive.c:1015-1036.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. jce_bundle_pack_diff is public, implemented, and emits a jce.bundle.diff document with added/updated/removed arrays -- and has NO caller anywhere under engine/src, editor/src, tools or scripts. Both ends unwired: nothing produces a patch and nothing applies one.
features.compared: Unity Addressables has a content-update workflow that diffs against addressables_content_state.bin and builds a patch catalog; UE ships patch pak chunks plus ChunkDownloader; Godot supports layered PCKs for patches. JCE has the format, the writer and the delta codec, and no product path that produces or consumes one.

features.feature: Build a server-only binary with no renderer
features.evidence:
Headless works as a runtime mode but not as a build target. engine/src/application/jce_engine.c:660-668 selects headless from the app descriptor or the JCE_HEADLESS environment variable, then inits only SDL_INIT_EVENTS and installs a headless renderer (engine/src/renderer/jce_renderer.c:1282), so a display-less host boots. But grepping engine/, editor/, cmake/, CMakeLists.txt and CMakePresets.json for JCE_SERVER, JCE_DEDICATED and SERVER_BUILD returns nothing, and CMakePresets.json contains no occurrence of "server" or "dedicated" at all -- so the server binary still links bgfx, the renderer and the audio stack and only picks NOOP at runtime. There is also no command-line switch: engine/include/jce/application/jce_args.h exposes exactly three accessors (--dev, --scene, --shader-dir), so a shipped exe cannot be told to go headless except through an env var.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. Headless is a runtime MODE selected from the app descriptor or JCE_HEADLESS, and there is no server target or option in CMakeLists.txt. A display-less host boots the full client binary; it does not build a smaller one.
features.compared: Unity's Dedicated Server is a distinct build target that strips rendering and defines UNITY_SERVER; UE has a Server target type producing a separate binary with rendering compiled out; Godot's dedicated-server export uses a server template and strips visual resources. JCE ships the full client binary and flips a bool.

features.feature: Override an asset's import settings per platform
features.evidence:
Import overrides exist but have no platform dimension. engine/src/resource/jce_bundle_pack.c:717-760 reads a sibling <asset>.import.json and applies a flat set of keys -- target_format, gen_mips, max_size, quality, colorSpace -- with no per-platform section anywhere in the parse. The only platform input is the whole-build opts.target_platform (engine/include/jce/resource/jce_bundle_pack.h:145-151, values Windows/Linux/macOS/Android/iOS/Web/Auto), which feeds jce_cook_auto_texture_format to pick BC on desktop and ASTC on mobile. The consequence is concrete: the moment an artist sets target_format on a hero texture (jce_bundle_pack.c:740-742 overwrites the auto choice), that one format is used for every platform, so an explicit BC7 override survives into an Android build. The runtime only detects the mismatch after the fact -- jce_bundle_loader.c:222-278 rejects a bundle whose target_profile does not match the running platform.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. The .import.json parse still takes a flat key set with no per-platform section; the only platform input is the whole-build option folded into the cache key. A texture cannot be BC7 on desktop and ASTC on mobile from one sidecar.
features.compared: Unity's texture importer has per-platform override tabs (Default/Standalone/Android/iOS), each with its own max size, format and compression quality; UE varies format per platform through device profiles and per-platform texture settings; Godot's importer exposes per-platform VRAM compression choices. JCE has one setting per asset for all platforms.

features.feature: Unused assets stay out of the shipped package
features.evidence:
The packaging path is a directory walk, not a reference walk. editor/src/core/jce_build_manager.cpp:1373-1400 collects assets with collect_asset_walk_cb over jce_fs_host_walk, admitting every file that passes editor/src/core/jce_build_asset_policy.cpp:32-80 -- and that policy is purely name-based (it rejects .git/.github/.idea/.vscode/__pycache__/raw_assets segments, dotfiles, and leaves named agents.md/cmakelists.txt/readme/thumbs.db/desktop.ini). Nothing consults what the scenes actually reference, so an unreferenced 200 MB texture sitting in the assets folder ships. The engine already owns the machinery to do better and only the bundle path uses it: engine/include/jce/resource/jce_bundle_deps.h scans a scene and harvests every asset-path key plus streaming chunk paths, and that scanner is only reachable through jce_bundle_pack, not through the game package build.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. Packaging is still a directory walk admitted by a name-based policy, not a reference walk from the scenes. Everything in the project folder ships, including the assets nothing points at.
features.compared: Unity ships only assets reachable from the included scenes plus Resources/ and Addressables groups; UE cooks strictly by reference from the maps in the packaging list; Godot's export walks resource dependencies and applies include/exclude filters. JCE's default single-exe package ships the folder.

features.feature: CPU profiler shows a zoomable per-thread timeline
features.evidence:
The engine has a real span recorder: engine/include/jce/os/core/jce_trace.h:110-121 declares task_begin/task_end with parent ids, and engine/src/os/core/jce_profiler.c:96-107 pushes every JCE_PROFILE_ZONE_N through a thread-local nesting stack into that ring, so spans really do nest (93 named zones across engine/src + editor/src). The editor consumer, however, renders none of that as a timeline: editor/src/panels/jce_panel_profiler_trace.cpp:545 calls only draw_summary/draw_gpu_scene/draw_counters/draw_threads/draw_work_items, and every one of those is an ImGui::BeginTable (:381, :409, :469) — there is no time axis, no lane per thread, no zoom, and the completed-span deque flattens nesting (:26 caps it at 2048). The nearest thing to a breakdown is a flat top-14 bar list of jce_perf_phase buckets at editor/src/panels/jce_panel_profiler.cpp:835-880. So the missing reader is a time-axis/flame renderer over spans the ring already carries; today you must export and open the trace elsewhere.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. The span recorder is real and nests correctly, and nothing in editor/src reads task spans -- no consumer of jce_trace's task_begin/task_end anywhere in the editor. The data is recorded into a ring that only a crash dump ever reads.
features.compared: Unity's Profiler Timeline view draws per-thread lanes with nested ProfilerMarker scopes you can zoom and click; Unreal Insights' Timing view does the same over TRACE_CPUPROFILER_EVENT_SCOPE with parent/child hierarchy. Godot 4's script profiler is a flat sortable function list, so JCE's tables are roughly Godot-level and behind both Unity and UE.

features.feature: See GPU milliseconds spent in each render pass
features.evidence:
The data path is complete: engine/src/renderer/jce_lowlevel.c:270-282 copies bgfx per-view cpu/gpu begin/end into JceViewStats (engine/include/jce/renderer/jce_lowlevel.h:239-247), views are named (bgfx_set_view_name at engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_scene_renderer.c:3417-3424, jce_scene_pick.c:850, jce_postfx.c:660), and the editor sorts them into a table shared by the Profiler and Frame Debugger tabs. But bgfx only fills per-view GPU timers when BGFX_DEBUG_PROFILER is set, and engine/src/renderer/jce_renderer.c:1095-1106 sets it only when Tracy is compiled in or getenv("JCE_PERF_LOG") is non-NULL at renderer init — there is no in-editor toggle, and the panel itself tells you to relaunch: editor/src/panels/jce_panel_profiler.cpp:370-376 prints 'start with JCE_PERF_LOG=1 (enables BGFX_DEBUG_PROFILER)'. The per-view draw-count column is also dead: editor/src/panels/jce_panel_profiler.cpp:112 sets r.draws = 0 with the comment 'per-view draw count not in this stats struct', so that column always reads 0.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20, and the panel still says so itself: jce_panel_profiler.cpp:375 prints 'JCE_PERF_LOG=1 (enables BGFX_DEBUG_PROFILER)', so per-view GPU timers require a RELAUNCH with an environment variable and there is no in-editor toggle. The per-view stats ARE surfaced (jce_panel_profiler.cpp:106 reads JceViewStats) -- the gap is that they are empty unless you knew to set the variable before starting.
features.compared: Unreal's ProfileGPU / GPU Visualizer gives a hierarchical per-pass GPU breakdown on demand with no restart; Unity's GPU Usage profiler module and Godot 4's Visual Profiler both show per-pass CPU/GPU milliseconds from a button in the running editor. JCE requires deciding to profile before process launch.

features.feature: Developer console for tweaking variables in a running game
features.evidence:
The registry is complete and public: engine/include/jce/os/core/jce_console.h declares typed cvars with flags/help/enumeration (:47-80), a command registry (:86), an output sink, and a parser at :102 (jce_console_exec) that handles 'name' to echo and 'name value' to set. 18 cvars are actually registered — r.forwardplus, r.point_shadows, r.taa, r.gpu_driven, r.upscaler and friends at engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_scene_renderer.c:1996-2115 and jce_sr_shadow.c:401-1582, plus time_scale/paused/master_volume at engine/src/application/jce_runtime.c:3558-3564. But the only interactive reader in the tree is the editor: editor/src/panels/jce_panel_console.cpp:286 is the sole jce_console_exec caller and :318 the sole jce_console_set_output caller. jce_cvar_set_from_string (jce_console.h:71) has no caller at all outside jce_console.c, so there is no command-line or ini override path either, and script-api.json exposes no console binding. A shipped game gets an FPS/frametime overlay (engine/include/jce/middleware/ui/jce_ui_debug_hud.h, consumed by caged_kingdom/src/game/ck_app.c:184) but no console. Missing readers: a runtime console overlay, a '+set name value' launch path, and a script binding.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. jce_console_exec still has exactly one interactive caller and it is the editor's console panel; there is no runtime console overlay, no '+set name value' launch path, and no script binding. A shipped game gets the FPS overlay and no way to change a cvar.
TRACED 2026-09-21, and one of the three missing readers is a DECISION the engine already made in writing. The row says a "'+set name value' launch path" is missing, which reads as an oversight. First, the correction to the premise: argv is NOT dropped. engine/src/application/jce_main_sdl.c:42 is the real main (SDL_AppInit) and forwards to jce_engine.c:548 jce_engine_create(argc, argv), whose FIRST act at :552 is jce_args_stash(argc, argv) -- "so any subsystem init below can read launch flags through jce_args_* without each one re-parsing argv". jce_default_main.inc.h has zero argc/argv because it is the app BODY, not main; JCE_MAIN() emits only jce_app_get_desc. So a launch-flag facility exists and runs before everything. WHAT IT HAS IS FOUR TYPED GETTERS, and their callers are the real finding: jce_args_has_dev has NO caller anywhere in the repository; jce_args_get_startup_scene and jce_args_get_shader_dev_dir are called ONLY by caged_kingdom/src/game/ck_app.c; only jce_args_get_dev_assets has an engine caller (jce_material_registry.c). So `--scene foo` does nothing for a game built on the engine's own default main. AND THE REASON IS NOT NEGLECT. jce_default_main.inc.h resolves the startup scene from the ENVIRONMENT first -- the getenv is at :482, under a rationale comment at :466-480 -- JCE_STARTUP_SCENE -- with a comment that gives the rationale and names the siblings: "Same shape as the other JCE_* debug toggles (JCE_MAX_FRAMES, JCE_INPUT_REPLAY, JCE_MULTI_INSTANCE) -- it is a developer/QA lever". It even explains the ordering: placed FIRST because the manifest path is non-NULL for every real project, so an override checked after it would never fire. => Adding `+set name value` would be a THIRD mechanism for launch-time configuration, beside a wired-and-documented env-var idiom and a half-wired argv facility. That is a decision to make, not a wire to reconnect, and it has an ordering hazard of its own: cvars are registered LATE (jce_scene_renderer.c:1996-2115, jce_sr_shadow.c:401-1582, jce_runtime.c:3558-3564) while jce_args_stash runs at engine create, so any launch-time apply must run after registration or be a deferred value the registry pulls when the cvar appears -- and jce_cvar_set_from_string still has no caller outside jce_console.c, so nothing in the tree demonstrates either shape. THE OVERLAY, by contrast, is the row's own feature sentence and needs nothing new. The template is exact and already consumed by a shipped game: jce_ui_debug_hud.{h,c} + engine/ui/engine_debug_hud.rml, loaded at jce_ui_debug_hud.c:131 and used by caged_kingdom/src/game/ck_app.c:184. The runtime UI is RML and already has every piece -- jce_ui_process_input(ctx, input) feeds the keyboard in (jce_ui.h:180), jce_ui_elem_get_value/set_value are form input (:111/:112), jce_ui_elem_on registers handlers (:171), jce_ui_elem_set_inner_rml writes an output pane (:130) -- and jce_input_text() has existed on the runtime input struct all along (jce_input.h:96). So the text-entry half I expected to be expensive is already there, and what is missing is the document, the toggle and the wiring to jce_console_exec / jce_console_set_output. => The three missing readers are three units, not one: the OVERLAY (this row's feature sentence, and the whole of the gap `compared` names), the LAUNCH PATH (blocked on the env-vs-argv decision above), and the SCRIPT BINDING (a third axis). Close what is closed.
LANDED 2026-09-21, and the row stays `behind` because a shipped game still has no console -- that is the overlay, and it is the unit that is left. What landed is the half underneath it, and tracing turned up a worse finding than the row's own: THE ENTIRE INTROSPECTION SURFACE HAD NEVER HAD A PRODUCT READER. jce_cvar_at, jce_cvar_help and jce_cvar_flags had no caller anywhere in the repository; jce_cvar_count, jce_cvar_format_value and jce_console_register_cmd were reached only by their own unit test. The header's opening sentence says a console UI "can list and mutate by name at runtime" -- mutating had a reader, listing did not, and the sentence is what makes that invisible. UNDERNEATH THAT, A SECOND ONE: `help` and `list` were an if-branch inside jce_console_exec, so they WORKED WITHOUT EXISTING -- absent from the command table, so `help` did not list itself (on a fresh registry it printed "commands (0)" while being a command) and nothing enumerating the table could offer them. They are now ordinary registered commands and the special case is deleted; one table answers "what commands exist" for every reader. AND A THIRD, in the editor: jce_panel_console.cpp intercepted `help` before the registry and printed a HARDCODED list -- "Commands: clear, help, echo <msg>, play, stop, pause, list" -- which named only its own if-chain and could never mention a registered command. That chain also matched on PREFIX (strncmp(cmd,"help",4) fired for "helpme"), and its five editor commands were invisible to any enumeration. They are registered now; exec dispatches everything; the engine's `help` lists them beside every cvar. WHAT IS NEW: jce_console_session.h/.c -- the line, the history (Up/Down, with the draft restored when you step off the newest, and a rejected line still recorded because a typo is what Up is for) and Tab completion over the live registry; plus jce_console_cmd_count/_at so completion covers commands and not just cvars. The editor's console panel consumes it, so the editor now has the autocomplete the `compared` field credits UE with. IT IS A SEPARATE OBJECT FROM ANY OVERLAY ON PURPOSE: jce_ui_create requires a JceRenderer for bgfx draws and NO test in the tree creates a JceUIContext, so the runtime UI layer has no headless coverage at all. A console written straight onto jce_ui.h would ship with nothing that runs in jce.py test. The session renders nothing, and its 16 cases run headlessly -- including the one that matters: when more names match than the match list can hold, the common prefix must still be folded over ALL of them, because folding it over the stored subset yields a LONGER prefix and Tab then writes a name that does not exist, only once a project has enough cvars to overflow. STILL MISSING, and each is its own unit: the overlay (blocked on nothing -- jce_ui has every piece, jce_ui_process_input/elem_get_value/elem_on/set_inner_rml, and jce_ui_debug_hud.{h,c}+engine/ui/engine_debug_hud.rml is the template a shipped game already consumes); the launch path (blocked on the env-vs-argv decision recorded above); and the script binding.
THE OVERLAY LANDED 2026-09-22, and the row is STILL BEHIND -- on a different sentence than before, so here is exactly which.
WHAT NOW EXISTS. jce_console_shell (os/platform) is the console's whole behaviour: the line, history, Tab completion over the live registry, a 256-line scrollback ring, and which keys are consumed. jce_ui_console_overlay (middleware/ui) + engine/ui/engine_console_overlay.rml draw one, following jce_ui_debug_hud exactly -- an engine-owned RML document loaded from the PAK -- and contain no logic at all. AND THE ENGINE'S OWN DEFAULT MAIN CREATES A SHELL under --dev, so a shipped game built on it can open a console, type, complete names, walk its history and change any registered cvar. Output goes to the log on that path.
THAT --dev GATE IS THE FIRST CALLER jce_args_has_dev HAS EVER HAD. It has been public and implemented since argv stashing landed with NO caller anywhere in the repository -- a fact recorded in this row's own earlier tracing. A console always on in a shipped game is the wrong default (it takes the tilde key from every player); a console nobody can open is the state this row describes.
THE SPLIT WAS FORCED, NOT CHOSEN, and it is the useful finding. The first version was ONE object that both edited a line and drew it. Its test would not LINK: linking jce_ui drags RmlUi in, and RmlUi's prebuilt objects reference an MSVC STL symbol this toolchain does not provide (__std_find_first_of_trivial_pos_1). So the untestable half was not a design preference -- the toolchain refused to build a test of it at all. Splitting put every decision in os/platform beside JceInput, where tests/os/platform/test_jce_console_shell.c exercises it headlessly, 10 cases. The load-bearing two: an OPEN console must consume input and a CLOSED one must not (either half alone is satisfied by a handler that always answers the same), and scrollback index 0 must stay the OLDEST line after the ring wraps -- invisible until a session prints more than the ring holds, i.e. one `list` over a few hundred cvars.
A DEFECT THE INPUT HEADER HAD ALREADY NAMED. Backspace and the history keys bind to jce_input_key_REPEATED, not _pressed. jce_input.h documents the strict rising edge as "correct for a jump button, wrong for text editing, where holding Backspace must keep deleting", and records that it already made "the shipped runtime's InputField delete one byte where the editor's deleted the line". Writing a cvar name wrong and holding Backspace is the most common thing that happens in a console.
AND THE TEST'S OWN HARNESS WAS WRONG FIRST: it sent key-down and never a key-up, so the second press of the toggle was not an edge and the console appeared not to close -- while Backspace, on _repeated, kept working and hid the pattern. A test that never releases a key is measuring a key nobody let go of.
WHY STILL BEHIND, precisely: a game on the engine's DEFAULT MAIN gets the console's behaviour but NOT a console on screen, because that path creates a scene renderer and no JceUIContext -- standing RmlUi up in every shipped game is a real cost and a separate decision. A game that already has a UI context (as it would for the debug HUD, which is likewise engine-provided and game-instantiated) adds jce_console_overlay_create and sees it. Beyond that, the two other readers this row named are unchanged: the LAUNCH PATH (`+set name value` / ini overrides, still blocked on the env-vs-argv decision recorded above) and the SCRIPT BINDING. Against Unreal's four -- editor console, development-build console, -ExecCmds/ini overrides, autocomplete -- this is two and a half.
features.compared: Unreal's cvar console is the reference: tilde console in editor and in development/shipping-with-console builds, plus -ExecCmds and ini overrides and autocomplete over thousands of cvars. Unity has no cvar system but ships a Development Build console overlay. Godot has no console either. JCE has UE's registry design with only Unity-editor-level reach.

features.feature: See which replicated objects and RPCs consume bandwidth
features.evidence:
What exists is transport-level only. engine/include/jce/middleware/net/jce_net.h:114-125 defines JceNetPeerStats as exactly five fields — rtt_ms, packets_sent, packets_lost, bytes_in, bytes_out — and engine/src/middleware/net/jce_net.c:379-394 fills them straight from ENetPeer counters. The editor panel builds 60-second rolling plots on top of that (editor/src/panels/jce_panel_network_stats.cpp:26-40) but its table has six columns: id, address, rtt, in, out, loss (:159-166). I checked the replication layer for finer accounting: engine/include/jce/middleware/net/jce_replication.h has no stats struct at all, and engine/include/jce/middleware/net/jce_session.h:186-189 just forwards the same JceNetPeerStats. So there is no per-entity, per-component or per-RPC byte attribution, and no way to answer 'which replicated thing is costing me bandwidth'.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. JceNetPeerStats is still the five transport counters (rtt, packets sent/lost, bytes in/out) filled straight from ENet. Nothing attributes a byte to a replicated object, so 'which entity is costing the bandwidth' has no answer.
features.compared: Unreal's Networking Insights and the legacy network profiler break bandwidth down per actor, per property and per RPC over time. Unity's Netcode for GameObjects ships profiler modules that attribute bytes sent/received to individual objects and messages. Godot 4's Network Profiler lists incoming/outgoing RPC bandwidth per node. All three answer the per-object question JCE cannot.

features.feature: Erosion and talus generators shape the heightmap
features.evidence:
engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_terrain.h:192-224 exposes jce_terrain_apply_erosion (gully carving, optional ridge mask out) and :226-256 jce_terrain_apply_thermal (angle-of-repose talus, mass-conserving). Both are wired: editor/src/panels/jce_panel_terrain.cpp:858-882 and :890-903 are real buttons with undo capture, and the terrain panel writes the result back through the shared terrain object. The header itself states the gully pass 'is a plausible-looking EROSION-STYLE FILTER, not a hydrology simulation... no water volume, no sediment transport and no connectivity between gullies' (:197-202), so there is no hydraulic/flow-accumulation erosion. Both are whole-grid one-shot passes, not brushes, and engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_terrain.c:1590 refuses them outright on a tiled or procedural terrain.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. Hydraulic gully carving and thermal talus both exist and are real editor buttons with undo capture. What is absent is the generator GRAPH -- there is no node stack, no reorderable operator list, no way to re-run a recipe on a resized terrain. Each button is a destructive one-shot on the current heightmap.
features.compared: Unity's Terrain Tools package ships hydraulic, thermal and wind erosion as paintable brushes with per-brush masks. UE Landscape has Erosion, Hydro Erosion and Noise sculpt tools plus Landmass/edit-layer blueprint brushes that re-run non-destructively. Godot ships no terrain system at all, so JCE is ahead of Godot and behind both Unity and UE here.

features.feature: Baked sky occlusion darkens canyon floors
features.evidence:
BUILT-BUT-UNWIRED. engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_terrain.h:258-295 exposes jce_terrain_bake_sky_occlusion (cosine-weighted visibility plus bent normals) and jce_terrain_sample_sky_visibility. The bake runs: editor/src/panels/jce_panel_terrain.cpp:908-916 fills s.sky_visibility, a panel-local std::vector<float> declared at :128. Its ONLY consumer is ImGui::Text at :918-928 printing min/max/mean. jce_terrain_sample_sky_visibility (engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_terrain.c:1546) has zero callers in engine/src or editor/src, and the .terrain side-car layout at engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_terrain.c:592-613 is header + heights + splat + optional hole mask only, so the field is never serialised and dies when the panel closes. Missing readers: a serialiser into the side-car, and any terrain/ambient shader path that multiplies sky ambient by it.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. jce_terrain_sample_sky_visibility is defined in jce_terrain.c and called by nothing under engine/src -- the bake fills a panel-local vector and no renderer, no shader and no runtime query reads the result. Built-but-unwired at the consumer end.
features.compared: Unity's Progressive Lightmapper bakes terrain into lightmaps with ambient occlusion that ships with the scene. UE bakes landscape AO into lightmaps, or resolves it at runtime via DFAO/Lumen. Godot's LightmapGI bakes AO over any mesh including terrain plugins. All three deliver the darkened canyon floor to a shipped build; JCE's bake reaches an ImGui label.

features.feature: Plants placed by altitude band and ridge-vs-crease
features.evidence:
BUILT-BUT-UNWIRED at three points. The rules exist and work: engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_foliage.h:95-127 documents height_min/height_max and ridge_field/ridge_min/ridge_max as the two axes that 'replace most hand-painted density masks', and engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_foliage.c:133-135, :176-180 and :187 implement the rejections. Nothing sets them. The renderer memsets the params and its own comment at engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_sr_environment.c:771-778 says 'this path never sets' ridge_*; the grass path repeats it at :1598-1604; the editor bake at editor/src/panels/jce_panel_inspector_gameplay.cpp:620-628 sets only seed/density/area/slope/scale/normals. The producer is equally cut: editor/src/panels/jce_panel_terrain.cpp:871-872 bakes the ridge mask into a panel-local vector (declared :129) and only prints its sample count at :930-931, and the file format that could carry it is never populated -- tools/jce_cook.c:641-643 passes NULL for the ridge argument so JCE_TERRAIN_CH_RIDGE is never set (engine/src/resource/jce_terrain_format.c:608-615), and jce_terrain_read_tile_ridge (:507) has no caller: engine/src/resource/jce_terrain_source.c:134 reads heights only. Missing readers: a scatter-component field carrying the bands, and a loader handing the ridge plane to the scatter.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20 -- see world.foliage.density-paint-brush for the carrier that bounds both: the scatter is driven by a 64x64 density mask and slope/altitude thresholds, not by an authored rule graph.
features.compared: UE's PCG framework (5.2+) filters scatter points by height, slope and curvature attributes, and Landscape Grass Types filter by layer weight. Unity's Terrain Tools ships a height/slope filter stack for detail scatter. Godot has neither. In JCE only max_slope_deg actually reaches the scatter, so a treeline or a scree band cannot be expressed as a rule.

features.feature: Sculpt a streamed multi-kilometre terrain in the editor
features.evidence:
engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_terrain.h:88-124 gives tiled and procedural terrains with LRU-capped residency and camera prefetch, and states plainly that 'Only the RUNTIME READ path (sample / raycast / collision / chunk-mesh build) is tile-aware; authoring (sculpt / import / export) requires a monolithic terrain'. The editor honours that by refusing: editor/src/panels/jce_panel_terrain.cpp:842-846 bails to a 'needResidentTerrain' label before any brush or generator is drawn, and engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_terrain.c:1297, :1521, :1590 and :1668 all early-return for a tiled grid. The only way to get one is hand-editing '"procedural": true' into a .terrain.json (engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_terrain.c:663-671); there is no editor path that creates a tiled terrain.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20. Nothing under editor/src authors a tiled terrain -- no tile-authoring panel, no create_tiled call. Streamed tiles are a runtime format a tool would have to produce, and the tool is the gap.
features.compared: Unity authors large terrain as a grid of Terrain tiles, each individually sculptable and each independently loadable. UE Landscape splits into streaming proxies under World Composition/World Partition that you sculpt in place at full size. Godot has no terrain. In JCE a terrain is either authorable or streamable, never both.

features.feature: Paint foliage density onto the ground with a brush
features.evidence:
Fully wired, but coarse. editor/src/panels/jce_panel_inspector_gameplay.cpp:292-297 describes the brush; :318-332 gate it on the focused entity's density_paint_active, :359-393 stamp a radial falloff into vs->density_paint, and :397-411 open a batched undo per stroke. The scene view drives it by raycasting the terrain (editor/src/panels/jce_panel_scene_view.cpp:2345, :2393-2423), and the renderer consumes the grid as JceFoliageScatterParams.density_mask at engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_sr_environment.c:809-810. The limit is the carrier: engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_scene.h:1172 fixes JCE_VEG_PAINT_DIM at 64, so the grid is 64x64 over the whole area rect regardless of size -- a 500 m field paints at ~8 m granularity -- and the brush modulates a probabilistic scatter rather than placing or erasing individual instances.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20 at the constant. JCE_VEG_PAINT_DIM is still 64 (jce_scene.h:1367) and the grid still covers the whole area rect, so a 500 m field paints at roughly 8 m granularity. The brush is fully wired -- scene-view raycast, radial falloff stamp, batched undo per stroke, consumed as JceFoliageScatterParams.density_mask -- and it modulates a probabilistic scatter rather than placing or erasing instances.
features.compared: Unity Terrain paints details/trees against a detailResolution configurable up to 4096, and tree painting places real instances you can also single-click. UE Foliage mode paints, erases, fills, lassos and single-instance-selects actual instances with no grid quantisation. Godot ships no foliage painter at all.

features.feature: One wind source drives grass, trees, cloth and weather
features.evidence:
A global wind exists and is now authorable: engine/include/jce/middleware/world/jce_environment.h:74-75 carries wind_direction_ws and wind_speed_mps, editor/src/panels/jce_panel_lighting_settings.cpp:760-780 authors the direction into JceSceneRenderingSettings, and engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_scene_environment.c:114-118 normalises it into the environment. But it only reaches two consumers -- cloud drift (engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_sr_environment.c:4390-4393) and the rain/snow overlay (:4435-4436). Grass takes the SPEED only and keeps its own direction, with an in-code justification at :1799-1811 that is now stale ('The environment's direction is a default that nothing authors'). Cloth is fully independent: engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_scene.c:3279-3293 pushes the per-component JceClothComponent::wind_velocity straight to jce_cloth_set_wind with no environment input. And trees/foliage have no wind at all -- JceVegetationScatterComponent (engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_scene.h:1173-1201) has no wind member, so scattered trees never sway.
CONFIRMED 2026-09-20, and the verification nearly produced a FALSE REFUTATION worth recording. A first pass matched wind_dir / wind_speed / wind_amplitude 'inside' JceVegetationScatterComponent and was about to refute the row -- but the pattern had run from a MENTION of that name in a comment to the next closing brace, which belongs to JceGrassFieldComponent. Slicing the struct body precisely gives the real answer: JceVegetationScatterComponent contains the string 'wind' ZERO times. Scattered trees still never sway, grass still takes the environment's speed but keeps its own direction, cloth is still fed per-component with no environment input, and the global wind still reaches only cloud drift and the rain/snow overlay. There is no wind zone or wind volume type anywhere.
features.compared: Unity's WindZone is a scene object whose direction, main strength and turbulence drive terrain grass, terrain trees and every SpeedTree asset from one place. UE's Wind Directional Source feeds foliage world-position-offset, cloth and Niagara together. Godot has no wind system whatsoever. JCE has four winds that need not agree, and the one an author can set reaches only clouds and rain.

features.feature: Sun shadow cascades follow the camera without swimming
features.evidence:
engine/include/jce/renderer/jce_csm.h:62-74 declares jce_csm_compute(cascade_count 1..4, split_lambda, caster AABB) and returns per-cascade VP plus a bounding sphere (center/radius, csm.h:32-33) used for caster culling. engine/src/renderer/jce_csm.c:139-150 snaps each cascade centre onto a world-anchored light-space texel grid (texel_size = radius*2/map_size, floor(+0.5)), which is the standard anti-swim fix. The real call site is engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_sr_shadow.c:1939, guarded by a change key (csm_key at 1946-1962) so an unchanged camera reuses last_csm. Consumption is wired: engine/shaders/pbr/fs_pbr_body.sh:786-800 cross-fades into the next cascade over a blend band and :843-848 fades shadows out over the last 15% of shadow_far. Designer-facing knobs (shadow_distance, cascade_count, split_lambda, shadow_resolution) live on JceSceneRenderingComponent (engine/include/jce/middleware/scene/jce_scene.h:291-295) and are edited at editor/src/panels/jce_panel_lighting_settings.cpp:396-421.
VERIFIED 2026-09-20: the consumer this row names was re-checked against today's tree and exists. Not behaviourally A/B'd against Unity/Unreal/Godot -- the call rests on the cited wiring reaching the shipped runtime, and a row that turns out narrower than its title gets split rather than quietly kept.
jce_csm_compute is named by six files including the renderer and a lint that asserts its per-cascade depth-range-per-texel contract (tools/lint/check_shadow_bias_units.py, added 2026-09-20) -- so this row now has a machine reader as well as a human one.
features.compared: Unity URP/HDRP: 1-4 cascades, cascade split sliders, stable fit, cascade blend, shadow distance fade. UE: dynamic shadow cascades with distance fade and transition. Godot 4: DirectionalLight3D 1-4 splits, blend splits, fade start. JCE has all four knobs plus texel snapping and a per-cascade caster-sphere cull; it does not offer UE's per-cascade resolution override.

features.feature: Spot lights use a real IES photometric profile
features.evidence:
engine/include/jce/renderer/jce_ies_profile.h:48-59 parses IES LM-63 (TILT=NONE) and bakes a 256-sample candela LUT; :84 adds jce_ies_lut_for_path, a bake-once path cache whose own docstring (:65-79) records that this header previously had ZERO callers while JceSpotLight already carried ies_path and ies_lut_texture -- i.e. it was the classic unwired field and has since been fixed. It is wired now: engine/src/middleware/scene/jce_sr_draw.c:3717-3718 resolves ies_path through the cache into the descriptor, engine/src/renderer/jce_lighting_system.c:447-451 binds it to s_iesLut, and engine/shaders/pbr/fs_pbr_body.sh:215 declares that sampler on stage 14. Two real limits: only the FIRST spot with a valid LUT is bound per frame (jce_lighting_system.c:447 'if (ies_spot < 0 ...)'), and the Forward+ variant drops IES entirely because stage 14 becomes s_cluster (fs_pbr_body.sh:204-213 and :1218).
VERIFIED 2026-09-20: the consumer this row names was re-checked against today's tree and exists. Not behaviourally A/B'd against Unity/Unreal/Godot -- the call rests on the cited wiring reaching the shipped runtime, and a row that turns out narrower than its title gets split rather than quietly kept.
The header's own docstring records that it once had ZERO callers while JceSpotLight already carried ies_path; that is exactly the shape this refutation pass exists to catch, and it is the previous state, not the current one -- jce_ies_profile is named by six engine files today.
features.compared: UE: IES profiles on any point/spot light, all lights simultaneously. Unity HDRP: IES import and per-light assignment; built-in/URP have none. Godot 4: no IES support. JCE parses and applies real photometric data, which beats URP and Godot, but only one light in the frame can use it, and a project on Forward+ clustered lighting loses it silently.

features.feature: The final image is dithered so smooth gradients do not band
features.evidence:
Wired on both output paths and each fires exactly once. On the HDR path fs_composite.sc:153-166 adds a screen-space hash of ~1/255 after tone mapping and after the 3D LUT grade, gated on the tonemap flag (u_compositeFlags.y, set at jce_postfx.c:1678) because that pass is the real 8-bit quantisation point. features.feature: A script that errors every frame reports once, then goes quiet
features.evidence:
engine/include/jce/middleware/script/jce_script.h:741-812 states THE FAILING-CALLBACK RULE -- a raising lifecycle callback is caught, logged, and then disabled on that instance only, with the exact re-enable conditions (hot reload or respawn) and three named exclusions each justified. It is implemented, not just documented: engine/src/middleware/script/jce_script.c:895-935 stores the disable mask in the instance's own metatable (so a recycled luaL_ref cannot inherit a dead instance's disables) and emits the fixed notice from jce_script.h:822-825. It is mirrored in Python (scripting/python/jce_script/vm.py:136, 434-448, cleared on rebind at :608), C++ (scripting/cpp/src/jce_script_vm_cpp.c:345) and Java (scripting/java/native/jce_script_vm_java.c:605), and pinned by three cross-language lifecycle differentials. The honest gap: C# and JS do not implement it -- scripting/csharp/managed/JceScript/JceEntityScript.cs:12-15 says outright "it does not disable itself either, so the message repeats until it is fixed", and searching scripting/js/ and scripting/csharp/ for the notice text finds nothing.

features.feature: An infinite loop in a script aborts instead of hanging the editor
features.evidence:
engine/src/middleware/script/jce_script.c:763 sets a 40,000,000-instruction budget; :816-833 installs it as a LUA_MASKCOUNT hook whose handler (:806-811) raises "script watchdog: call exceeded %d instructions (infinite loop?)" out of the enclosing pcall, so a runaway dispatch becomes an ordinary caught error rather than a hard hang of the single-threaded loop. It is genuinely armed on every entry point, not just one: :328 and :1151 (coroutine resume), :693 (module run), :956, :995, :1020 (lifecycle), :1067, :1090, :1114 (named globals) and :1193 (hot-reload rebind), each re-arming for a fresh budget. JCE_SCRIPT_WATCHDOG_INSTR overrides it and the literal string "off" disables it (:802-812). The limit: it is Lua-only -- grepping scripting/ for "watchdog" across the C, C++, C#, Java, JS and Python backends returns nothing.
VERIFIED 2026-09-20: the consumer this row names was re-checked against today's tree and exists. Not behaviourally A/B'd against Unity/Unreal/Godot -- the call rests on the cited wiring reaching the shipped runtime, and a row that turns out narrower than its title gets split rather than quietly kept.
The 40,000,000-instruction LUA_MASKCOUNT budget is in jce_script.c and the crash handler knows about it. A prior campaign in this tree recorded that raising this budget is NOT the fix for a script that needs longer -- 400 million was still cut -- so the number is a watchdog, not a quota.
features.compared: None of the three has this. `while true: pass` in a Godot _process hangs the editor; the same in a Unity Update hangs the Unity editor and the usual advice is to kill the process; an infinite Blueprint loop trips Unreal's own infinite-loop guard only for Blueprint bytecode, not for C++. JCE's guard covers authored Lua including coroutine bodies.

features.feature: The same commit rebuilds to the same bytes
features.evidence:
CMakeLists.txt:1380-1423 targets byte-identical Release output on purpose: MSVC gets /Brepro plus /INCREMENTAL:NO to kill the link-time PE timestamp, and /d1trimfile:${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/ to strip absolute paths out of __FILE__; the else branch at :1424-1428 uses -ffile-prefix-map and -fdebug-prefix-map for Clang/GCC. The other non-deterministic input is handled at CMakeLists.txt:86-100, where the embedded build timestamp is taken from the HEAD committer date under TZ=UTC rather than the wall clock. editor/CMakeLists.txt:238-241 hashes the linked editor into jce_editor_sha256.txt via tools/write_sha256.cmake. Caveat I checked and did not find: nothing builds twice and compares -- the hash is emitted and later just copied into the package (jce.py:1833), never verified against a previous build, so the flags are right but no gate proves the property holds.

features.feature: Players can drop in mod archives that override assets
features.evidence:
A first-class, sandboxed mod loader is in the public umbrella: engine/include/jce/api_resource.h:40 pulls in jce_mod_loader.h, whose header (:1-46) documents scanning a mods directory for *.jpak/*.jmod, reading a per-mod manifest for id/name/version/load_order/enabled, and mounting the enabled ones as override layers where last-added wins. engine/src/resource/jce_mod_loader.c:130-202 reads the manifest from an in-archive mod.json and then a sibling <stem>.mod.json that overrides it, and :440-466 builds the layer stack over an optional base archive. The threat model is explicit and enforced: mods are data only, path lookups go through jce_archive_normalize_path so "../../system/x" cannot escape, and discovery never runs from engine boot. The archive format has a real producer -- tools/jce_pak.c:1469-1515 writes JPAK v1 -- and the loader is covered by tests/os/resource/test_jce_mod_loader.c:118-220. What is missing is authoring convenience: no editor panel builds or manages mods.

features.feature: Sample where native code actually spends time, uninstrumented
features.evidence:
engine/src/os/core/jce_sampler.c is a real PC sampling profiler: a worker thread suspends the profiled thread at a fixed rate, reads its instruction pointer, and histograms it keyed on (thread, pc) (:44-53), symbolising with dbghelp and reporting percentage/count/function/line ranges at :596-599. It is armed by JCE_SAMPLER=<hz> (:249), with JCE_SAMPLER_ALL for a whole-process sweep (:255), JCE_SAMPLER_DELAY warm-up (:258) and JCE_SAMPLER_OUT (:262); the engine calls jce_sampler_init at engine/src/application/jce_engine.c:588 and jce_sampler_shutdown at :2604. features.feature: World-space transform accessors (Transform.position vs localPosition)
features.compared:
Unity: Transform.position / rotation / lossyScale beside localPosition /
localRotation / localScale, plus SetPositionAndRotation.  Unreal:
GetWorldLocation / SetWorldLocation beside GetRelativeLocation.  Godot:
Node3D.global_position / global_transform beside position / transform.  All
three treat the world pose as the PRIMARY accessor and the local one as the
qualified case; this scene had only the qualified one, which is why every
consumer that needed a place read an offset instead.
features.evidence:
WAS ABSENT, AND ITS ABSENCE WAS LOAD-BEARING.

Unity exposes Transform.position beside localPosition, UE has
GetWorldLocation beside GetRelativeLocation, Godot has global_position
beside position.  This scene had only the local half.
jce_scene_get_world_matrix composed the parent chain, but it composes a
MODEL matrix for rendering -- it carries JcePivotComponent's offset and
returns a mat4, not a pose -- so every non-rendering consumer read the raw
JceTransform instead.  For a child that is an offset from its parent, not a
place.  "Put it where the door is" could not be written.

jce_scene_get_world_pose / jce_scene_set_world_pose / jce_scene_solve_local_pose.

THE SOLVE IS THE PRIMITIVE AND THE SETTER IS BUILT ON IT, because the
physics write-back runs for every non-static body every frame and mutates
Transforms IN PLACE on purpose: jce_scene_set_transform calls ecs_set_ptr
and bumps the entity subtree's world-cache generation, which is what the
in-place design plus jce_scene_notify_physics_writeback_entity exists to
avoid.  A hot-path caller asks for the numbers and writes them itself, and
there is still exactly one place that knows the world->local math -- the
same composition jce_scene_reparent has used since it was written.

A ROOT IS VERBATIM IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.  jce_m4_from_trs -> jce_m4_decompose
costs three sqrtf and does not return what it consumed, so routing every
entity through a matrix would leave every unparented scene -- which is every
scene authored before this -- approximately where it was authored.  Asserted
with EQUAL_MEMORY, because EQUAL_FLOAT passes on a round-trip.

THE ENTITY'S OWN PIVOT IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED.  A pivot is a model-matrix
offset that decides where a mesh draws and which point a gizmo turns about;
Unity's Transform has no such field, so excluding it is what makes this
Transform.position rather than a second model matrix.

MEASURED: tests/middleware/scene/test_jce_scene_world_pose.c, 7 of 7 --
IN the tree: tests/ is tracked on this branch (562 files), which is the
opposite of what every test header here claimed.

features.feature: A physics body on a child entity simulates at its world pose
features.compared:
Unity, Unreal and Godot all simulate a body at its world pose regardless of
where it sits in the hierarchy, and convert back into the parent's space on
write-back.  Unity's documented caution about parenting a Rigidbody to a
moving object is about the transform hierarchy WINNING on the frame the
parent moves -- which presumes the body follows its parent at all.  Here it
did not: it sat at its local offset from the world origin, so the caution
had no counterpart and neither did the behaviour it cautions about.
features.evidence:
WAS BEHIND, AND IT WAS THE SAME CONFUSION IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.

Reported by a peer session with a four-row A/B: a trigger volume parented to
a door at x=4 and authored at local x=0 measured BIT-IDENTICAL to the same
trigger with no parent at all -- same penetration to six digits, same 1221
contacts.  The authored volume sat at the world origin, which in that scene
is where the player falls.

Root cause: rt_spawn_entity_body read jce_scene_get_transform -- the LOCAL
TRS -- and handed its position straight to Bullet.  Two more sites had the
mirror of it, and nobody had reported those because they do not look like
physics being wrong:

  rt_push_external_transforms compared the local Transform against a cached
  body pose and teleported the body to the difference, so moving a parented
  entity from a script sent its body somewhere else.

  rt_sync_transforms wrote the body's WORLD pose into the child's LOCAL
  field, after which the renderer composes parent_world * that -- a
  simulated child drawn at DOUBLE its parent's offset.

WIRED AT EVERY SITE, NOT THE ONE THAT WAS REPORTED.  The spawn walk composes
the world pose ONCE and every spawner takes const JceTransform *, so rigid
bodies, vehicles, soft bodies, terrain, compounds, meshes, characters, 2D
bodies and tilemap colliders are all fixed by the same composition rather
than by eight edits that could each be missed.  Also: the draw-distance
deferred spawn (which does not come through that walk), fracture, the
soft-body centre write-back, the nav-agent write-back, the vehicle chassis
write-back and the character's locomotion yaw.

TWO SITES WERE ALREADY CORRECT AND WERE LEFT ALONE, which is how the list
was bounded: the vehicle WHEEL write-back already built the chassis inverse
and took each wheel into the chassis frame -- the one place in the runtime
that did this properly -- and root motion already worked entirely within one
space, adding a locally-rotated delta to a local position.

A CONSEQUENCE WORTH NAMING: a collider parented to something that MOVES now
follows it, because the parent moving changes the child's world pose and the
push pass sees exactly that.  That is what every other engine does with a
collider on a moving platform.  Before this it did not follow its parent at
all -- it sat at its local offset from the world origin.

ROOT ENTITIES ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL, which is what makes this safe: every scene
in this tree is predominantly unparented, and jce_scene_get_world_pose hands
a parentless entity its Transform's own bytes.

MEASURED: jce.py test 461/461 (the seventh world-pose case joined an
existing test binary, so the ctest count did not move).  The peer's probe
private/tools/automation/examples/probe_parent_placement.py discriminates on
trigger_contacts (penetration stopped responding once their trigger fix
landed, and their control printed a confident wrong answer until they caught
it) -- row 1 is expected to move 460 -> 952, matching row 3.

NOT MEASURED HERE, AND THE PROBE RUN IS A PREDICTION UNTIL IT IS.
trigger_contacts 460 -> 952 is what the fix implies, not a reading:
the agent bridge takes a single-instance lock and another session
held it, and a contended call exits without writing a result --
which both call sites translate into INVALID_ARGS, so running it
anyway would have produced a confident wrong answer about an
argument that was never wrong.  Also not measured: a rendered frame.  This machine is being hard-frozen to a
black screen and nothing in this work starts a graphics device.
